item.title: Applied Human Science College students demand principal's resignation
item.description:
Students of Government College of Applied Human Science, formerly known as Home Economics College, staged a sit-in for a second consecutive day on Friday, blocking the road in front of the institution in Dhaka's Azimpur and demanding the principal's resignation and an investigation into alleged police assaults on students.
They issued a 72-hour ultimatum for the fulfilment of their two-point demands, warning that they would continue their movement until the demands were met.
The protest began at 8am on Friday, with students chanting slogans including “Home Economics has risen”, “Why were police on campus? We want answers” and “Why was my sister injured? We want answers”.
Their first demand is the resignation of Principal Professor Meherunnessa. They said classes and examinations would remain suspended and the principal would not be allowed on campus until she submits a written resignation.
Their second demand is an investigation into the police operation at the college and its residential halls late on Wednesday night, including allegations of baton charges and assaults on students. They also demanded an update on the investigation within 72 hours and punishment for those responsible.
The protest began on Thursday morning, when students gathered outside the principal's office at around 10:30am and later locked her inside by putting a padlock on the office door.
Police arrived at around 11:30pm and rescued the principal after nearly 13 hours. However, more than 100 students continued their demonstration outside the college until around 2:30am.
Students alleged that police dragged female students down the stairs by their hair, beat them and charged at them with batons during the operation.
Several students were injured, according to the protesters, with three to four receiving hospital treatment. One student, who was allegedly trampled by police, is being treated at Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
The protesters also alleged that police entered the residential halls and assaulted students. They further claimed that officers took away several students' mobile phones and identity cards.
The students said the movement was not politically motivated but stemmed from their opposition to the principal's alleged arbitrary decisions and misconduct towards students. They said several of their classmates had been injured, with some still receiving treatment at hospitals.
Although the students had resume their sit-in at 8am on Friday, they said they would allow scheduled recruitment examinations to take place. However, they demanded that the principal be barred from entering the campus during the examinations.
The dispute began over a farewell program held at the college auditorium before the Puja holidays.
According to students and college administration sources, postgraduate final-year students from five departments across three residential halls were initially allowed to hold the program until 10pm. Following their request, the deadline was extended to midnight, but the event continued until 5am.
Principal Meherunnessa subsequently decided to cancel the residential hall seats of two students who coordinated the program, citing the use of the auditorium beyond the permitted time.
Students alleged that when the two approached her to apologise, she demanded Tk12,600 to cover the auditorium's air-conditioning and electricity costs for the night as a condition for reinstating their residential seats.
The principal, however, denied the allegations.
Speaking to journalists on Thursday evening, Meherunnessa said the students had been permitted to hold the programme until midnight but continued until 5am.
She said she initially cancelled the residential seats of the two students over the violation but later softened her position after they apologised. However, she decided to recover the cost of electricity wastage to maintain discipline.
“What the students are saying is the total opposite of what happened. I allowed them to hold a programme until midnight. They continued until 5am. I became a little angry and cancelled the residential seats of the two students,” she said.
Responding to the demand for her resignation, she said: “They are asking me to sign my resignation on a blank sheet of paper. Why should I resign to them?”
Lalbagh police station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Jamil Hossain said students were staging a sit-in demanding the principal's resignation.
“The situation is calm. Police are present at the scene,” he said.

item.title: Kumarkhali loses Tk 35C in potential farm output annually to waterlogging
item.description:
Around 1,250 hectares of cultivable land in Kumarkhali upazila of Kushtia remain waterlogged for seven to eight months every year, causing an estimated annual loss of Tk35 crore in potential agricultural production.
The upazila, surrounded by the Padma, Gorai, Kaliganga and Dakua rivers, has around 18,240 hectares of cultivable land. Farmers can grow crops on the waterlogged land only once a year during the Boro season, producing around 6,225 tonnes of paddy.
If the waterlogging problem is resolved, the land could produce an additional 10,000 tonnes of paddy and other crops during the Aman and Aus seasons, with an estimated market value of Tk35 crore.
Agricultural officials and local farmers say food production could increase further if modern farming methods and high-yielding crop varieties were introduced.
Farmers said although the upazila had numerous irrigation canals under the Ganges-Kobadak (G-K) Irrigation Project, managed by the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB), there was no proper drainage system.
Many canals have remained neglected for years, while some have been filled in to build houses and others blocked by dams for fish farming.
As a result, land that could produce crops three times a year remains submerged for seven to eight months, severely affecting agriculture.
Farmers said the problem continued for nearly a decade without any effective initiative to resolve it. This has reduced agricultural production and caused recurring financial losses for farmers.
A visit to the wetlands of Bahalbaria, Chandpur, Banshara, Bakhai, Karatkandi and Jagonnathpur found large areas under water. Stagnant water was covered with water hyacinths, water spinach (kolmi) and water lilies. Some locals were seen fishing from small boats, while others cleared weeds to prepare their land for cultivation this season.
Many farmers have turned to fish farming by digging ponds after suffering repeated losses from crop cultivation. Ponds have also been dug along canals near the wetlands, while houses and roads have been built in the areas.
Poor maintenance has also left many canals unable to drain water properly.
Rabiul Islam, a farmer from Bahalbaria Beel in Nandolalpur union, said he owned 16 bighas of land.
"Ten to 12 years ago, water used to flow through a canal into the Gorai River, allowing us to grow rice three times a year. Now, as water cannot drain out, we can barely grow even one crop," he said.
Majed Ali, another farmer from the same area, said it was frustrating that water remained stagnant despite the presence of four nearby rivers.
"The stagnant water is covered with water hyacinths and weeds. Clearing them requires six labourers per bigha. Farming has become costly, but yields and profits remain low," he said.
Abdus Samad, a farmer from the Gobindapur Beel area, said some areas had no canals, while existing ones were clogged with weeds and silt.
As a result, water remains trapped on the land, allowing farmers to cultivate crops only once a year.
He said planned excavation of canals could help farmers grow crops three times a year.
Azahar Biswas, a farmer aged over 60, owns three bighas of land in Karatkandi Beel under Sadki union.
He said farmers were struggling because of the lack of proper drainage channels.
A single harvest produces around 12 to 14 maunds of rice per bigha, but the income is almost entirely spent on clearing weeds, Azahar said.
"If we could cultivate the land two or three times a year, farming would become profitable," he added.
According to the local Department of Agricultural Extension office, around 1,250 hectares of the upazila's 18,240 hectares of cultivable land are currently waterlogged.
Of the affected land, 290 hectares are in Nandolalpur union, 250 in Sadki, 240 in Jagannathpur, 205 in Shelaidaha, 75 in Jadu Boyra, 120 in Kaya and 70 hectares in Chapra union.
The waterlogging is affecting agricultural production and making it difficult to meet the upazila's overall food production targets.
In 2024, the area of waterlogged land was only 510 hectares, according to the office.
Upazila Agriculture Officer Md Monir Hossain said the extent of waterlogging had increased over the years with rising rainfall.
He said around 1,250 hectares of land were currently affected, producing only 6,225 tonnes of paddy during the Boro season.
If the land could also be cultivated during the Aman and Aus seasons, farmers could have produced an additional 10,000 tonnes of crops, worth around Tk35 crore, the official said.
He added that the issue had been brought to the attention of the local administration and higher authorities.
Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Md Raisul Islam said proposals for excavating two canals in Kumarkhali had been submitted under the government's ongoing canal excavation project.
Once the excavation work begins, the waterlogging problem will be partly reduced, he said.
Further initiatives would be taken after discussions with local public representatives, the DAE, farmers, the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) and the BWDB, the UNO said.

item.title: Putin slams 'political' moves to keep Russia out of sport events
item.description:
Vladimir Putin on Thursday slammed countries who oppose reinstating Russia into international sports as several European teams said they will refuse to play them at next year's world ice hockey championships over the Ukraine war.
Denmark, Norway, Sweden and the Czech Republic on Tuesday all followed Finland in saying they would not play Russia at the 2027 world championships to be held in Germany.
Russia has been banned from International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) events since Putin launched the 2022 war in Ukraine, but the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled in favour of admitting them to the world championships.
Russia has been mostly banned from international sport since 2022 but some restrictions have eased in recent months -- a trend slammed by Ukraine.
Putin praised the International Olympic Committee and CAS for "taking decisions to uphold the Olympic Charter and its principles", as restrictions have been eased.
"Unfortunately, however, not all countries are prepared to honour the commitments they once undertook, and restrictions on Russian sport -- which are political rather than legal -- continue," Putin told a televised government meeting.
Amid the ice hockey stand-off, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday Russia would not be allowed to compete at next month's World Junior Hockey Championships.
The world championships are due to be held in Germany next May, but the draw and scheduling for the tournament have already taken place, without Russia.
Putin has regularly appeared playing ice hockey during his long presidency.
Russia's war against Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands, forced millions to displace and is Europe's worst conflict since World War II.

item.title: Gold price drops by Tk2,739 per bhori
item.description:
Gold prices in Bangladesh fell by Tk2,739 per bhori on Friday, a day after a major increase, according to the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus).
The new prices came into effect at 10am on Friday.
Under the revised rates, 22-carat gold is priced at Tk2,26,937 per bhori (11.664 grams), down from Tk2,29,676 on Thursday.
The price of 22-carat gold has been set at Tk19,455 per gram.
The new rates were announced following a meeting of the Bajus Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring on Friday morning.
The association said the prices were adjusted in response to a decline in the price of pure gold in the local market.
According to the revised rates, 21-carat gold is priced at Tk18,580 per gram, 18-carat gold at Tk15,955, and traditional-method gold at Tk13,035.
Bajus has also reduced silver prices.
Under the new rates, 22-carat silver is priced at Tk300 per gram, 21-carat silver at Tk290, 18-carat silver at Tk250, and traditional-method silver at Tk190.
Bajus said making charges will vary depending on the design of the jewellery.
VAT is included in the prescribed selling prices, so jewellers cannot charge it separately from customers.
For exchanges of old gold jewellery, a 12% deduction will apply to the prescribed price after excluding making charges and stone prices.
For purchases of old gold, an 18% deduction will apply.
VAT cannot be deducted separately in either case.
The revised prices will remain in effect at all jewellery shops across the country until further notice, Bajus said.
Gold prices in the domestic market have been adjusted 133 times this year, with 64 increases, 68 reductions and one VAT adjustment.
In 2025, Bajus adjusted gold prices 93 times, raising them 64 times and lowering them 29 times.
The number of price adjustments has increased significantly compared with last year, as fluctuations in pure gold prices in international and local markets have prompted frequent changes in domestic rates.

item.title: Dhaka air quality ‘very unhealthy’ Friday morning
item.description:
Dhaka's air quality turned ‘very unhealthy’ on Friday morning, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 203 at 8:40am.
With this score, the capital ranked fourth among the world's most polluted cities, according to the AQI scale.
A ‘very unhealthy’ air quality level means everyone, regardless of their health condition, may experience more serious health effects or discomfort from air pollution. Even short-term exposure can affect anyone.
Pakistan's Lahore topped the list with an AQI score of 456, followed by India's Delhi with 251 and Kolkata with 221.
On Thursday, Dhaka ranked fifth among the world's most polluted cities, recording an AQI score of 174 at 10:25am.
According to the AQI scale, readings of 101-150 are considered unhealthy for sensitive groups, while scores of 151-200 indicate unhealthy air quality. Readings of 201-300 are classified as very unhealthy, while scores above 301 are considered hazardous and pose serious health risks.
The AQI measures daily air quality and indicates pollution levels and their potential effects on public health.
In Bangladesh, air quality is assessed based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulphur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths worldwide each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

PM Tarique’s Khulna visit brings big promises for industry, jobs
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday unveiled plans to develop an industrial corridor stretching from Mongla in the southwest to Panchagarh in the north, seeking to revive struggling industrial regions, attract investment and create employment through expanded port facilities, energy infrastructure and improved connectivity.
During a daylong visit to Bagerhat and Khulna, he laid the foundation stone of a Tk4,068 crore project to expand and modernise Mongla Port, witnessed the signing of an investment cooperation agreement with a Chinese state-owned company and pledged to reopen closed factories while encouraging the establishment of new industries.
The prime minister also assured workers that a new minimum wage would be fixed within one or two months, as garment workers continued demonstrations across several industrial areas demanding higher pay.
Addressing a roadside meeting at Katakhali intersection on the Khulna-Mongla highway, Tarique said his government wanted to restore Khulna’s former industrial prominence and extend industrial development across Bagerhat, Kushtia, Chuadanga and other districts towards Panchagarh.
He said the government would gradually develop the necessary electricity, gas and transport infrastructure to attract factories and generate employment along the proposed corridor.
Earlier, the prime minister laid the foundation stone of the Tk4,068 crore Mongla Port expansion and modernisation project, which includes two container jetties and supporting infrastructure to increase cargo-handling capacity and improve services.
Speaking at the ceremony, he described Mongla as a potential economic hub for the country’s southwestern and northwestern regions.
He said modernising the port would help expand trade and industrial activities in Khulna, Bagerhat, Satkhira and Jashore while strengthening economic connectivity with northern districts.
The government also plans to improve road links between Panchagarh and Mongla, expand port supply chains and facilitate cargo transportation.
According to the prime minister’s deputy press secretary, the project would enable direct container train services between Kamalapur Inland Container Depot in Dhaka and Mongla Port once the necessary facilities are operational.
Tarique also identified the development and operation of Khan Jahan Ali Airport as a government priority.
He stressed that the project’s success would depend not merely on completing infrastructure but also on reducing cargo-handling costs, improving efficiency and attracting investment.
At Mongla Port, the prime minister witnessed the signing of a memorandum of understanding between Invest Bangladesh and China Railway Construction Corporation (CRCC) on economic and infrastructure cooperation.
Invest Bangladesh Member (Industrial Zones) Saleh Ahmed and China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation Chairman Li Chongyang signed the agreement.
The cooperation framework covers potential investment in energy, industrial and environmentally sustainable infrastructure, transport, logistics and human resource development.
Tarique later held discussions with a Chinese delegation led by CRCC Chairman Dai Hegen.
He urged Chinese investors to establish industries around Mongla and emphasised the importance of reliable electricity and gas supplies for industrial expansion.
The prime minister also thanked the Chinese delegation for supporting opportunities for Bangladeshi workers to secure employment with Chinese companies in the Middle East.
The prime minister said the government wanted to reopen closed mills and factories, including state-owned establishments, and encourage domestic and foreign investment to create employment.
Later, he visited the shrine of Hazrat Khan Jahan Ali in Bagerhat, where he offered prayers.
In Khulna, he inaugurated the second season of Notun Kuri Sports at the district stadium, highlighting the importance of sports, arts and cultural activities alongside academic education.
He said the government was committed to fulfilling its election promises and developing the next generation through education and extracurricular activities.
Around 1.6 million children are participating in the nationwide sporting initiative, according to the program details provided.
The prime minister also reiterated that his government would continue efforts to strengthen the economy despite global challenges.

Health minister: Five Dhaka hospitals to launch PPP-based healthcare services
item.description:
Health and Family Welfare Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain on Thursday said the government plans to launch improved healthcare services under a public-private partnership (PPP) model, initially at five hospitals in Dhaka on a trial basis.
“Plans are underway to expand the healthcare program to other cities,” he said while addressing an event held at Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Medical College Hospital (SZMCH) in Bogra.
The health minister said discussions with the five hospitals had been finalised, but another meeting would be held next week to determine the fees private partners would charge. The pilot program would begin once financial arrangements were settled, he added.
"We will initially introduce the program on a trial basis at five hospitals in Dhaka before expanding it to other cities. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is interested in the initiative, and we are working to implement it," he said.
Describing SZMCH as a major healthcare centre for northern Bangladesh, the minister said the government was considering expanding access to advanced treatment for complex diseases, including cancer and liver conditions.
Hospital authorities had been asked to submit written lists of their problems, which would be addressed gradually, he added.
On the shortage of doctors and the absence of a separate paediatric ICU at SZMCH, the minister said the government planned to establish around 20 new ICUs across the country, including one in Bogra. He said 17 of the 500 newly appointed doctors had been posted to different healthcare facilities in Bogra, with more appointments planned.
Recruitment of another 5,000 doctors is also underway. Applications have closed, and the Public Service Commission is conducting the interview process, he added.
Blaming corruption and mismanagement over the past 17 years for the deterioration of the healthcare sector, he said the current government was working to restore discipline and improve services.

item.title: QS Asia Rankings: DU retains top position from Bangladesh, 16th in South Asia
item.description:
Dhaka University has retained its position as the top university in Bangladesh in the QS World University Rankings: Asia 2027, securing 136th place among Asian universities and 16th among those in South Asia.
The UK-based international higher education and research organization Quacquarelli Symonds (QS) published the rankings on November 3. DU also held the top position among Bangladeshi universities in last year's rankings.
According to a press release issued by DU, a total of 1,722 universities from 26 countries across Asia have been included in this year's rankings. The University of Hong Kong secured the first position, followed by Peking University of China.
The QS Asia University Rankings assess universities based on several indicators, including academic reputation, faculty-student ratio, research quality and impact, the proportion of staff holding PhD degrees, international research collaboration, and the number of international faculty members and students.
DU Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr ABM Obaidul Islam expressed his satisfaction over the university's position in the international rankings. "This position in the international rankings is a matter of joy and pride for us. Consistently retaining the top position among Bangladeshi universities is recognition of collective efforts of our teachers, students, researchers and all concerned," he said.
However, he said the university's goal was not merely to maintain its ranking but to further strengthen its position internationally through improvement in the quality of education and research.
The vice-chancellor said enriching the academic and research environment, expanding research facilities, strengthening international collaborations and creating opportunities for students to develop globally competitive skills were among the university's key priorities.

item.title: World Bank: Bangladesh’s external debt rises to $113.4bn
item.description:
Bangladesh’s total external debt climbed 8.6 percent to reach $113.4 billion in 2025, according to the World Bank’s International Debt Report 2026, even as the country maintained manageable debt-to-GNI and debt-service ratios amid a broader global financing squeeze.
The new report reveals that Bangladesh’s long-term public and publicly guaranteed (PPG) external debt stands at $89.5 billion. Multilateral creditors hold the majority share of these public obligations at $51.1 billion—primarily driven by the World Bank’s International Development Association ($22.6 billion) and the Asian Development Bank ($17.5 billion).
Bilateral debt accounts for $32.6 billion, anchored by major partners like Japan ($12.7 billion) and the Russian Federation ($9.0 billion).
Private nonguaranteed debt of $9.9 billion and $14.1 billion in short-term liabilities make up the remainder of the nation's external profile.
Despite the rising debt stock, Bangladesh’s macro-fiscal indicators reflect resilience compared to regional peers.
The country's external debt-to-GNI ratio stood at a moderate 24 percent, while the debt service-to-exports ratio eased by 3.1% to 16%.
Official commitments extended to Bangladesh also retained favorable terms, featuring an average maturity of 25 years, a 6-year grace period, and an average interest rate of 3%.
Zooming out to the regional picture, total external debt across South Asia reached $955 billion in 2025.
While regional debt-to-GNI ratios remain contained at an average of 21 percent, South Asian economies face an increasingly unforgiving global capital environment.
On a global scale, total external debt across all low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) surged 5.5% to a record $9.4 trillion in 2025, marking the sharpest increase in four years as private lenders and bond markets forcefully reopened.
However, this renewed market access has come at an exorbitant price, particularly for the poorest economies. Private creditors charged IDA-eligible countries an average interest rate of 8.2% on new commitments in 2025—the highest level seen since the late 1980s.
Total debt service payments for LMICs rose for the fifth consecutive year to $1.4 trillion, consuming over 40% of government revenues in vulnerable nations and crowding out vital spending on health, education, and infrastructure.
Commenting on the global outlook, World Bank Chief Statistician Haishan Fu warned that access to finance is not enough.
“We must know the debt, understand its terms, and ensure that the financing developing economies receive strengthens rather than constrains their ability to grow, withstand shocks, and improve the lives of their people."
Adding to this, World Bank analysts noted a troubling paradox where developing nations are borrowing more and paying steeper prices, ultimately leaving fewer resources available for long-term sustainable development.

item.title: July atrocities: ICT accepts charges against Amu, 6 others
item.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) on Thursday took cognisance of charges against seven individuals linked to the Awami League, including former minister Amir Hossain Amu, in a case filed over crimes against humanity committed during the July 2024 uprising.
The three-member bench of the ICT-2, led by Justice Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, also ordered that six of the accused, who were in jail, be produced before it on November 22 in connection with the case.
It issued a warrant for the arrest of Awami League Organising Secretary Mirza Azam, who had been absconding.
The other accused in the cases were former Shipping Minister Shajahan Khan, former Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister Lt Col (retd) Faruk Khan, former Agricultural Minister Abdur Razzaque, former minister Dr Dipu Moni and former Energy Adviser to the ousted Prime Minister Tawfiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury.
Briefing reporters, Prosecutor Gazi Tamim said former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina had taken state-level and political decisions to suppress the July mass uprising.
Plans had been devised to use lethal weapons against protesters, impose a curfew, shut down the internet and control the media, he said.
Records of conversations, documents, supporting evidence and witness statements had been submitted to the tribunal in support of these allegations, Tamim added.
He said various pieces of evidence, including a United Nations report, had been submitted to support allegations that state forces and intelligence agencies had been used to carry out killings to suppress the movement.
The prosecutor also claimed that the UN report had contained an alleged instruction by Sheikh Hasina to "kill them and hide the bodies."
Regarding the individual roles of the accused, he said the prosecution had presented information that Tk 5 crore in cash had been found in sacks at the residence of Amu after August 5, 2024.
Faruk Khan attended a security committee meeting on August 4, where a decision had allegedly been taken to shoot and kill protesters at the entry points to Dhaka on August 5, according to the prosecution.
Dipu Moni, meanwhile, had participated in a meeting on imposing the curfew and had been involved in planning to suppress the movement, Tamim alleged.
He also claimed that Shajahan Khan, through conversations with Sheikh Hasina, had issued instructions to deploy police, Awami League leaders and activists, and workers against the protesters.
The case also includes allegations of arson at various establishments during the movement.
The prosecutor said recordings of conversations involving Sheikh Hasina, Obaidul Quader and Hasan Mahmud had been submitted to the tribunal in this regard.
Forensic reports verifying the authenticity of the recordings, along with video reports verified by experts from the BBC, Al Jazeera and the United Nations, had also been submitted, he added.
Tamim said the seven accused had been charged with incitement, assistance, conspiracy and contribution to the commission of crimes. They also face allegations of superior command responsibility.
The prosecution alleged that the accused, from their respective positions, played roles in making and implementing political decisions to suppress the movement.
The prosecutor further said the investigation into the abduction and torture of six coordinators of the July uprising while in the custody of the Detective Branch (DB) was nearing completion.
Earlier, on November 2, the prosecution submitted formal charges against the seven leaders.

item.title: Tahsif Sauri death: Dip gets fresh 3-day remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court has granted a third spell of remand, this time for three days, for Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip in a murder case filed over the death of former air force officer KM Tahsif Sauri.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Monirul Islam passed the order on Thursday following a petition by the investigation officer. State lawyer Muhammad Shamsuddoha Sumon confirmed the development.
Inspector Firoz Uddin of the Tongi River Police Outpost, the investigation officer, had sought seven days’ remand, citing five reasons. These included establishing the motive behind the alleged killing, recovering evidence, identifying the suspected mastermind and accomplices, checking Dip’s statements against eyewitness accounts and CCTV footage, and understanding how the incident took place.
Dhaka Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruqui argued in favour of the remand, while Dip’s lawyer, Monirul Islam, sought his release on bail and opposed further questioning. After hearing both sides, the court granted three days’ remand.
Tahsif’s body was recovered by river police from the Rajabari Ghat area of the Turag River on the afternoon of October 28. He had left home on his motorcycle on the evening of October 27 after Dip called him downstairs.
Dip said on October 29 that he had dinner with Tahsif at a restaurant before parting ways in the Uttara House Building area. He was handed over to river police on the night of October 30, amid discussions over what action would be taken against him after no case had been filed within three days of the body’s recovery.
After Tahsif’s father filed the case that night, police showed Dip arrested. He was initially remanded for four days, followed by a second three-day remand on Tuesday.
Police recovered Tahsif’s motorcycle from Tongi’s Mazar slum area on the morning of October 30, based on information provided by Dip. He also admitted to visiting the area with Tahsif late at night. Investigators from the Police Bureau of Investigation later visited the area with him.
Dip is described in the case as a close acquaintance of Tahsif. The former air force officer had drawn attention for allegedly recording a video of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina leaving the country.
Meanwhile, Tahsif’s girlfriend, Jerika Tasnim Disha, was placed on a second three-day remand on Wednesday after an initial four-day spell. She was reportedly seen with Tahsif at a bar in Uttara on the night of the incident.

item.title: Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury sent to jail in murder case; no bail sought
item.description:
A Dhaka court has ordered former information adviser to ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and DBC News Chairman Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury to be sent to jail in a case filed over the killing of madrasa student Md Arif in Jatrabari during the July uprising.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Sarah Farzana Haque passed the order on Thursday following a petition filed by the investigation officer, said public prosecutor Muhammad Shamsuddoha Chowdhury.
Sub-Inspector Mohammad Amir Hossain of Jatrabari police station and also the investigation officer of the case sought an order to keep Iqbal Sobhan in jail.
Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury's lawyer Chowdhury Mohammad Galib Ragib did not seek bail but requested proper medical treatment and division facilities for his client.
He told the court that Iqbal Sobhan is a senior journalist and CEO of DBC News who suffers from diabetes, high blood pressure and neurological complications. He requested the court to ensure that his client receives division facilities and proper medical care in jail.
During the hearing, Dhaka Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruq Faruqi outlined the allegations against Iqbal Sobhan.
He alleged that Iqbal Sobhan secured ownership of DBC News by pleasing Sheikh Hasina and was subsequently appointed her information adviser. In that capacity, he allegedly facilitated the issuance of television licences and exercised control over the media.
The prosecutor further alleged that the former adviser took steps to prevent protesters' statements from being broadcast during the July uprising. He also accused him of forming an organisation with journalist Mozammel Haque Babu and bringing television channels under government control.
Faruqui claimed that Iqbal Sobhan amassed considerable wealth in the Gulshan and Banani areas through these activities before going into hiding following the fall of the Hasina government. Law enforcement agencies arrested him on Wednesday, he added.
The defence lawyer Chowdhury Mohammad Galib Ragib said Iqbal Sobhan had served as the former prime minister's information adviser, a position equivalent in rank to a state minister, and requested that his status be considered under the jail code.
In response, the public prosecutor said no official declaration had been made recognising Iqbal Sobhan's position as equivalent to that of a state minister.
After hearing both sides, the court ordered his detention in jail, saying he would be granted any applicable privileges after the relevant matters had been examined.
Police arrested Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury from the DBC News office in the capital’s Mohakhali area on Wednesday afternoon. They also took the television channel’s chief crime reporter, Rajib Ghosh, into custody.
Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury is also the editor and publisher of The Daily Observer.
Following the arrest, DMP Deputy Commissioner (Public Relations) Aktar Hossain said an “untoward situation” had arisen at DBC over the broadcast of a news report. “Journalists Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury and Rajib Ghosh were taken into DB custody from there,” he said. However, he did not elaborate on the circumstances that led to the incident. Later that night, police showed Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury arrested in the murder case. Meanwhile, DMP Detective Branch chief Shafiqul Islam said a decision had been made to release DBC News special correspondent Rajib Ghosh after obtaining a bond from him. According to the case statement, Arif, a first-year Alim student at Lord Hardinge Senior Fazil Madrasa, was shot in the eye during an exchange of gunfire between police and Awami League leaders and activists near Boubazar in Jatrabari’s Kutubkhali area on the afternoon of July 19, 2024, during the July uprising. He was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where the on-duty doctors declared him dead. Arif’s father, Md Yusuf filed a murder case with Jatrabari Police Station on August 25, 2024, naming Sheikh Hasina and 232 others. Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury is listed as the 53rd accused in the case.

PM inaugurates 2nd season of nationwide Notun Kuri Sports competition
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday inaugurated the second season of the nationwide “Notun Kuri Sports-2026-27” competition, aimed at discovering young sporting talent and encouraging children and adolescents to participate in sports.
The inaugural ceremony was held at Khulna District Stadium, with the prime minister also virtually launching the program simultaneously in 503 upazilas across the country.
Tarique Rahman entered the stadium around 3:45pm when State Minister for Youth and Sports Md Aminul Haque and acting Secretary Mahfuzul Alam Khan welcomed him.
As the prime minister arrived, students and young athletes in the galleries greeted him by waving at him. He reciprocated their greetings by walking across the field towards the galleries and waving back at the young spectators.
He then inaugurated the competition by releasing balloons and hoisting the national flag.
The prime minister also interacted with some young athletes participating in the competition's 10 disciplines.
Students from China’s Yunnan Minzu University perform a traditional dragon dance during the inauguration ceremony of Notun Kuri Sports (Season 2) at Khulna District Stadium on Thursday, November 5, 2026. Photo: PMO
Traditional Chinese dragon and lion dances performed by a group of students from China added a cultural touch to the opening ceremony of Notun Kuri Sports (Season 2) in Khulna.
The students from Yunnan Minzu University in Kunming, Yunnan Province, China, performed the dances in the presence of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at Khulna District Stadium. The performance was part of sports and cultural diplomacy between Bangladesh and China.
A total of 1,623,218 participants have registered online for the second season of the competition, according to information presented at the event.
The competition is being organized under the theme, “Make sports a profession, give families confidence”, with the aim of identifying sporting talent among children and adolescents across the country and creating opportunities for their development from the grassroots level.
The Department of Sports is implementing the initiative under the supervision of the Ministry of Youth and Sports, in line with a commitment in the BNP's election manifesto.
Inspired by the popular “Notun Kuri” talent-hunting program of the 1980s, the initiative seeks to revive the spirit of that program through the discovery of young talent in sports.
In the second season, volleyball and table tennis have been added to the previous eight disciplines, taking the total to 10. Children aged between 10 and 14 are eligible to participate.
The first season of “Notun Kuri Sports” was inaugurated in Sylhet on May 2 last to help children and adolescents develop their latent talents, foster interest in sports, and encourage greater participation in sporting activities.

Humaiun Kobir: Bangladesh wants Hasina extradited from India
item.description:
Referring to the existing extradition treaty with India, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Thursday said they want former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who now faces the death penalty, to be handed over to Bangladesh.
“We want Hasina to be handed over. She will be handed over. She is a terrorist. She is a fled criminal. There is an active extradition treaty between Bangladesh and India,” he told reporters, noting that there is no need to issue her a passport.
Kobir made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport after seeing off Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee.
Hasina, ousted in a mass uprising in 2024, has told The Associated Press that she remains committed to returning to Bangladesh from exile in India next month, despite being sentenced to death over her government's deadly crackdown on protesters.
“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” she told AP in response to questions by email. “So, I will return to Bangladesh. That decision has not changed.”
Hasina fled to India after student-led protests forced her from power and has remained there ever since.
In 2025, a Bangladeshi special tribunal sentenced her to death for crimes against humanity, ruling that she was responsible for ordering the crackdown, which left hundreds of people dead and thousands of others injured.
Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina’s extradition, but India has declined to hand her over. She first announced in August her intention to return in December.
On October 3, Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi stressed that former Prime Minister Hasina was not brought to India by the Indian Air Force or the Indian Army. He said the legal process concerning Bangladesh’s request for her extradition was ongoing and that no timeframe could be given as the courts were involved.
“To give you a straight answer, again and again, the government of India, through the Spokesperson at the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), has replied to this that there is a process, and the process involves legality, and it is well structured. So, as far as that is concerned, the process is on,” Trivedi said.
He said the courts were involved in the matter and, therefore, “nobody can give you a timeframe.”
Trivedi said Hasina was still the Prime Minister of Bangladesh when she arrived in India, and New Delhi had to respond to the situation as a neighboring country.
“At that point in time, Hasina was still the prime minister of Bangladesh. We had hardly any choice on that. It was our duty as a neighbor to accept the reality of life, because situations are such where at times you are not prepared for it,” the Indian envoy said.
Trivedi also referred to the circumstances under which Hasina came to India after leaving Bangladesh in August 2024, saying the Indian authorities were not prepared for the situation.
“Going back to history, Hasina Ji was not brought to India by the Indian Air Force or Indian Army,” he said, referring to the circumstances surrounding her departure from Bangladesh.
He said the situation unfolded because of “tragic circumstances” in Bangladesh at the time, adding that such circumstances should never be repeated anywhere in the world, where innocent people get killed, regardless of which part of the world it is.
He questioned what India's alternative could have been under those circumstances. “What was our choice? If you would have said that no, we are not going to accept, we don’t give landing permission. Things would have been I don’t know what,” Trivedi said.
Bangladesh has repeatedly requested India to extradite Hasina, who has been staying in India since her departure from Bangladesh in August 2024.
The issue was also raised by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman during his meeting with Trivedi in Dhaka in August.
India’s Ministry of External Affairs subsequently said that Bangladesh’s request was being examined in line with established procedures.

PM envisions modernized Mongla Port as economic hub for southwest, northwest regions
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday said the modernization and expansion of Mongla Port will turn it into a promising economic hub for the country’s south-western and north-western regions, with the government planning to expand road connectivity, port supply chains and cargo transport facilities from Pantagraph to the Bay of Bengal.
“If Mongla Port is modernized and its facilities are expanded...It will become a promising economic hub for the country’s south-west and north-west,” he said.
The prime minister said this while addressing the foundation stone laying ceremony of the Tk 4,068 crore “Mongla Port Facilities Expansion and Modernization Project” in Mongla on Thursday morning.
He said the capacity building and modernization of the port will strengthen trade links with different parts of the country and help expand economic activities.
There is huge scope to expand economic activities in the south-western region, including Khulna, Bagerhat, Satkhira and Jessore, centered on the port, he said.
The prime minister said, “Development of Khan Jahan Ali Airport is also one of our priorities. In the present global order, it is extremely important to keep energy and food security effective above all.”
“I firmly believe Mongla Port, as a complementary port for importing fuel, fertilizer, foodgrains and industrial raw materials and exporting domestic products, can further enrich national economic security,” he added.
Tarique Rahman said the initiative will help strengthen the country’s industry, trade and economic security, and add sustainable socio-economic value, especially in youth employment, entrepreneurs’ confidence in investment and balanced regional development.
He laid the foundation stone of the project, which includes two container jetties and related infrastructure, at 11:15 am.
Once the project is implemented, container trains from Dhaka’s Kamalapur Inland Container Depot (ICD) will be able to run directly to Mongla Port, turning it into a major import-export hub of the country, he said.
Under the modernization project, necessary infrastructure, including a modern container terminal, yard and cargo handling facilities, is being built, he said.
“If the work is completed on time, the economic condition of this region will change, Inshallah, and a new door of economic possibilities will open not only for this region but for the whole country,” he added.
Noting that the project’s success does not end with the completion of construction, the Prime Minister said, “The real success of any project depends on how much port service quality improves, how much time and cost of cargo handling fall, how much investment and employment grow, and how much the environment is protected.”
“We must follow international environmental and safety standards, build climate-resilient infrastructure and increase the use of renewable energy,” he said.
In this connection, he stressed on eco-friendly service management, pollution control and safe waste management of ships.
He also said fire safety, trained manpower and emergency response capacity are needed to handle hazardous operations.
Highlighting the country’s economic target, the prime minister said his government has set the goal of turning Bangladesh into a $1 trillion economy by 2030.
“To achieve this goal, top priority is being given to investment, industrialization, export diversification, energy and food security, and skilled human resource development,” he said.
The prime minister urged international stakeholders, development partners and, in particular, expatriate Bangladeshis to come forward with investment to help make the country self-reliant.
In this context, he said the government is committed to ensuring a favorable investment climate, easy service procedures, reliable infrastructure and policy continuity.
“The modernization of Mongla Port is only one step in the plan to transform Bangladesh into a $1 trillion economy,” he added.
“So, it is extremely necessary to ensure the port’s navigability, the reliability of the navigation channel, the safe movement of ships and competitive port services,” he said.
The prime minister also said Mongla Port must now be made attractive to international shipping companies and developed into a first calling port on suitable commercial and operational terms.
He said the government has taken steps to supply gas as quickly as possible to existing industries and to those who may set up new ones in the area. “Work has already been started to this end,” he said.
Recalling the region’s industrial past, he said Khulna and the surrounding areas once had many mills and factories. “We want to bring back that lost heritage,” he said
Minister for Road Transport and Bridges, Railways and Shipping Shaikh Rabiul Alam, State Minister for Shipping and Bridges Md Razib Ahsan, State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shaikh Faridul Islam, Mongla Port Authority Chairman Rear Admiral Arif Ahmed Mostafa and CRCC Chairman Dai Hegen spoke on the occasion.
State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit, Invest Bangladesh Chairman Ashik Chowdhury and other senior officials were present.

item.title: PM: People will give conspirators befitting reply, as in 2024
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday said the people will unitedly give a befitting reply, as they did in 2024, to those conspiring to destroy the country’s industries.
In this context, he assured workers that a new minimum wage will be fixed for them within a month or two.
“We will stand against the conspirators with all our strength, together with the people of the country, the working people and our brothers and sisters among the workers. Just as the people of Bangladesh gave them a befitting reply in 2024, they will be given a befitting reply in the same way in the days ahead.,” he said.
The prime minister was addressing a roadside meeting at Katakhali intersection on the Khulna-Mongla highway at 12:30 pm, on his way to visit the mazar of Hazrat Khan Jahan Ali (R) in Bagerhat.
Tarique Rahman said the people’s government has been established and has taken up work and plans to change the fate of the general masses, but the conspirators want to derail them.
“The people and the country’s workers must stand up against these conspiracies so that the conspirators get no opportunity in any way. Now is the time to build our country and change the fate of our people,” he said.
Warning the conspirators, the premier said, “We will give a befitting reply to these conspirators with all our strength, Inshallah. Our goal is one: ‘Let us work, build the country, Bangladesh first’ (Korbo Kaj, Gorbo Desh; Sobar Agee Bangladesh).”
Tarique Rahman said those who had failed to improve people's living conditions over the past 15-16 years, deprived them of their voting rights and siphoned off the country's wealth abroad were forced to flee following the mass uprising on August 5, 2024. “They (ousted forces) are now pulling strings from across the border and trying to create disorder and chaos in the country. Not only that, they are about to destroy the country’s mills and factories,” he said.
Tarique Rahman said the mills and factories are the wealth of the people and of the country’s workers. “If they are destroyed, the working people will be the first to suffer. My brothers and sisters among the workers will suffer the most, and their children’s future will be ruined,” he said.
On the wage board, the prime minister said the elected government is working day and night to solve the country’s problems and expand industry and trade so that people can live well. “We know the workers have made some demands about their wages. You have seen that we have already formed a wage board to consider those demands,” he said.
The wage board has already started work and will fix a new minimum wage within a month or two, he said, so that workers can live even better.
The prime minister said BNP had promised, if it formed the government, to create jobs, reopen closed public and private mills and factories, and encourage local and foreign investors to set up new industries.
“We will try to reopen the mills and factories that have been shut down across the country at different times, especially the public ones. Alongside that, we will encourage investors at home and abroad to set up new mills and factories, because we want to create employment for the country’s young people,” he said.
Recalling that Khulna was once one of the country’s leading industrial regions, he said many of its factories have closed over time for various reasons.
The government wants to set up thousands of factories, from the south-west, including Khulna, Bagerhat, Kushtia and Chuadanga, to Panchagarh in the north, added the premier.
Earlier in the morning, the prime minister attended the signing ceremony of an MoU on economic and infrastructure cooperation between Invest Bangladesh and China Railway Construction Corporation (CRCC), a Chinese state-owned company, in Mongla, and later laid the foundation stone of the Mongla Port expansion and modernization project.
After the roadside meeting, he visited the mazar of Hazrat Khan Jahan Ali (R) in Bagerhat and also attend the opening ceremony of Notun Kuri Sports (Season-2) at the Khulna District Stadium in the afternoon.

item.title: 20 crude bombs, 41 torch-sticks seized in Mirpur
item.description:
Police have recovered 20 crude bombs, 41 torch-sticks and around two litres of kerosene during an operation near the Ansar Camp in Paikpara, Mirpur.
The items were seized on Thursday following a tip-off, according to Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP).
Hasan Mohammad Naser Bikabdar, deputy commissioner of the DMP's Mirpur division, confirmed the recovery.
He said police received information overnight that suspected crude bombs and torch-sticks had been left on the road in front of the Ansar Camp.
A team led by Mirpur Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Hafizur Rahman recovered 20 crude bombs, including 15 inside three paper bags and five lying on the road.
Police also seized 41 torch-sticks, around two litres of kerosene in two bottles inside a shopping bag, and several sheets of soft polystyrene, commonly known as thermocol.
The 20 crude bombs were later detonated in two separate operations inside a pit dug at an open area of a construction site belonging to the Ministry of Housing and Public Works, near Hakkani Goli in Kalyanpur, the deputy commissioner said.
Legal proceedings are underway, he added.
Bikabdar also said the recovery took place around the time of the arrest of Al Mahmud Tarek, a former central organising secretary of the banned Chhatra League and former general secretary of its Dhaka College unit.
He said police suspected the seized materials might have been intended for a major act of sabotage.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,272 as three die in 24 hours
item.description:
Three more children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours ending at 8:00am on Thursday, bringing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,272 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) classified the latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths.
With this, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,167, while confirmed deaths have remained the same at 105.
A total of 1,327 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, taking the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 235,475.
Meanwhile, 69 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, pushing laboratory-confirmed infections to 24,219.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 209,854 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 201,153 have recovered, according to the DGHS.

item.title: 33 platoons of BGB deployed in Dhaka, industrial areas
item.description:
A total of 33 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed in different industrial areas of Dhaka and its surrounding districts to ensure the security of garment factories and maintain law and order.
Of the deployed personnel, three platoons are stationed in Mirpur, 11 in Savar and Ashulia, 12 in Gazipur and seven in Narayanganj.
The activities are being monitored and coordinated round the clock by a monitoring cell at the BGB headquarters, says BGB headquarters public relation officer Shariful Islam on Thursday morning.
Armoured Personnel Carriers (APCs) and Riot Control Vehicles (RCVs) have also been deployed to strengthen security and tackle any untoward situation.
To make security operations more effective, live monitoring is being conducted through drones.
Body-worn cameras and improvised body-worn cameras are also being used by BGB personnel while performing their duties.
BGB members remain on alert in coordination with the local administration and police to maintain a peaceful environment in the industrial areas and deal with any possible untoward situation.
The overall situation in the areas concerned is being closely monitored, he said.
The BGB's security operations will continue to ensure public safety, maintain a normal working environment in the industrial areas and keep the law and order situation under control.

item.title: Two motorcyclists killed in collision with covered van on Airport Road
item.description:
Two men riding a motorcycle were killed after it collided with a covered van in front of Xinxian Restaurant on the capital's Airport Road on Thursday morning.
The deceased were identified as Arifur Rahman, 40, and Falu, 55. Both worked at scrap shops in Postogola.
The accident occurred around 10am. Falu died at the scene, while Arifur succumbed to his injuries at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH).
Abul Hasan, a tea stall owner who helped take Arifur to the hospital, said a private car first collided head-on with a covered van in front of the restaurant. A motorcycle then crashed into the same covered van.
One of the motorcyclists died on the spot, while the other, identified as Arifur, was taken to DMCH by police in critical condition, he said.
Fazle Rabbi, a scrap dealer from Postogola, said Arifur worked at his shop, Mitu Enterprise, while Falu was employed at a neighbouring scrap shop.
The two were heading to Tongi in Gazipur to buy scrap materials when the accident occurred, Rabbi said, adding that he learned about the incident over the phone.
Arifur was the son of Awal Molla and hailed from Bedbaria village in Bera upazila of Pabna. He lived in Konapara, Demra, and is survived by two sons and a daughter.
Further details about Falu were not immediately available.
Airport Police Station Sub-Inspector Manik Mahmud confirmed that the motorcycle collided with a covered van in front of Xinjian Restaurant, leaving one person dead at the scene and another dead at the hospital.
The covered van's driver also sustained minor injuries. Police seized both the covered van and the motorcycle.

item.title: Sheikh Hasina's former information adviser arrested in murder case
item.description:
Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury, former information adviser to then prime minister Sheikh Hasina and former chairman of television channel DBC, has been arrested in connection with a murder case filed with Jatrabari police station over the anti-discrimination movement.
Md Shafiqul Islam, additional commissioner (Detective Branch) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), confirmed the arrest Wednesday night.
He said the case was filed on August 26, 2024.
Meanwhile, DBC News journalist Rajib Ghosh was released around midnight after prolonged questioning. He was handed over to his family at around 2am after signing a personal bond.
Earlier on Wednesday afternoon, Detective Branch (DB) officials took Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury and Rajib Ghosh into custody from the DBC News office in Mohakhali, Dhaka, and questioned them at the DB office.
Md Aktar Hossain, deputy commissioner of the DMP's Media and Public Relations Division, earlier said an “unwanted situation” had arisen at the DBC office over the broadcast of a news report.
He said the DB went to the office after receiving information about the incident, following which the two men were taken to the DB office.

item.title: Sagar-Runi murder case: Probe report postponed for 131st time
item.description:
A Dhaka court has postponed the submission of the investigation report in the journalist couple Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi murder case until December 9, marking the 131st delay in the case.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam set the new date after a hearing on Thursday, as the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI), the current investigating agency, failed to submit its report.
The information was confirmed by Rafiqul Islam, a sub-inspector of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s prosecution division.
Sagar, news editor of private television channel Maasranga TV, and Runi, a senior reporter at ATN Bangla, were murdered at their rented home in West Rajabazar, Dhaka, on February 11, 2012. Their four-and-a-half-year-old son, Mahir Sarowar Megh, was at home at the time.
Runi’s brother, Nowsher Alam Roman, filed a murder case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station.
The accused are Rafiqul Islam, Bakul Mia, Masum Mintu, Kamrul Islam alias Arun, Abu Sayeed, the couple’s two residential security guards Palash Rudra Pal and Enayet Ahmed, and their friend Tanvir Rahman Khan. Tanvir and Palash are out on bail, while the others are in jail.
The case was initially investigated by Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police before being transferred to the Detective Branch of Dhaka Metropolitan Police and later to the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB).
On September 30 last year, the High Court directed the formation of a high-powered task force comprising experienced investigators from different law enforcement agencies to investigate the murders. A High Court bench comprising Justices Farah Mahbub and Muhammad Mahbub Ul Islam ordered that the task force be formed through the Ministry of Home Affairs.
On October 23, 2025, the government formed a four-member task force in line with the court directive, with the PBI chief as its convener.

item.title: Workers take to streets again in Ashulia, more than 100 factories shut
item.description:
Labour unrest flared up again in the Ashulia industrial zone on Thursday as garment workers left their factories to press for higher wages, prompting more than 100 factories to suspend operations and disrupting traffic on the Abdullahpur-Baipail road.
Workers initially reported for duty at around 8am, registering their attendance by punching their ID cards. They later left their workplaces, gathered outside other factories and urged workers inside to join the protests.
As the unrest spread, more than 100 factories declared general holidays, and workers took to the streets.
The protesters occupied the Abdullahpur-Baipail road, disrupting traffic. Police intervened at several points to disperse them, after which groups of workers moved to nearby side roads.
Meanwhile, the situation in the Savar industrial zone remained relatively calm on Thursday morning, a day after workers blocked the Dhaka-Aricha highway and set fire to a police van and a motorcycle.
Workers said the Wage Board Commission had announced that a wage increase would take effect in December, but the amount had not been disclosed. They said the uncertainty had contributed to the continuation of their protests.
Security was tightened across the industrial zone to prevent further unrest. Police and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel were deployed, while police armoured vehicles were stationed at key points.
Industrial Police-1 Superintendent Mominul Islam Bhuiyan said the overall situation in the Ashulia area under his unit's jurisdiction was stable.
He said 70 of the 1,863 factories under the unit's jurisdiction had suspended operations for the day, while the rest remained open.
According to Mominul, some people began throwing bricks and stones in the Jamgara area after workers from several factories were dismissed. When police detained some of them, others attacked officers and vandalised police vehicles.
Police then used sound grenades and tear gas to bring the situation under control, he said.
He added that around 2,500 workers had recently held a peaceful march from Jirabo to Envoy factory to protest the killing of a worker in Gazipur.
Mominul said Industrial Police did not have a confirmed figure for those detained in connection with Thursday's incidents and that no one was in their custody at the time of his statement.
He said five BGB platoons, equipped with armoured personnel carriers, had been deployed in the area.
Local police and Industrial Police were coordinating their operations, and legal action was being taken where necessary, he added.
Mominul said most workers wanted to return to their jobs but alleged that outsiders were provoking them and disrupting factory operations, including through social media.
He said the government had formed a Minimum Wage Board and that the new wage structure was scheduled to take effect from January. He added that factory owners were committed to implementing the new minimum wage and that law enforcement agencies were urging workers to return to work.
The police official also said authorities were trying to identify people allegedly inciting unrest through social media. He claimed several people had been detained and information had been obtained during questioning, but declined to disclose their identities, citing the ongoing investigation.
He further alleged that outsiders were using workers as a front to create unrest and sharing information on social media about protest locations and incidents of vandalism. He said it was not clear whether the individuals had any political backing.

item.title: PM lays foundation stone for Tk4,068cr Mongla Port project
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday laid the foundation stone for a Tk4,068 crore project to construct two container jetties and develop supporting infrastructure to expand and modernise Mongla Port.
He laid the foundation stone at a ceremony in Mongla, Bagerhat, at 11:15am, said Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony.
The project aims to expand the port's capacity and modernise its facilities through the construction of two container jetties and the development of associated infrastructure.
Earlier in the morning, the Prime Minister arrived in Mongla by helicopter around 9:50am to attend a series of programmes as part of his daylong visit to Bagerhat and Khulna.
After the arrival, Tarique attended the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) between Invest Bangladesh and China Railway Construction Corporation (CRCC) on economic and infrastructure cooperation in Mongla.
On behalf of Invest Bangladesh, its Member (Industrial Zone) Saleh Ahmed signed the agreement, while China Civil Engineering Construction Corporation Chairman Li Chongyang signed it on behalf of the Chinese side.
Under the MoU, the two sides will explore investment opportunities in key sectors, including energy, industrial infrastructure, green infrastructure, transport, logistics and human resource development.

item.title: Gazipur garment workers return to factories peacefully
item.description:
Garment workers across Gazipur's industrial zones returned to their workplaces peacefully on Thursday morning, following several days of unrest over wage demands and the blacklisting of workers.
Workers reported for duty in Shafipur, Chandra and Palli Bidyut areas of Kaliakair upazila, as well as Bhogra Bypass, Konabari, Kashimpur and Salna in Gazipur metropolitan area.
To maintain law and order, 25 platoons of security personnel remain deployed across the industrial zones, supported by 25 executive magistrates.
The deployment includes 12 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), eight of the Special Reserve Battalion (SRB) and five of Ansar, Arif Hossain, assistant commissioner (Media) at the Gazipur deputy commissioner's office, said.
According to Industrial Police and local sources, workers began arriving at factories in the morning, some using factory-provided transport and others travelling on foot. Workers were seen entering factories in an orderly manner, with no reports of fresh unrest.
Amjad Hossain, superintendent of Gazipur Industrial Police, said workers had joined their shifts peacefully.
He said police and other security forces had intensified patrols to prevent any untoward incidents and maintain law and order.
The situation remained calm and stable amid the deployment of joint security forces, he added.
In recent days, protests and clashes broke out in several industrial areas of Gazipur as workers demanded a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000, reinstatement of laid-off workers and an end to the blacklisting of workers who took part in the demonstrations.

item.title: Police on high alert in Mirpur amid garment workers' protests
item.description:
Law enforcement agencies remain on high alert in Mirpur-11 following protests by garment workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
Additional police personnel have been deployed in the area, with officers patrolling roads and preventing gatherings on streets and sidewalks.
The heightened security measures have been in place since Thursday morning.
Pallabi Police Station Officer-in-Charge Jalal Uddin said the workers had not taken to the streets on Thursday, but police remained prepared to respond to any situation.
“The workers have not taken to the streets today; however, we remain on alert. Additional police have been deployed, and patrols are being conducted. The situation remains normal,” he said.
On November 1, garment workers blocked roads in Mirpur to press their demand for a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Clashes and chases between workers and police continued intermittently from morning until afternoon.
At one point, a police vehicle was set on fire beneath the Mirpur-11 metro rail station. Police later detained several people from different parts of Mirpur in connection with the incident.
Workers also staged protests in Mirpur on Monday and Tuesday.
Similar demonstrations over the wage demand have taken place in Gazipur, Savar, Ashulia and Narayanganj, triggering clashes, disrupting production and forcing many factories to suspend operations.
Meanwhile, Taufiq Sheikh, a garment worker injured during the unrest in Gazipur, died at Shin-Shin Japan Hospital in Uttara, Dhaka, on Tuesday while undergoing treatment.

item.title: Two auto-rickshaw drivers killed after truck hits vehicles in Dhaka
item.description:
Two auto-rickshaw drivers were killed and another person injured after a truck lost control, hit two auto-rickshaws and mounted a sidewalk in Postogola, Kadamtali, in the capital early Thursday.
The deceased were identified as Md Jahangir Poddar, 40, and Md Zakir Hossain, 50.
The accident occurred around 3am. The victims were taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH), where doctors declared Jahangir dead at 4:25am. Zakir was admitted for treatment but later died. The third injured person is receiving medical care.
Both men were auto-rickshaw drivers who had been waiting for passengers at the time of the accident.
Sub-Inspector Md Jamal Hossain of Kadamtali police station said the truck had been seized, but its driver fled the scene.
“The bodies of the two victims have been sent to the Dhaka Medical College morgue for autopsies. Efforts are underway to apprehend the driver,” he said.
Hridoy, a colleague of Jahangir, said three people were injured in the accident. Two died, while the third received treatment at the hospital.
Zakir was the son of Jinnat Ali of Ajmiriganj upazila in Habiganj. He lived in the Pakar Matha area of Mohammadbagh, Kadamtali.
Jahangir was the son of Shah Alam Poddar of Patuakhali Sadar upazila. He lived in the Nama Shyampur area.

The performance was part of sports and cultural diplomacy between Bangladesh and China.

Under the program, BKSP coaches provide cricket training to students of the Chinese university, while its coaches train BKSP students in wushu, a traditional Chinese martial art.
BKSP athletes also receive training from Chinese coaches in table tennis, athletics, badminton, swimming and diving.
The training exchange and cultural performances reflect the growing sports and cultural cooperation between the two countries.
