item.title: Indian visa applicants face new form requirement
item.description:
The Indian High Commission in Dhaka has made it mandatory for all visa applicants to submit a prescribed ‘Visa Undertaking Form’ along with their applications.
The high commission announced the requirement in an urgent advisory published on its visa portal on Thursday.
Under the new instructions, applicants must download the designated form from the link provided by the high commission, fill it out correctly, scan it and upload it with their online applications through the NIC Visa Application Portal. Applications submitted using any other format will not be accepted.
The high commission said the initiative aims to make the visa application process more transparent and orderly.
The one-page form requires applicants to declare that they will visit India only for the purpose stated in their applications, that they reside within the jurisdiction of the Indian High Commission in Dhaka on the date of application, and that all information provided is accurate.
In the personal details section, applicants must provide five mandatory details: their name as shown in the passport, passport number, nationality, date of birth and current address in Dhaka.
They must also clearly state the purpose of their visit, such as tourism, business, medical treatment or attending a conference.
The undertaking includes commitments to return to their home country immediately after the visit, not overstay their visa and comply with Indian laws, regulations and culture while in the country.
The form warns that violations of Indian laws may lead to visa cancellation and affect an applicant’s eligibility for future visas.
Applicants must sign the form and mention the place and date of signing. For minors, both parents are required to sign it.

item.title: BNP leader’s son shot dead in Khulna during PM’s visit
item.description:
A youth was shot dead by unidentified assailants at a tea stall in Dumuria upazila of Khulna on Thursday, coinciding with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s visit to the district.
The deceased, Tarikul Islam Sheikh, 35, was the son of Abdus Salam Sheikh, convener of the BNP’s No 12 Rangpur Union unit.
The incident took place at around 1:45pm at Gaffar’s tea stall in the Jora Botola area of Amvita-Ramkrishnapur. The prime minister entered Khulna by road from Bagerhat at around 3pm.
According to local residents and eyewitnesses, Tarikul was sitting inside the tea stall when assailants entered and opened fire on him, killing him on the spot.
The motive behind the killing and the identities of the attackers were not immediately known.
Dumuria Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Khandaker Hafizur Rahman said he went to the scene after receiving information about the incident. Police have launched an investigation and are conducting operations in the area to identify and arrest those involved.
Khulna Superintendent of Police Omar Faruk said he had received reports that a young man had been shot.
"The motive behind the shooting is being investigated. Necessary action will be taken based on the findings," he said.
Earlier, on October 22, a man named Tushar, 35, was shot dead in the Mistripara area of Khulna city in the early hours of the day Prime Minister Tarique Rahman visited the Sundarbans, made a landing in Dacope and visited Mongla.
Later that evening, assailants shot dead Khushi Akter in the Jinnahpara area in front of her mother.

item.title: Zverev, Djokovic crash out of Paris Masters, Alcaraz advances
item.description:
Alexander Zverev said he was "annoyed" at having to justify being world number one as he lost his opening match at the Paris Masters, while 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic also fell on a Wednesday full of upsets.
Carlos Alcaraz avoided a similar fate, however, as the seven-time major winner beat Alex Michelsen 7-6 (7/4), 6-3 to get his campaign off to a safe start.
Long seen as tennis' nearly-man, 29-year-old Zverev broke his major duck this year by winning the French and US Opens, which propelled him to the top of the ATP rankings for the first time in his career this month.
But his reign as world number one got off to a disappointing start as 24th-ranked Lorenzo Musetti eased to a 7-6 (7/5), 6-2 win over the German to reach the third round.
"Stress, I don't know if stress. I was a bit annoyed, to be honest," Zverev told reporters.
"I feel like I'm the only world number one in tennis history that has to explain why it's okay for me to be world number one, which I find quite difficult, because I think I deserve to be where I am, even though I lost today."
After being in a dominant position in the first-set tie-break, Zverev accumulated errors to lose five consecutive points and then six of the following eight games to crash out at the first hurdle.
"I said even before playing with him that today was going to be the best challenge and the toughest challenge that this sport can give me. So I'm really happy that I took my chances today," Italian former world number five Musetti said.
Djokovic saw his hopes of winning an eighth Paris Masters title and qualifying for the ATP Finals disappear as he went out 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 to world number 83 Rinky Hijikata.
After sailing to the first set, the 39-year-old then found himself in a battle with the Australian qualifier.
Hijikata broke Djokovic in the eighth game of the second frame before serving out to force a decider.
The third set ground on until the Serb cracked twice in a row on serve to hand his 25-year-old opponent victory.
The loss effectively brought to an end Djokovic's season with the veteran telling reporters his plan for the coming weeks was "just rest".
The 2023 Australian Open doubles champion will play Tomas Martin Etcheverry for a berth in the quarter-finals, after the Argentine downed Australian eighth seed Alex de Minaur 7-6 (7/2), 6-3.
Former world number one Daniil Medvedev joined the top-seed exit list as the fifth-ranked Russian crashed out in straight sets to Peru's Ignacio Buse.
Second seed Alcaraz managed to buck the trend with victory over 35th-ranked American Michelsen in the night session.
"Really happy to get the win," Alcaraz said on-court.
"It's been a really difficult day for the top guys, but I just try not to think about it and I try to step out there, play my best and enjoy," he later told reporters, after avoiding a repeat of his own opening defeat in the French capital last year.
Both players exchanged breaks of serve midway through the first set as the opener rumbled towards a tie-break.
Michelsen raced into a 4-1 lead in the breaker before Alcaraz found his forehand and blitzed through the next six points to seize the lead.
After a tightly-contested second frame, Alcaraz got a crucial break ahead in the eighth game and then promptly served out to move into the last 16.
Elsewhere, seventh seed Frances Tiafoe also lost his opening match, going down 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (11/9) to Quentin Halys.
The Frenchman's victory over the American was doubly good news for the host country as it meant Arthur Fils qualified for the ATP Finals.
The French world number seven is now assured of making his debut at the season-ending tournament, which runs November 15-22 in Turin.
With that weight off his shoulders the 22-year-old closed play for the day with a 6-3, 7-6 (7/4) win over Czech qualifier Tomas Machac.
Ben Shelton will headline the day session on Thursday as the third seed takes on home favourite Arthur Rinderknech for a spot in the last eight, before Alcaraz returns in the night session to face Matteo Berrettini.

item.title: Real Madrid set to appoint tennis great Nadal to board
item.description:
Real Madrid plan to appoint retired tennis superstar Rafael Nadal to their board of directors, the club said on Wednesday.
Nadal, a 22-time Grand Slam winner, has been an honorary club member since 2011 and shares a strong relationship with Madrid president Florentino Perez.
"For Real Madrid and for all Madrid supporters, it is a source of immense pride that a figure of his sporting and human stature -- a benchmark of Spanish and world sport -- should become part of our board of directors and, in this role, contribute to the present and future of our club," said Los Blancos in a statement.
Real Madrid's socios -- members -- are expected to ratify Nadal's appointment at the club's general assembly on November 21.
"I want to thank president Florentino Perez and the board for proposing that I join the board of directors of Real Madrid," wrote Nadal on social media platform X.
"I have accepted this proposal with great excitement, I'm eager to learn and to contribute everything I can."
Nadal, 40, won a record 14 French Open singles titles in a glittering career.
In 2023 Nadal said one day he would like to be Madrid president, but did not know if he was qualified for the post.
Ahead of club elections this year Nadal distanced himself from reports that he would stand as a candidate.
Perez triumphed in June, beating Enrique Riquelme.

First ship of the season departs for Saint Martin’s with over 800 tourists
item.description:
After a long wait, the Cox’s Bazar–Saint Martin’s sea route has reopened for the new tourist season, with the first vessel carrying more than 800 passengers departing for the island on Thursday morning.
The vessel, MV Auliya, left the BIWTA jetty in Cox’s Bazar at 7:40am.
The jetty area was crowded from the early hours as families, groups of friends and students gathered for the season’s maiden voyage. Tourists expressed excitement at the prospect of visiting the country’s only coral island after the long break.
Md Mashiyur Rahman, a representative appointed by the Cox’s Bazar district administration and the Land Commissioner of Cox’s Bazar Sadar Upazila, said the vessel departed on schedule.
He said the district administration, Coast Guard, Naval Police, Fire Service and other agencies had coordinated security arrangements to ensure passengers’ safety.
Hossain Islam Bahadur, general secretary of the Sea Cruise Operators Owners Association of Bangladesh (SCOAB), said the turnout of more than 800 tourists on the first day was encouraging.
He said public interest in visiting Saint Martin’s remained strong and that the government had permitted tourist vessels to operate, taking into consideration the livelihoods of the island’s residents.
Bahadur said operators were working to build tourists’ confidence by prioritizing safety, punctuality, environmental protection and service quality.
He added that tourists had been instructed to avoid polluting the vessels and the island, particularly by improperly disposing of plastic bottles and other waste.
Sabina Yasmin, who travelled from Dhaka with her family, said she had been planning the trip for a long time.
“It feels wonderful to be on the first ship of the season. Seeing the beauty of the sea this morning makes it feel as though the journey itself is half the joy of the entire trip,” she said.
Mehedi Hasan, a university student from Chattogram travelling with friends, said he had visited the island once before and was excited to return at the start of the season.
He urged visitors to protect the island’s natural environment and avoid leaving plastic and other waste behind.
Rubel Ahmed, a tourist from Rajshahi, said he had long wanted to see Bangladesh’s only coral island.
“My entire family is overjoyed. I hope that, following a safe journey, we will return home with wonderful memories,” he said.
Saint Martin’s is known for its clear waters, coral formations, coconut trees and beaches, attracting domestic and international visitors. Tourism is also a major source of income for the island’s residents.
Business owners said the resumption of the sea route was expected to benefit hotels, resorts, restaurants, transport services and small businesses on the island.
The Cox’s Bazar district administration said tourism activities must be conducted responsibly to protect the island’s environment and biodiversity. It urged visitors to reduce plastic use, follow travel guidelines and avoid damaging natural resources, including coral.
The successful start to the season has raised hopes among tourism operators and local businesses. Further growth in visitor numbers will depend on favourable weather and compliance with the rules governing travel to the island.

item.title: CPC leader Liu: Ready to work together with all sectors of society in Bangladesh
item.description:
Minister of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee (IDCPC) Liu Haixing on Wednesday said they, standing at a new historical starting point, stand ready to work together with all sectors of society in Bangladesh to carry forward friendship, foster consensus, deepen exchanges and mutual learning.
“We must stand together through thick and thin and jointly build a path of friendship,” said Liu, a member of the Communist Party of China (CPC) central committee, while delivering keynote speech at a seminar.
He also highlighted the importance of enhancing people-to-people ties, so as to turn the traditional friendship into momentum for progress and let Bangladesh-China relations shine more brilliantly in the new era.
"In China, there is a saying - one should mirror the past to understand the present; without the past, the present cannot be. History has bestowed on us a precious friendship that spans generations," said the Chinese leader.
The seminar titled “Where History Illuminates the Future: China-Bangladesh “Political Parties Plus” Roundtable & Inauguration Ceremony of Bangladesh-China Centre for Party and State Governance Studies”, was hosted by the Chinese Embassy in Dhaka at InterContinental Dhaka.
BNP acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi spoke as the chief at the seminar chaired by Chargé d'Affaires (CDA) at the Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Dhaka Dr Liu Yuyin.
Secretary General of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Mia Golam Parwar, National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener and Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam, President of Bangladesh China Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BCCCI) Mohd. Khorshed Alam and international affairs expert Dr Imtiaz Ahmed, among others, spoke at the seminar.
Prime Minister’s Adviser Nazrul Islam Khan, BNP Vice Chairman, a former Bangladesh Air Force Chief, and a former Minister of Home Affairs Air Vice Marshal (retd) Altaf Hossain Chowdhury, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam, State Minister for Land and Chittagong Hill Tracts Affairs Mir Mohammed Helal Uddin and State Minister for Social Welfare Farzana Sharmin, among others, were present.
This year marks the 105th anniversary of the founding of the Communist Party of China. "As a century-old major party still in its prime, the CPC has been continuously exploring ways to strengthen itself," Liu said.
"Since the 18th CPC National Congress, centering on the epochal question of what kind of long-term ruling Marxist political party we should build and how to build it, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has put forward a series of new ideas, thinking and strategies to govern, invigorate and strengthen the Party, thus forming Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building," he said.
Last week, Liu said, the CPC successfully convened the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, during which important arrangements were made for persevering with full and rigorous party self-governance from the strategic height of consolidating the ruling status of the party and fulfilling its missions and tasks.
"We are ready to strengthen exchanges on the outcome of the Plenary Session, especially Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building with political parties and all sectors of Bangladesh," he said.
Liu said Bangladesh and China are linked by mountains and seas, across the millennia, they have respected each other amid exchanges of civilizations, stood by one another amid shifting circumstances, and advanced side by side along our development journeys, jointly writing a remarkable chapter of friendship between close neighbors.
He said history not only records their precious past, but also lights the path ahead. “Ten years ago, General Secretary Xi Jinping paid a historic visit to Bangladesh, elevating bilateral relations to a strategic cooperative partnership,” Liu said.
Last June, President Xi Jinping met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman during his visit to China.
The two leaders jointly announced the building of a China-Bangladesh community with a shared future in the new era, charting the course for a new chapter in their friendship. “We must stay firmly on course and jointly build a path of trust.”
“I cherish a special bond with Bangladesh. Forty-six years ago, my father served as China’s Ambassador to Bangladesh. From then on, I often heard him speak of the hardworking and kind-hearted Bangladeshi people and his deep affection for this land caressed by monsoon,” he said.
The CPC leader said this reflects the continuity of Bangladesh-China friendship, and reinforces my conviction that our friendship enjoys enduring vitality that transcends time, takes deep root among our peoples, and grows ever stronger.
Since the establishment of diplomatic relations, he said Bangladesh and China have been committed to friendship.
“We stand firm as trusted good friends, neighbours and partners. Amid profound changes unseen in a century, it is all the more important for us to follow the guidance of our leaders, and firmly respect, understand and support one another on issues bearing on each other’s core interests and major concerns,” Liu said, adding that “We must light the way for each other and jointly build a path of development.”
Over the past five decades, bilateral trade surged from 15 million to more than 23 billion US dollars.
Liu said Bangladesh was the first South Asian country to sign a memorandum of understanding on Belt and Road cooperation with China.
Over the years, a host of projects including highways, bridges and tunnels have been delivered across Bangladesh, giving a strong boost to local economic and social development, he said.
“Today, progress is steady on major projects such as the Mongla Port Industrial Park and the comprehensive treatment and restoration of the Teesta River. We believe these initiatives will bring greater benefits to peoples of both countries,” said the CPC leader said.
He said they should work together to act on the four Global Initiatives put forward by General Secretary Xi Jinping, step up communication and coordination within multilateral frameworks including the UN, and promote an equal and orderly multipolar world and a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalisation.
“This will better safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of China, Bangladesh and the shared interests of the Global South,” he said.
He said China-Bangladesh friendship is not an undertaking of a small number of people, but a consensus across all sectors of our societies.
“That is what makes it so precious. Polls show that 90 percent of Bangladeshi people hold a favorable opinion of China. This hard-won achievement deserves to be cherished,” he said.
“Over the years, you have devoted yourselves to your respective fields and helped nurture the foundation of China-Bangladesh friendship with great care,” said the CPC leader.
“We count on your continuous efforts to further consolidate the broad consensus for friendship between our two countries, and let the tree of China-Bangladesh friendship flourish ever more vibrantly.”
Going forward, Liu said, it is hoped that the Center will deepen research on and interpretation of the underlying logic of governance of the two countries to enhance mutual understanding; share each other’s governance philosophies to enhance mutual learning; and boost cooperation across the board to deepen the friendship.
He said the Center can facilitate more exchanges between political parties, youths, business communities, media outlets and think tanks, so as to contribute to building a China-Bangladesh community with a shared future in the new era.

item.title: President calls for stronger Bangladesh-China ties
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Wednesday called for further strengthening bilateral relations between Bangladesh and China, describing the country as a trusted friend and an important strategic partner.
He made the remarks when Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee Liu Haixing paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban, President's Press Secretary Md Sarwar Alam told UNB.
During the meeting, the president referred to the signing of a framework agreement for the modernisation and expansion of Mongla Port and the groundbreaking of the Chinese Economic and Industrial Zone (CEIZ), saying these initiatives would make significant contributions to Bangladesh's connectivity, industrialisation and economic development.
He also welcomed Chinese President Xi Jinping's proposals for expanding multidimensional connectivity, including the proposed Kunming-Chittagong corridor and the China-Myanmar-Bangladesh Economic Corridor.
Mirza Fakhrul thanked and congratulated Xi Jinping and invited him to visit Bangladesh at a convenient time.
Emphasising greater Chinese investment in Bangladesh, he highlighted sectors that could contribute to technology transfer, employment generation and export diversification.
Liu Haixing assured continued Chinese cooperation in areas such as green energy, education and cultural exchanges.
The president thanked China for its support in financing and constructing the 1,000-bed Bangladesh-China Friendship General Hospital and sought Beijing's continued active role in ensuring the safe repatriation of Rohingyas to Myanmar.
The Chinese minister assured that China would continue its cooperation in this regard.
Mirza Fakhrul also expressed gratitude for China's continued assistance amid the ongoing energy crisis.
Recalling the visits to China by Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman in 1977 and 1980, he said those historic visits had laid the foundation for bilateral relations between the two countries.
Liu Haixing said Bangladesh's diplomatic relations with China had been established during Ziaur Rahman's tenure and further strengthened during the tenure of then prime minister Khaleda Zia.
He expressed hope that bilateral relations would become stronger and broader under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
Referring to his recent visit to China, the president said his meetings with the Chinese vice president and the visiting minister had been fruitful and helped further strengthen mutual relations.
Mentioning Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to China in June, he said the visit would play an important role in taking bilateral relations to new heights.
Mirza Fakhrul described the prime minister's interactions with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Premier Li Qiang and other top Chinese leaders, along with the signing of memorandums of understanding and other cooperation documents, as positive developments in bilateral ties.
He wished Liu Haixing continued success and good health.
Earlier, the president welcomed the Chinese minister with flowers when he arrived at Bangabhaban and introduced him to his secretaries.
Among the members of the Chinese delegation were Chargé d'Affaires of the Chinese Embassy in Dhaka Liu Yuin and Director General of the Bureau of Southeast and South Asian Affairs of the CPC Central Committee's International Department Peng Xiubin.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam and Foreign Ministry Secretary Salahuddin Noman Chowdhury were also present.
After the meeting, the president accompanied the Chinese minister and other delegation members on a tour of Bangabhaban.
During the visit, video footage of Liu Haixing's father, former ambassador Liu Shuqing, presenting his credentials to then President Ziaur Rahman in 1980 was shown.
Photographs of Mirza Fakhrul's visit to China during his tenure as Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives (LGRD) Minister were also displayed.
The president's military secretary, secretary of the public division and press secretary were present.

item.title: Bangladesh, Kosovo stress parliamentary ties, trade and investment
item.description:
National Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad Bir Bikram on Wednesday held a courtesy meeting with Kosovo Ambassador to Bangladesh Lulzim Plana at his office in the Parliament Complex, highlighting the need to strengthen parliamentary cooperation, trade and investment between the two countries.
During the meeting, the speaker said the people of Kosovo had made supreme sacrifices for their country's independence, adding that Bangladesh and Kosovo shared common bonds of independence and cultural heritage.
He also highlighted the close cultural ties between the two nations, said a press release issued by the Parliament Secretariat this evening.
The speaker alleged that the democratic rights of the people of Bangladesh had been undermined over the past 17 years through farcical elections.
He said the Awami League government had established a reign of terror through enforced disappearances, killings, extrajudicial executions and vote rigging.
Referring to the UN fact-finding report, the Speaker said it had exposed the brutal and inhumane nature of the previous government's rule.
He said the July Mass Uprising of 2024 had ended Sheikh Hasina's autocratic rule and paved the way for Bangladesh's renewed democratic journey.
Major Hafiz described the 13th parliamentary election as one of the freest, fairest and most credible elections in the country's history. He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman was working to fulfill the aspirations of the people.
Kosovo Ambassador Lulzim Plana said a new democratic chapter had begun in Bangladesh, praising the active participation of lawmakers in parliamentary debates.
He noted that a large section of Bangladesh's population was young and economically active, saying they could make significant contributions to the national economy through quality education and information technology (IT) skills.
The ambassador expressed gratitude to Bangladesh for recognising Kosovo as an independent state and invited the Speaker to visit Kosovo.
Both sides emphasised the formation of a parliamentary caucus between the two countries, expansion of trade and investment, promotion of joint academic and research activities, and strengthening of exchanges in sports and culture.
Representatives of the Kosovo Embassy, the Parliament Secretariat secretary and other senior officials concerned were present at the meeting.

item.title: ECNEC approves 13 projects worth Tk58088.92cr; govt to drill 2 new gas wells
item.description:
The Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) on Wednesday approved a total of 13 development projects with an estimated cost of Tk58,088.92 crore, including a fresh project to drill two new gas wells at Tk592 crore for availing 30 mmcfd.
Prime Minister and ECNEC Chairman Tarique Rahman presided over the sixth ECNEC meeting of the current fiscal year (FY27) at the Cabinet Room of Bangladesh Secretariat on Wednesday.
Of the approved 13 projects, 11 are new while two are revised projects.
Of the total estimated cost of Tk58,088.92 crore, the government will provide Tk50,041.20 crore, Tk73.07 crore will come from concerned organization’s own funds, while the rest of Tk7,974.65 crore from project assistance.
State Minister for Planning Md Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki briefed reporters after the meeting at the NEC Conference Room in the city’s Sher-e-Bangla Nagar area.
According to the Planning Commission, the government will drill two appraisal-cum-development wells at the Titas Gas Field at an estimated cost of Tk592 crore to increase domestic gas production by around 30 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd).
The project titled "Drilling of Two Appraisal-cum-Development Wells (Titas-32 and Titas-33) at Titas Gas Field" will be implemented by the Bangladesh Gas Fields Company Limited (BGFCL), a Petrobangla subsidiary, under the Energy and Mineral Resources Division of the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources till September 2029.
Of the total estimated cost, Tk414.40 crore will come from government financing and Tk177.60 crore from the company's own funds.
The government has set a target to drill 150 wells by 2031 to raise gas output, followed by another 150 wells during the 2031-'35 period to further strengthen the country's local gas production.
According to the proposal, the wells could produce around 100.74 billion cubic feet (BCF) of gas and 60,444 barrels of condensate over 10 years. The estimated value of the output at the company's existing wellhead prices stands at Tk339.07 crore, including Tk285.26 crore for gas and Tk53.81 crore for condensate.
At consumer-level gas prices, the estimated value of the gas output over the same period would be Tk6,523.97 crore.
BGFCL currently supplies around 480-485 million cubic feet of gas daily to the national grid from five of its six operational gas fields. The Titas Gas Field, the company's largest, produces around 330 million cubic feet daily from 23 of its 28 drilled wells.
The project follows a review of three-dimensional seismic survey data collected at the Titas and Bakhrabad gas fields during 2010-2012. BGFCL engaged BGP Inc. of China National Petroleum Corporation to review the data. The consultant recommended drilling 16 infill wells and seven deep wells.
The government has prioritised Titas-32 and Titas-33 under its plan to drill 150 onshore gas wells to increase domestic production.
The project will cover drilling the two wells through a foreign contractor, engaging local and foreign consultants, installing gas-gathering pipelines and carrying out related works.
The Infrastructure Investment Facilitation Company (IIFC) conducted the feasibility study in 2026. The Planning Commission said the project would support domestic gas production, industrial development and foreign exchange savings by reducing LNG imports.
The proposal was revised following a Project Evaluation Committee meeting held on June 18, 2026, which recommended rationalising project costs. The estimated cost was reduced by Tk40 crore from the initial proposal of Tk632 crore to Tk592 crore.
In the day’s meeting, the Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Ministry secured approval for five projects, while the Home Ministry received approval for two projects. The Ministries of Defence, Housing and Public Works, Science and Technology, Education, Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, and Disaster Management and Relief received approval for one project each.
Planning Ministry officials said the 13 projects include initiatives covering safe water supply and sanitation in the Barind region with Taka 1,203.73 crore, re-excavation of canals in Barishal City Corporation, and local economic development in selected municipalities with Tk730.66 crore.
The three other projects under the Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Ministry include Innovation for Climate-Smart Urban Development Project with Tk87.40 crore; Social Infrastructure Development Project (SIDP) with Tk2,565.59 crore and the Priority Basis Important Rural Infrastructure Development Project-03 (Third Revision) with an additional cost of Tk3,951.37 crore.
The two projects approved under the Home Ministry involve the procurement of specialised vehicles and operational vehicles to enhance the capacity of Bangladesh Police.
The Defence Ministry will implement a project to construct Type-B officers’ residential accommodation in the Moinul Road residential area of Dhaka Cantonment with Tk177.19 crore.
The Housing and Public Works Ministry will construct multi-storey residential buildings for government employees at Gabtala Colony in Jigatala with Taka 200.11 crore.
The Science and Technology Ministry will establish Institutes of Nuclear Medicine and Allied Sciences (INMAS) on the campuses of five medical college hospitals across the country with Tk535.54 crore.
The Education Ministry received approval for the Fifth Primary Education Development Programme (PEDP-5) with Tk41,090.48 crore.
The Disaster Management and Relief Ministry will implement the third revised project for constructing bridges and culverts up to 15 metres in length on rural roads with an additional cost of Tk523.34 crore.
Meanwhile, the meeting was informed about five projects costing less than Tk50 crore each that the planning minister had already approved.
The projects include the modernisation of cardiac treatment services at Zia Heart Foundation Hospital and Research Institute in Dinajpur; ensuring safe internet use for children, adolescents and secondary-level students; improvement of traffic infrastructure and road safety in Dhaka North City Corporation (first revision); expansion and modernisation of the Dhaka Central Drug Addiction Treatment Centre (first revision); and procurement of modern vehicles and equipment to improve waste management in Gazipur City Corporation.
Ministers, advisers to the prime minister, and state ministers concerned attended the meeting, while Planning Commission members and secretaries concerned were present.

item.title: PM’s Mongla visit raises hopes for economic growth in southwest
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is scheduled to visit Mongla Port and Khulna on Thursday, raising expectations of a major boost to port capacity, investment, and employment across the southwestern region.
During the visit, he will lay the foundation stone for a Tk4,068 crore project to construct two container jetties and develop associated facilities at Mongla Port.
The port project is expected to modernize infrastructure, increase cargo-handling capacity, and create new opportunities for domestic and foreign investment, generating employment in the region.
According to Mongla Port Authority, the project follows an agreement signed between Bangladesh and China on October 10. China will provide Tk3,593 crore, while the Bangladesh government will contribute Tk475 crore.
The project includes a 368-metre container terminal and yard, specialized facilities for handling hazardous goods, and 49 pieces of equipment. Once completed, the facilities will enable the port to handle more than 30 containers per hour and raise its annual handling capacity to 400,000 TEUs.
The prime minister will also attend the signing of a memorandum of understanding between Invent Bangladesh and China Railway Construction Corporation (CRCC).
State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Sheikh Faridul Islam said the visit would help establish Mongla Port as an important hub for international trade while accelerating economic activities, and creating employment opportunities across the region.
After visiting Mongla, the prime minister will pay his respects at the shrine of Hazrat Khan Jahan Ali before travelling to Khulna District Stadium to inaugurate the "Notun Kuri sports competition (season 2)".
At a press briefing, National Parliament Whip Rakibul Islam said the initiative would encourage young people to pursue sports professionally and help restore Khulna's reputation as a sports city.
Youth and Sports Ministry Secretary Mahfuzul Alam Khan said around 16.23 lakh online registrations had been received for the sports competition, compared with 168,000 in the first. The competition will feature 10 sporting events.

item.title: Moyeen Khan returns home from hospital
item.description:
Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives Minister and BNP Standing Committee Member Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan returned home from hospital on Wednesday afternoon after receiving treatment.
He was discharged from Evercare Hospital Dhaka at 3:30pm, said BNP Media Cell Member Sayrul Kabir Khan.
Moyeen Khan was admitted to the hospital on October 21 after suddenly falling ill.
He received treatment under the supervision of a medical board.
According to doctors' advice, he will have to take rest for a few more days.

Sajek blockade chokes supplies, paralyses local economy
item.description:
Sajek in Rangamati has remained under a blockade for 14 consecutive days, disrupting road communication, triggering shortages of essential commodities and bringing tourism-related businesses to a standstill.
No vehicles operated on the Sajek road on Wednesday, leaving residents struggling to access food and other daily necessities. Farmers are also unable to transport their produce to markets, putting their livelihoods at risk.
Hundreds of drivers and their assistants who depend on transporting tourists have lost their income. Many are borrowing money to support their families, while vehicle owners who purchased vehicles with loans are struggling to repay instalments.
Meanwhile, the Parbatya Chattagram Rakkha Committee has announced a separate 48-hour blockade for November 4 and 5, protesting the ongoing blockade in Sajek. The program was announced in a press release signed by the organization's member secretary, Bindu Lal Chakma, on Tuesday evening.
The move has further complicated efforts to resolve the crisis through dialogue between the administration and protesters.
Although progress was made on four of the five demands raised by the protesters, no agreement has been reached on the main point of contention. At a meeting between protesters and a government delegation in Ujobaazar on October 26, the two sides reached an understanding on four demands. However, disagreements over the demand to remove armed JSS members from Sajek prevented a final agreement.
The Sajek Gono Odhikar Rakkha Committee and Sajek Karbari Association resumed the blockade on Monday, November 2, after a one-day relaxation on November 1. On Tuesday, protesters placed tree trunks and lit fires at several points along the Sajek tourist road, effectively halting traffic.
However, leaders of the two organizations have announced exemptions for vehicles carrying locally produced agricultural goods, teachers, and students.
In a joint statement on Tuesday, Sajek Gono Odhikar Rakkha Committee convener Babudhan Chakma and Sajek Karbari Association president Natun Joy Chakma said the decision was taken at a joint meeting of the organizations.
Vehicles carrying agricultural produce and transporting teachers and students to educational institutions will be exempt from the blockade. Earlier exemptions for ambulances, electricity supply vehicles, vehicles used for religious and wedding ceremonies, and journalists' vehicles will also remain in place.
The leaders said the decision was taken considering the interests of farmers and agricultural traders from both the Pahari and Bengali communities. However, they reiterated that the blockade would continue until all five demands were met.
Baghaichhari Upazila Nirbahi Officer Amena Marjan said no decision had been made on holding another meeting. She added that Sajek Valley would remain closed until further notice on the instructions of the district administration due to security concerns.
On November 1, protesters announced a 12-hour relaxation to allow residents to collect food and other essential supplies. However, a counter-blockade by the Parbatya Chattagram Rakkha Committee and a work abstention by transport owners and workers prevented normal traffic from resuming.
Rahul Chakma, organizing secretary of the Sajek Resort-Cottage Owners Association, said the tourism-dependent economy had been hit hardest by the crisis.
With no tourists, resorts, cottages, restaurants, transport services, local shops and other tourism-related businesses have virtually ground to a halt.
He estimated that the blockade had already caused losses of Tk30-35 crore, warning that the figure could rise further if the disruption continued.
According to him, Sajek has more than 116 resorts, 14 restaurants and over 100 small and large shops. The prolonged absence of tourists has left business owners, cottage operators and employees struggling to make ends meet.
The blockade has also disrupted road communication between Sajek, Baghaichhari upazila headquarters and Khagrachhari, worsening shortages of rice, lentils and other essential commodities.
Anitya Tripura, a member of Ward 2 of Sajek Union Parishad, said residents were running out of food and other essential supplies stored at home. Five shops in Ruilui Para had also run out of daily necessities.
Jaupeithang Tripura, headman of Shialdai Mouza and a union parishad member, said farmers and small traders were unable to take their produce to markets because of the blockade and the absence of tourists. He said the disruption had paralyzed the rural economy, with shortages of medicines and other essential goods also emerging.
Khagrachhari Transport Owners' Association president Ayush Chakma said the association had 250 registered vehicles, while the Jeep Owners' Association had more than 500. In addition, more than 1,500 vehicles, including Mahindra three-wheelers, Chander Gari and CNG-run auto-rickshaws, operate in Sajek.
He said the blockade had cut off the income of drivers and their assistants, while many vehicle owners were struggling to repay loans. The transport sector in the district was suffering estimated daily losses of Tk30-40 lakh, he added.
Sajek police station Officer-in-Charge Tofazzal Hossain said large vehicles were not operating on the road due to the blockade, although a few auto-rickshaws and motorcycles were moving occasionally.
He said the situation remained calm and peaceful, with no major untoward incidents reported so far.
The latest blockade began on October 22, following earlier disruptions. A temporary relaxation was announced from October 16 to 21 for Durga Puja, while tourism activities had already been suspended following a blockade that began on October 11.
Despite repeated blockades and temporary relaxations, no lasting solution has emerged, leaving residents, farmers, businesses and transport workers uncertain about when normal life will resume.

item.title: Workers' protest: Additional police, water cannons deployed in Mirpur, Uttara
item.description:
Police have deployed additional personnel in the capital’s Mirpur and Uttara areas as garment workers continue protests demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
In Pallabi, police dispersed workers who had gathered in front of several garment factories, while law enforcement agencies remained on high alert in Uttara.
The heightened security measures have been in place since Wednesday morning.
Md Hafizur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Mirpur Model Police Station, said there had been no major incidents related to the workers’ protests in the area.
Of the eight garment factories under the police station’s jurisdiction, seven remained operational. Workers at one factory had initially stopped working but resumed operations after being persuaded to do so, he said.
Additional police personnel had been deployed since the morning and remained on high alert, the OC added.
Earlier on Wednesday, police dispersed workers who had gathered outside several garment factories in an alley near Purabi Cinema Hall in Mirpur-11. Tension arose between workers and police, but no untoward incidents were reported.
In Uttara, police and other law enforcement personnel were also on high alert. Police took positions along the stretch from Rajlokkhi to the airport to prevent any untoward incidents. Water cannons and police vans were stationed in the area.
On November 1, garment workers blocked roads in Mirpur, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Clashes and chases between workers and police continued from morning until afternoon. At one point, a police vehicle was set on fire beneath the Mirpur-11 metro rail station.
Police have since detained several people from different parts of Mirpur on suspicion of involvement in the incidents.
Garment workers also staged protests in Mirpur on Monday and Tuesday. Workers in Gazipur, Savar, Ashulia and Narayanganj have also been demonstrating over the wage demand. The protests have led to clashes, disrupted production at several factories and forced some to suspend operations.
Taufiq Sheikh, a garment worker injured during the protests in Gazipur, died on Tuesday afternoon while undergoing treatment at Shin-Shin Japan Hospital in Uttara, Dhaka.

item.title: SAU students block roads again in Agargaon over research field
item.description:
More than 1,000 students of Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University (SAU) blocked roads in Agargaon on Wednesday, demanding the restoration of their former research field.
Around 11am, the students marched from the university's flagpole area and took positions at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Centre intersection, bringing traffic to a halt.
The protesters also announced plans to burn an effigy in front of the Public Works Department (PWD) complex in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar on Wednesday.
At a meeting between teachers and students on Tuesday, the protesters announced a boycott of all examinations and said they would not attend classes scheduled after 11am.
Later that night, around 10pm, students from all academic batches gathered at the university's TSC premises and declared an indefinite shutdown. As a result, all academic activities were suspended from Wednesday.
The protests began on October 27, with students claiming that the former trade fair grounds belonged to the university and demanding that the land be handed over to it.
On that day, students seized machinery and vehicles being used for soil testing ahead of the planned construction of a secretariat building on the site and brought them onto the campus.
The following day, after issuing an ultimatum to halt fair-related activities, students vandalised several structures on the grounds.
On October 29, they blocked roads. That same day, State Minister for Youth and Sports Md Aminul Haque announced the suspension of all fairs, including the National Youth Fair.
However, the protesters continued their agitation, demanding the removal of structures from the site and withdrawal of cases filed against unidentified students.
On November 2, they took further action by tilling the land and asserting control over it.

item.title: Hospital vandalized in Mohammadpur over medical bill discount dispute
item.description:
City Hospital and Diagnostic Centre in the capital’s Mohammadpur area was vandalized by a group of young men following a dispute over a discount on a patient's medical bill.
Several people have been arrested in connection with a case filed over the incident, and police are verifying their involvement.
The attack took place around midnight on Tuesday when a group of young men entered the hospital and vandalized the premises. The front section of the facility and its ground-floor reception area were damaged, with furniture and medical equipment left in disarray.
According to hospital sources, a patient named Asma had received treatment at the facility for a lip injury. Her medical bill amounted to Tk2,780, and her relatives requested a discount.
Hospital authorities agreed to reduce the bill partially, but an argument followed. After the patient received treatment and left, a group of young men gathered at the hospital and carried out the attack.
Mohammad Usman Gani, assistant manager of City Hospital Ltd, said the attackers had arrived from the direction of the Graphic Arts Institute.
He alleged that the attackers also looted the facility, causing an estimated Tk50-60 lakh in losses.
Police said they were reviewing CCTV footage to identify those involved. Hospital authorities have filed a case over the incident.
Abdul Halim, officer-in-charge of Mohammadpur police station, confirmed that several people had been arrested in connection with the case. Their involvement is being further investigated, he said.

item.title: Garment worker injured in Gazipur unrest dies in hospital
item.description:
Garment worker Toufiq Sheikh, 22, who was injured during unrest in Gazipur, died at a hospital in Dhaka on Tuesday.
He was a junior layman in the cutting section of Laila Styles Ltd.
Toufiq died at Shin Shin Japan Hospital in Uttara, where he had been undergoing treatment. His body reached his village in Chhaygharia, Gobindaganj, Gaibandha, at around 10pm.
His janaza was scheduled for 9:30am on Wednesday, followed by burial at the village graveyard.
According to his family, Toufiq was recording the unrest on his mobile phone on Monday when he was attacked and beaten.
However, police official Mohammad Belayet Hossain gave a different account, saying outsiders had pressured the factory to shut down, triggering a clash with workers.
Toufiq's brother, Harun Mia, and local teacher Pradip Kumar also spoke about the incident. Officer-in-Charge Mahfuz Alam, Union Parishad chairman Zahurul Haque and Toufiq's uncle Bachchu Mia were among those who provided information about the incident.

item.title: Police fire tear gas as workers throw bricks on Dhaka-Mymensingh highway
item.description:
Police fired tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse garment workers after they threw bricks and stones at law enforcement personnel on the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway near the Signboard area under Gazipur’s Gacha police station on Wednesday morning.
Traffic came to a standstill around 9:30am after workers occupied the highway, bringing vehicles to a halt.
Mohammad Amjad Hossain, superintendent of the Gazipur Industrial Police, said the situation had been calm earlier in the morning.
Around 9:30am, between 2,000 and 4,000 workers took to the streets in the Gacha police station area. A standoff followed, with workers throwing bricks and stones at police, prompting law enforcement personnel to fire tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse them, he said.
Earlier, around 8:30am, another group of workers had gathered near Joydebpur but was also dispersed.
Amjad said the situation remained stable in Salna, Rajendrapur, Shafipur and Palli Bidyut, while tension persisted near Kashimpur. Police remained on high alert, he added.

item.title: Ishraque Hossain named president of martial arts confederation
item.description:
Dhaka-6 MP Ishraque Hossain has been appointed president of the new ad-hoc committee of the Bangladesh Martial Arts Confederation.
Former athlete and sports organizer Mahfuz Hasan has been named its general secretary.
The 29-member committee was announced on Tuesday through an order signed by Md Doltuzzaman Khan, executive director of the National Sports Council (NSC).
According to the order, the previous ad-hoc committee has been dissolved and replaced by the new body, which has been tasked with holding an election within the next three months and handing over responsibility to the elected committee.
The committee has six vice-presidents: Jasmine Nahar, secretary at the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education; Md Monirul Islam, an athlete and sports organizer; Engineer Md Abdul Halim, CEO of Mallick Group; sports organizer Mohammad Tarikul Alam; Md Shahidul Islam; and Shahed Wahed Ali.
Md Shahadat Hossain Khan and Sayeed Md Alvi have been appointed joint secretaries, while Md Habibullah Parvez has been named treasurer.
The committee also includes sports organizers, former athletes, coaches, and international referees and judges.
The NSC said the committee was formed to arrange an election in accordance with the constitution of the Bangladesh Martial Arts Confederation and transfer responsibility to the elected body within three months.

Four killed in head-on collision between bus, laguna in Mirpur
item.description:
Four people, including two women, were killed in a head-on collision between an Asian University bus and a laguna in the Nawab-er-Bagh area of Diabari, Mirpur Beribadh, on Wednesday morning.
The accident occurred around 7:38am within the jurisdiction of Shah Ali police station, said Talha Bin Jasim, media officer of the Fire Service and Civil Defence.
A unit from Kalyanpur Fire Station rushed to the scene after receiving the report and began rescue operations.
According to the Fire Service, the collision took place around 7:30am on Nawab-er-Bagh Road when a speeding passenger bus hit the laguna coming from the opposite direction, killing four people — two men and two women.
No other injuries were reported.
Police arrived at the scene shortly after the accident and took steps to restore normal traffic movement.

item.title: 25 platoons of BGB, SRB, Ansar deployed in Gazipur amid worker unrest
item.description:
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), the Special Reserve Battalion (SRB) and Ansar personnel have been deployed alongside police in Gazipur's industrial areas to maintain law and order amid ongoing garment worker protests over wage demands.
Md Arif Hossain, assistant commissioner (Media and Research Cell) at the Gazipur deputy commissioner's office, confirmed the deployment on Wednesday morning.
He said 10 BGB platoons and 21 executive magistrates were initially deployed on Monday. The deployment was increased on Tuesday to 11 BGB platoons and 25 executive magistrates.
On Wednesday, another BGB platoon was added, bringing the total to 12. Eight SRB platoons and five Ansar platoons were also deployed.
In total, 25 platoons of BGB, SRB and Ansar personnel are working to maintain law and order in Gazipur's industrial areas under the supervision of 25 executive magistrates, Arif said.
As of 8:30am on Wednesday, no reports of worker protests or highway blockades had been received from anywhere in Gazipur.
Traffic on the Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways was moving normally, he added.

item.title: Why Bangladesh is missing the technology revolution
item.description:
A country can become increasingly connected without becoming technologically advanced. It can expand internet access, digitize public services, produce thousands of computer science graduates, and encourage young people to pursue freelancing, yet remain a marginal player in the global technology economy.
Bangladesh risks becoming such a country. While the world is reorganizing its economic architecture around artificial intelligence, semiconductors, robotics, and advanced manufacturing, Bangladesh is still struggling to move beyond the consumption and adaptation of technologies developed elsewhere.
The uncomfortable question is whether the country is preparing to participate in the next industrial transformation or merely positioning itself as a market for its products. The distinction matters because the nature of economic competition is changing.
For decades, Bangladesh's comparative advantages have rested largely on inexpensive labour, export-oriented manufacturing, and a large domestic market. These advantages helped sustain growth, particularly through the ready-made garment industry.
But the emerging global economy increasingly rewards something different: The capacity to generate knowledge, develop intellectual property, design sophisticated products, and commercialize scientific discoveries. The countries that control these capabilities will exercise disproportionate influence over trade, investment, and the distribution of economic power.
The transformation is already visible in the corporate landscape. Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and TSMC represent more than successful businesses. They illustrate how technological capabilities can become strategic national assets.
South Korea's Samsung has been central to its industrial development, while Taiwan's semiconductor industry has established the country as an indispensable part of the global technology supply chain. These achievements were built through sustained investments in research, industrial expertise, and institutional capacity. Technology did not simply follow their economic progress; it helped create it.
The scale of the emerging opportunity is extraordinary. UNCTAD estimates that the global market for 17 frontier technologies, including artificial intelligence, the internet of things, and advanced robotics, could expand to $16.4 trillion by 2033. The AI market alone could approach $4.8 trillion.
Meanwhile, digitally delivered services have already become a multitrillion-dollar segment of international trade. This is not a distant technological possibility. It is an economic transformation unfolding in real time, attracting investment and reshaping the competitive relationship between nations.
Yet Bangladesh's participation remains remarkably modest. The country had set an ambitious target of earning $5bn from ICT exports by 2025. Actual ICT service exports amounted to approximately $724.6m in the 2024-25 fiscal year.
The shortfall is revealing. India has developed an enormous international technology services industry, while Pakistan's reported technology services exports have also exceeded Bangladesh's. The issue is not simply the difference in export earnings. It is the difference in the industrial ecosystems, research capabilities, and international market presence that make such earnings possible.
Bangladesh's predicament is perhaps best understood as an innovation trap - it has made progress in adopting digital technologies but has not developed a corresponding capacity to produce them. It has expanded the number of technology users without building enough technology creators.
Providing services through existing platforms is economically useful; designing the platforms, developing the underlying technologies, and owning the intellectual property can generate substantially greater strategic value.
The roots of this problem extend deep into the education system. Bangladesh continues to measure educational achievement primarily through examinations, grades, and certificates. Students are trained to reproduce information more efficiently than to challenge it, experiment with it, or transform it into new knowledge.
This approach may produce academic credentials, but technological innovation demands a different intellectual culture. It requires curiosity, independent reasoning, tolerance for failure, and the ability to connect knowledge across disciplines. These qualities cannot flourish in an environment where completing the syllabus often takes precedence over developing the capacity to think.
The answer, however, is not to dismiss humanities and social sciences in favour of engineering and computer science. Technological development is not exclusively a scientific enterprise.
Artificial intelligence raises questions of ethics, language, law, culture, and social responsibility. Advanced manufacturing requires management, communication, and institutional expertise.
What Bangladesh needs is an education system capable of connecting scientific knowledge with social understanding and practical application. The problem is not the presence of particular academic disciplines but the absence of meaningful intellectual and professional integration among them.
The weakness of the research environment makes this educational limitation even more serious. According to the University Grants Commission, public universities allocated only Tk190.65 crore for research out of a total approved budget of approximately Tk13,222 crore in the 2025-26 fiscal year. That amounts to around 1.44%.
Even this modest allocation is not always fully utilized. How can universities become centres of innovation when research remains a marginal component of their institutional priorities?
A university should be more than an institution that supplies graduates to the employment market. It should be a place where existing knowledge is questioned, new ideas are developed, and practical solutions emerge.
In Bangladesh, however, the connection between academic research and economic production remains weak. Researchers frequently lack adequate laboratories, funding, technological equipment, and opportunities to work with industries. Businesses, meanwhile, often prefer imported solutions because domestic research institutions cannot consistently provide commercially viable alternatives.
This disconnect creates a peculiar economic contradiction. Universities produce graduates, industries complain about the shortage of appropriately skilled workers, and the government invests in technology-related infrastructure, yet these three components rarely operate as parts of a coherent system. The result is an economy in which academic knowledge struggles to become industrial capability.
Memoranda of understanding and occasional research collaborations cannot resolve this structural problem. What is required is a permanent framework for industry-funded research, university-based innovation centres, technology incubation, and the commercialization of locally developed intellectual property.
The semiconductor sector offers a glimpse of what Bangladesh might achieve, provided its ambitions are matched by institutional preparation. According to BIDA, the country has more than 700 chip designers and recorded semiconductor-related exports exceeding $8m in 2024.
The ambition to increase exports to $1bn by 2030 is significant. But semiconductor development is not simply a matter of producing more designers. It involves specialized infrastructure, advanced research, substantial investment, intellectual property protection, and integration into complex international supply chains.
Bangladesh must recognize the distance between having a small presence in chip design and becoming a meaningful participant in the global semiconductor industry.
Artificial intelligence presents a similar challenge. Developing a Bengali-language large language model may be strategically important, particularly for a country with a large linguistic community. But a national AI ambition cannot be reduced to developing a model or announcing a policy.
It requires reliable datasets, computing capacity, skilled researchers, cybersecurity safeguards and an ecosystem capable of translating applications into productive services. Without these foundations, technological ambitions risk becoming another collection of policy documents with limited practical consequences.
There is also a governance dimension that deserves greater attention. Technological investment depends on confidence in institutions. Investors need predictable regulations, transparent decision-making, effective protection of intellectual property, and a stable policy environment.
Bureaucratic complications and frequent policy changes can undermine long-term investment, particularly in industries where research and product development require years before generating returns.
Public expenditure must also be judged by what it produces. Spending on buildings, equipment, and digital infrastructure is not synonymous with technological progress if these investments do not strengthen research, productivity, and innovation.
The objective should not be to accumulate technology projects, distribute devices, or increase the number of digital services. It should be to develop an economy capable of creating technological solutions to its own problems and competing in international markets.
HM Nazmul Alam is an academic, journalist, and political analyst based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Currently he teaches at IUBAT.

item.title: LDC graduation is deferred by three years. Does it make things better?
item.description:
Last December, I argued in this column that Bangladesh should graduate from least developed country status on schedule in 2026. I argued against deferral for three reasons.
First , it sends a wrong signal to the investors, that even though we passed all the markers for graduation we are not ready to accept it, which means our fundamentals remained weak and the economy was weaker than we had been projecting.
Second , the delay would fix nothing. We would be buying time but time does not fix our woes.
Third , I asked that the debate shifts from when or whether to graduate to preparing for graduation so that we benefit from it.
For me, LDC graduation is a stress test. But the deferral has happened and we now have three years. Does it make things better or worse?
The resolution grants the extension on an exceptional basis, and the graduation framework does not treat a domestic political transition as grounds for one. This was a concession and it is not a precedent.
Attached to it is an obligation to implement a national smooth transition strategy and report progress to the Committee for Development Policy every year. The Committee has also revised its supplementary indicators for the 2027 review to a set of 44, calling the change a shift from once-off measurement to continuous assessment.
We will be judged every year, in public, on a trajectory rather than a snapshot, and no stated ground is left on which to ask for more time.
What is the case for the deferral?
Merchandise exports were $48 billion in FY2025-26, of which readymade garments accounted for $38.70bn, about four-fifths of our export.
The European Union took $19.06bn of those garment exports. Nearly three-quarters of everything we sell abroad moves under duty-free terms we hold only because we are a least developed country, and that share has to find new terms by 2029.
Two things change when that access ends; the tariff is the smaller of them. The first is the rule of origin.
Everything But Arms lets imported fabric made up into garments here qualify as ours, while standard preferences require both the fabric and the garment to be made in Bangladesh.
We import about 60% of our woven fabric, so a large part of the woven trade would fail that test and bear the full tariff whichever scheme we sit under.
The second change is the duty itself, as European Union tariffs on apparel run at about 11.8% at the most-favoured-nation rate and 9.6% under standard preferences, against zero today.
The published estimates of what this costs differ by a factor of three. UNCTAD's Trade Preferences Outlook 2025 puts the annual loss above $17.5bn, a fall of 32%, with 77% of it in the European Union alone.
SANEM puts it near 11% of exports and the UN readiness assessment at between 5.5% and 15%, where UNCTAD's own earlier modelling also sat.
The spread is not a dispute about arithmetic. It turns on whether our garments pay the full tariff or fall back on standard preferences.
Against last year's $48bn, the bill is somewhere between $2.6bn and more than $17bn a year, and we are preparing without knowing which.
Our external position is already resting on remittances rather than on exports. The trade deficit reached $27.28bn in FY2025-26 and the current account closed about $1.6bn in deficit. Record remittances of $35.6bn held reserves at $36.21bn in mid-October. An export loss at the modest end of those estimates lands on that arithmetic, as no second earner can absorb it.
The timing is worse than the amount. External debt stood at $78.22bn in March and 62% of it is concessional. Debt service rises from $4.11bn in FY25 to a projected $7.6bn by FY29, the year the preferences end, and graduation closes the windows that made the debt cheap.
The debt is already about 140% of annual exports, and that ratio worsens from both directions if exports fall while servicing rises at market rates.
Last December, the IMF put our growth near 3.5% with inflation easing. In October, it cut the projection for this year to 3.2%, the weakest since 1988-89, and raised inflation to 10.9%.
The World Bank expects the weakness to persist through FY28, two of the three years we have been given, and private sector credit growth fell to 4.5% in June, a 33-year low.
A diversified export base is built out of investment in laboratories, certification, cold chain, and reliable power, and none of that is financed out of 3.2% growth.
First , the choice is not ours. Graduation follows from meeting the thresholds at two consecutive reviews, and at the 2024 review our income per head stood at $2,684 against a threshold of $1,306, the Human Assets Index at 77.5 against 66, and the vulnerability index at 21.9 where 32 or below qualifies. A government can ask for time, which we have now done, and after that the question is closed.
Second , the preferences are worth less every year even if we keep them, as a margin of preference is only the gap between our duty and our competitors'. Vietnam already sells into the European Union under a trade agreement and India is negotiating one, so that gap narrows on its own.
Third, the preferences shape what we make. They apply to the goods we already produce, so they reward more of the same, and a quarter-century of duty-free access to Europe has left one sector supplying four-fifths of exports. A country off the list negotiates agreements instead of receiving concessions, and an agreement can be written for a product we do not yet sell. The loss above is the price of the transition rather than a permanent cut in what we can earn.
First , the Ministry of Commerce should obtain a written position from the European Commission, before the 2027 review, on whether our apparel qualifies for GSP+ or standard preferences. On Mohiuddin Rubel's reading of the safeguard threshold, it qualifies for neither, and every other decision depends on the answer.
Second , the government should ratify the outstanding conventions required for GSP+ and file the first implementation reports by December 2027, as the scheme rests on a record of enforcement.
Third , the Ministry of Textiles should publish an annual target for domestically produced woven fabric, beginning this fiscal year, as the origin rule applies to the fabric rather than to the duty.
Fourth , it should bring the agreements with Japan and South Korea into force by December 2027 and conclude one more by the end of 2028.
Fifth , the national accreditation board should secure European recognition of its certificates by 2028, as a buyer who will not accept our test report needs no tariff to refuse our goods.
Sixth , the Directorate General of Drug Administration should settle licensing before November 2029 for the fifth to a quarter of locally made medicines patented abroad, as a 4% royalty adds 2% to 3% to the price of a generic.
Seventh , the Ministry of Finance should release the annual progress report at home when it submits it to the Committee, stating the target, the deadline and the responsible ministry for each item above.
Every one of the seven can be completed before November 2029, provided each has a named ministry and a date set against it in writing. Otherwise the three years will pass as the past year has.
Md Rubaiyath Sarwar is Managing Director of Innovision Consulting, a Trustee of Panam Institute.

Minister of the International Department of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee Liu Haixing arrived in Dhaka on Tuesday night on a three-day visit to Bangladesh.

He arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 11pm on Tuesday aboard an Emirates Airlines flight, said Prime Minister's Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony.
BNP Standing Committee Member and Prime Minister's Public Administration Affairs Adviser Ismail Zabiullah, BNP Vice Chairman Air Vice Marshal (Retd) Altaf Hossain Chowdhury and BNP Joint Secretaries General Khairul Kabir Khokon, Syed Emran Saleh Prince, Advocate Abdus Salam Azad and Prime Minister's Protocol Officer Kamrul Islam, among others, welcomed the Chinese delegation at the airport.

Information and Communication Bureau Hu Zhaoming, Deputy Director General-level official of the Bureau of Southeast and South Asian Affairs Li Jinyan, Director of the same bureau Wang Siqi, and Deputy Division Director of the department's General Office and Minister's Assistant Liu Chengxiao.

He will then join a breakfast meeting with Foreign Affairs State Minister Humaiun Kobir at the State Guest House Padma.
