item.title: Sajek grinds to halt as 14-day blockade triggers food shortages
item.description:
Sajek in Rangamati has remained cut off for 14 consecutive days as a road blockade continued on Wednesday, disrupting the supply of essential goods and leaving people facing an increasingly severe food shortage.
The blockade has also left farmers struggling to transport their produce to markets, while hundreds of drivers and their assistants who depend on tourist transport services are being forced to run their households on borrowed money. Many vehicle owners are also worried about repaying loan instalments.
Adding to the uncertainty, the Sajek Gono Odhikar Rakkha Committee has announced a 48-hour blockade on Wednesday and Thursday in protest against the ongoing blockade in Sajek. The programme was announced in a press release signed by the organisation’s member secretary, Bindu Lal Chakma, on Tuesday evening.
The latest announcement has further stalled efforts to bring the administration and protesters to the negotiating table. Although progress had been made towards resolving four of the five demands, no agreement has been reached on the central point of disagreement. As a result, the indefinite road blockade remains in place.
With another round of blockade underway, Sajek’s tourism, transport, trade and local economy are facing severe disruption. Leaders of the two organisations leading the movement have, however, announced some exemptions for the transport of agricultural produce and vehicles carrying teachers and students.
In a joint statement to the media on Tuesday, Sajek Gono Odhikar Rakkha Committee convener Babudhan Chakma and Sajek Karbari Association President Natun Joy Chakma said the decision had been taken at a joint meeting of the two organisations.
They said vehicles transporting locally produced agricultural goods, as well as those carrying teachers and students to schools, colleges and universities, would be exempted from the blockade.
The exemptions would be added to those already announced for emergency services, including ambulances, electricity supply vehicles, vehicles used for religious and wedding ceremonies, and those carrying journalists.
The decision was taken in consideration of the interests of farmers and agricultural traders from both indigenous and Bengali communities in Sajek, they said. However, the indefinite blockade would continue until all five demands of Sajek residents were met.
The Sajek Gono Odhikar Rakkha Committee and Sajek Karbari Association resumed the blockade on Monday after a one-day relaxation on Sunday. On Tuesday, vehicle movement remained virtually suspended after protesters placed tree trunks and lit fires at several points along the Sajek tourist road.
At a meeting between protesters and a government delegation at Ujopara Bazar on October 26, the two sides reportedly reached an understanding on four of the five demands. However, discussions failed to produce a final decision because of disagreement over the demand to remove armed members of the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Samhati Samiti from Sajek.
Although another round of talks was promised, no effective initiative for a fresh meeting has been reported. Protesters have said the blockade will continue until all their demands are met.
Baghaichari Upazila Nirbahi Officer Amena Marjan said no decision had yet been made about holding another meeting. She added that, following instructions from the district administration and in view of security concerns, Sajek Valley tourist destination would remain closed until further notice.
On November 1, protesters had announced a 12-hour relaxation of the blockade to allow residents to collect food and essential supplies. However, a counter-blockade by the Parbatya Chattagram Rakkha Committee and a work stoppage by transport owners and workers prevented normal traffic from resuming that day. Local residents said the relaxation therefore failed to ease public suffering.
Rahul Chakma, organising secretary of the Sajek Resort-Cottage Owners Association, said the tourism-dependent economy had been hit hardest.
With no tourists visiting the area, resorts, cottages, restaurants, transport services, local shops and other tourism-related businesses have become virtually inactive. The blockade has caused estimated financial losses of Tk30-35 crore so far, he said, warning that the losses could rise further if the disruption continues.
Sajek has more than 116 resorts, 14 restaurants and over 100 small and large shops, Rahul said. With tourists staying away for an extended period, business owners, cottage operators and employees are facing severe hardship and losing their investments.
The blockade has also disrupted road links between Sajek, Baghaichari Upazila Headquarters and Khagrachhari. As a result, residents are struggling to obtain essential food items such as rice and lentils and face uncertainty when travelling for emergencies.
Anitya Tripura, a member of Ward 2 of Sajek Union Parishad, said residents had nearly exhausted their household stocks of food and essential goods. Five shops in Ruilui Para had also run out of essential items, he said, warning that the situation could become more serious if the blockade continued.
Jaupeithang Tripura, headman of Shialdai Mouza and a union parishad member, said local jhum farmers and small traders were unable to take their produce to market because tourists were absent and roads remained blocked. This had brought the rural economy to a virtual standstill, while shortages of medicines and other essential goods were also emerging.
Officer-in-Charge of Sajek police station Tofozzal Hossain said large vehicles were not operating on the roads because of the blockade. Only a few auto-rickshaws and motorcycles were moving occasionally. The situation remained calm, and no major untoward incident had been reported so far, he added.
Protesters have reiterated that they will continue the movement until their demands are met.
The latest blockade began on October 22, following calls by the Sajek Gono Odhikar Rakkha Committee and Sajek Karbari Association. It is the third round of blockades called by the two organisations. Citing security concerns, the Rangamati Zila Parishad temporarily closed the Sajek tourist destination, prompting visitors to leave the area.
Tourism activities had first come to a halt after a continuous blockade beginning on October 11. The programme was relaxed from October 16 to 21 for Durga Puja, but vehicle movement was suspended again from October 22. Repeated blockades and temporary relaxations have failed to produce a permanent resolution.
Sajek Union Parishad Chairman Atulal Chakma said that the administration was working to resolve the crisis, but no satisfactory solution had yet been reached.
Khagrachhari Transport Owners Association president Ayus Chakma said the association had 250 registered vehicles, while the Jeep Owners Association had more than 500. In addition, over 1,500 vehicles, including Mahindra vehicles, Chander Gari, and CNG-run auto-rickshaws, operated in Sajek.
The blockade has cut off the income of drivers and their assistants, while owners who bought vehicles with loans are struggling to pay instalments. The transport sector is suffering estimated daily losses of Tk30-40 lakh across the district, he said.

item.title: Police vehicle set on fire as clashes leave at least 50 injured in Savar
item.description:
At least 50 people, including police personnel, garment workers and passersby, were injured in clashes between workers and police in Savar on Wednesday morning over demands for a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
The clashes broke out in the Padma Mor area of Hemayetpur around 8:15am and later spread to Ulail, where confrontations took place in front of the Al-Muslim Group factory around 9am.
During the violence, workers threw bricks and stones at police, who responded with tear gas shells, sound grenades and rubber bullets. A police vehicle belonging to the officer-in-charge of Savar Model Police Station was also set on fire.
The injured included OC Saiful Alam, who sustained serious injuries, according to Dhaka District Superintendent of Police Shamima Parveen. The injured received initial medical treatment.
According to police and local sources, workers gathered near Padma Mor in the morning to press for their wage demands. Tensions escalated when police attempted to clear the road after workers occupied it.
The workers later split into several groups and took positions at different locations, including Padma Mor and Hemayetpur bus stand.
Around 9:10am, protesters blocked the Dhaka-Aricha highway, halting traffic in both directions and causing severe congestion.
Industrial Police said workers threw bricks and stones at law enforcement personnel, prompting police to fire tear gas shells to bring the situation under control. A tense atmosphere prevailed in and around Padma Mor.
In Ulail, police also fired tear gas shells and rubber bullets after workers blocked the road and threw bricks and stones during a confrontation.
Shamima Parveen said between 30,000 and 40,000 workers had gathered from both directions in the Padma Mor area in the morning and attacked police. Law enforcement personnel took measures to resist the assault, she said, adding that the protesters set fire to the vehicle belonging to the Savar Model police station OC.
Separately, several garment factories in Hemayetpur, Ulail and nearby areas declared a general holiday amid the unrest. Some workers later returned home peacefully.
Three platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel were deployed in Savar and Ashulia to strengthen security in the industrial zone.
Savar Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) said around 9:30am that workers had occupied the road and the administration was taking steps to restore normal traffic movement.
Lieutenant Colonel Taimun, commander of the BGB Dhaka Battalion deployed in the area, said around three platoons had been stationed at different locations in Savar and Ashulia.
He said BGB personnel were working to disperse people involved in creating disorder and causing public hardship. He also claimed that many of those involved were not actual workers, but people creating unrest.

item.title: Recognizing our reality
item.description:
While state statistics do suggest a modest 6% growth driven by exports rising for our apparel sector, we must listen to key industry voices marking the reality behind these figures which state that export numbers are misleading.
When factored against soaring production expenses, Bangladesh’s primary export engine could actually be experiencing net negative growth, and this reality cannot be swept under the rug.
To be sure, there is a genuine bright spot: Remittance inflows. Overseas workers sent home $11.465 billion during the July-October period, representing a robust 13% year-on-year surge. This steady inflow from our expatriate workforce once again has offered vital support to our macro-stability.
However, while we can never be thankful enough for the work our expat workers do for the economy, relying on remittances to prop up an economy is an unsustainable strategy, and we need better solutions.
Above all, we must stop taking comfort in superficial statistical milestones and acknowledge our reality, that the economy remains grim: Overall GDP growth has stalled, private sector credit growth languishes at historic lows, and millions of workers remain trapped in a relentless real-wage crisis.
This is the time for our government to work towards genuine national recovery. From restoring liquidity and credit flow to private enterprises to taming persistent inflationary pressures and rebuilding investor confidence, we remain far from solving these issues, and yet they are what must be solved.
Cautious optimism may be warranted, but complacency is fatal. Sustaining export growth is important and necessary, but more important is recognizing where we stand. We must move past short-term statistical relief and focus relentlessly on comprehensive, structural economic revival.

Workers from several garment factories gathered near Hemayetpur bus stand around 9am and occupied the highway, bringing traffic to a halt.

The workers said the rising cost of living had made it increasingly difficult to support their families on the current monthly minimum wage of Tk12,500. They are demanding that the minimum wage be raised to Tk30,000, alongside an end to the blacklisting of workers and arbitrary layoffs.

item.description:
The Dhaka Elevated Expressway will remain toll-free for six hours on Saturday, marking National Revolution and Solidarity Day. All vehicles will be allowed to use the expressway free of charge from 6:00am to 12pm.
The Bangladesh Bridge Authority announced the decision in a press release on Tuesday.
According to the press release, the toll-free facility will apply to all vehicles using the expressway during the designated six-hour period.
Last year, the expressway was kept toll-free for four hours on December 25, when BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman returned home from London after nearly 17 years. The BNP organised a public reception to mark his return.
The expressway also operated without toll collection for several days after toll plazas were damaged during the July Mass Uprising.
Built under a public-private partnership (PPP), the Dhaka Elevated Expressway was partially opened to traffic in September 2023. Currently, the operational section stretches from Kawla, near Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, to the FDC intersection in the capital. Vehicles are normally charged tolls for using the expressway.
Toll rates vary by vehicle category. Cars, taxis, sports utility vehicles (SUVs), microbuses with fewer than 16 seats and light trucks weighing less than three tonnes are charged Tk80.
Medium trucks with up to six wheels are charged Tk320, while trucks with more than six wheels pay Tk400. Buses with 16 or more seats are charged Tk160.
Rickshaws, motorcycles and auto-rickshaws are not allowed on the expressway.
The 19.73-kilometre expressway is designed to connect Kawla, near Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, with Kutubkhali near Jatrabari on the Dhaka-Chittagong Highway, passing through Tejgaon, Moghbazar and Kamalapur along the railway corridor.
However, construction of the full route is yet to be completed.
The project comprises two components: the main construction work and associated works.
The main construction component has an estimated cost of Tk8,940 crore, of which the government is contributing Tk2,413 crore, with the remaining amount being financed by the investor consortium.
A separate project covers land acquisition, rehabilitation of affected people and consultancy services, with its entire cost borne by the government. The estimated cost of this component is Tk4,917 crore.
The combined estimated cost of the two projects stands at Tk13,857 crore.
The project was initiated in 2009, and the construction agreement was signed in 2011. The construction period was initially set at three and a half years, but the project could not be completed within the stipulated timeframe.

item.title: Dengue: 6 more die, 2,010 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Six more people died from dengue across the country in the 24 hours until 8:00am on Tuesday, while 2,010 new patients were hospitalised with the mosquito-borne disease.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) confirmed the figures in a press release issued on Tuesday.
Of the newly hospitalised patients, 943 were in Dhaka Division, 245 in Chittagong, 235 in Khulna, 219 each in Rajshahi and Barisal, 65 in Rangpur, 60 in Mymensingh and 24 in Sylhet.
Since the beginning of this year, a total of 140,909 people have been admitted to hospitals with dengue across the country, according to the DGHS.
Of them, 134,594 have recovered and been discharged, while 5,876 patients are currently receiving treatment at hospitals.
The dengue death toll this year has reached 439.

item.title: Exhibition marking Jail Killing Day postponed over security concerns
item.description:
The Liberation War Museum has postponed a special exhibition commemorating the four national leaders at the request of law enforcement agencies on Tuesday.
Mofidul Hoque, a trustee of the museum, said the decision to postpone the event was taken on Tuesday, following a request from law enforcement agencies citing security concerns.
The exhibition was scheduled to be inaugurated at 4pm on Tuesday at Gallery 6 on the museum's sixth floor. Waliul Islam, a former secretary who served in the wartime government, was scheduled to speak at the opening ceremony.
According to the invitation, the exhibition was organised to commemorate the contributions of the four national leaders, who played a significant role in the country's independence struggle and the Liberation War.
On November 3, 1975, the four leaders – Syed Nazrul Islam, acting president of the wartime Mujibnagar government; Tajuddin Ahmad, the country’s first prime minister; and cabinet members Captain M Mansur Ali and AHM Qamaruzzaman – who led Bangladesh's Liberation War, were killed inside Dhaka Central Jail.
The 15-day exhibition, titled “The Four National Leaders in the Independence Struggle,” was scheduled to run from November 3 to 17.
Officer-in-Charge of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station Monirul Islam told Dhaka Tribune that intelligence information had raised security concerns surrounding the event.
“After informing the organisers about the matter, they cancelled the programme,” he said.

item.title: World Bank: Bangladesh has two more decades to harness demographic dividend
item.description:
Bangladesh has roughly two decades before its working-age population share peaks in 2045, offering a crucial but temporary window to turn rapid demographic shifts into economic opportunity, according to a new World Bank report Tuesday.
While Bangladesh has more time than most of its regional peers, structural obstacles urgently require action, warns the report, titled Demographic Change in South Asia: From Tailwinds to Headwinds for Development .
Across South Asia, the working-age population numbering 1.17 billion people will peak and begin shrinking in less than 10 years.
By 2049, South Asia is projected to become an aged regional economy, with 14 percent of its population aged 65 and older. Bangladesh is expected to hit aged status in 2051.
Since 2000, an expanding share of prime-age adult workers has added 0.4% annually to South Asia's GDP and boosted labor productivity by 1.1% per year.
However, the region's demographic transition from an aging to an aged population is moving faster—and at lower per capita income levels—than in comparable emerging and developing economies.
As a result, the annual contribution of demographics to GDP growth is projected to shrink to just 0.1% between now and 2050.
“South Asian economies are aging faster and earlier in their development journeys,” said Johannes Zutt, World Bank vice president for South Asia.
“They need to act now to adopt policies and build infrastructure that create more and better jobs and deepen the gains from their ‘youth dividend’, while at the same time preparing for aging. This will enable South Asia to make the most of its large working age population and lay the foundations for a ‘second dividend’ as healthier older people continue contributing to the economy.”
The report highlights a persistent jobs gap in Bangladesh, where a favorable age structure has not fully translated into higher employment or productivity gains.
This shortfall is driven by limited formal job creation, low female labor-force participation, and lingering human capital gaps.
Approximately 84% of Bangladeshi workers—around 58 million people—are informally employed.
Higher education offers little guarantee of formal work, with 44% of university graduates holding informal jobs.
Furthermore, formal firms are expanding employment slowly, while small enterprises have, on average, shed workers recently.
“Bangladesh’s demographic opportunity depends on what it does now: help firms create better jobs, equip young people with market-relevant skills, and remove barriers that keep women out of work,” said Jean Pesme, World Bank division director for Bangladesh and Bhutan.
“At the same time, the country needs to start strengthening healthcare and old age income security for an aging population. That means meeting the growing financing need for aging transition will require stronger domestic resource mobilization.”
Systems for healthcare, long-term care, and pensions across South Asia remain poorly equipped for a population living longer without necessarily living healthier.
Currently, only 17% of the region's working-age population contributes to a pension scheme, and just 10% of older South Asians receive pension benefits—the lowest coverage rate worldwide.
To navigate this transition, the report recommends a dual strategy: sustaining the primary "youth dividend" by boosting job productivity, expanding MSME access to finance, streamlining regulations, enhancing education and health systems, and promoting female employment; and unlocking a "second dividend" through expanded healthcare, long-term care, pension safety nets, and increased national savings to raise long-term productivity.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,263 as 6 die in 24hrs
item.description:
Six more children died with measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours ending at 8am on Tuesday, bringing the country’s combined tally of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 1,263 this year.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) classified the latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths.
With this, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,158, while confirmed deaths have remained the same at 105.
A total of 1,318 new suspected measles cases were reported during the 24-hour period, taking the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 232,823.
Meanwhile, 82 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, pushing laboratory-confirmed infections to 24,073.
Since March 15 this year, a total of 207,428 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalised across the country, of whom 198,752 have recovered, according to the DGHS.

item.title: HRFB expresses concern over sedition case against Satkhira rights activist
item.description:
Human Rights Forum Bangladesh (HRFB) has expressed deep concern over the filing of a sedition case against Shampa Goswami, executive director of Prerona Women Development Organisation in Satkhira, and fears that she may face further harassment and security risks.
According to information received from reliable sources, a case was filed against Shampa under Section 124A of the Bangladesh Penal Code at Shyamnagar police station in Satkhira on September 29, 2026.
Shampa has alleged that police surveillance is being conducted at her residence and her organisation’s office, while her family members are also being harassed.
In a statement, HRFB said allegations of this nature require particular consideration of the fundamental rights and privacy protections guaranteed by the Constitution of Bangladesh.
It noted that Article 36 of the Constitution guarantees citizens the right to freedom of movement, while Article 43 protects the privacy of the home and correspondence.
The organisation said allegations of surveillance at an individual's residence and workplace, as well as harassment of family members, must be treated with due seriousness.
HRFB also stressed that specific allegations are essential when bringing serious criminal charges, such as sedition, against individuals involved in human rights activities.
The forum called on the relevant authorities to examine the legal basis of the case against Shampa and verify the allegations, while also conducting an impartial investigation into the complaints she has raised.
It further urged the authorities to ensure that Shampa can continue her peaceful and legitimate human rights activities, including participating in international forums.
HRFB also called for appropriate measures to protect Shampa, her family members, and the staff and volunteers of the women's development organisation from intimidation, harassment or retaliatory action.
The statement was signed by Tahmina Rahman, convener of Human Rights Forum Bangladesh and executive director of Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK).

item.title: Workshop calls for evidence-based approach to tackling corruption
item.description:
A two-day national workshop on strengthening evidence-based approaches to measuring corruption and improving accountability in Bangladesh concluded at the Six Seasons Hotel in Gulshan-2, Dhaka, on Tuesday.
Titled “Measuring Corruption for Reform: Strengthening Evidence and Accountability in Bangladesh,” the workshop was jointly organised by the U4 Anti-Corruption Resource Centre, its partner embassies of Switzerland, Norway, the UK, Denmark and Germany, and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).
The workshop brought together government officials, development partners, academics, civil society representatives and international partners to strengthen Bangladesh’s capacity to monitor corruption trends and assess the impact of reform initiatives.
Over the two days, participants discussed international best practices, the operationalisation of the UNODC Statistical Framework to Measure Corruption, and ways to identify gaps, opportunities and priorities for improving corruption measurement and collaboration in Bangladesh.
Around 40 experts from relevant institutions reviewed existing data sources, including household surveys, administrative records and transparency assessments, to help build a comprehensive evidence base for ongoing national reforms.
The opening high-level session was attended by Anti-Corruption Commission Chairman Justice AKM Asaduzzaman as the chief guest.
In his speech, he stressed that sustainable anti-corruption reforms require collective commitment, adding that strong institutions, effective oversight, public participation and a culture of integrity are essential to building a society free from corruption.
Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics Director Md Emdadul Haque, who attended as a special guest, said the BBS remained committed to supporting national efforts to strengthen the evidence base for development and governance reforms within its mandate, and, where necessary, in collaboration with relevant institutions.
Swiss Ambassador to Bangladesh Reto Renggli said addressing corruption requires a collective shift in attitudes and mindsets, beginning in kindergartens and classrooms.
“Following rules is one thing, believing in the rules is a social precondition,” he said.
Norwegian Ambassador to Bangladesh Håkon Arald Gulbrandsen said Bangladesh would be among the first countries to implement the UNODC Statistical Framework to Measure Corruption if the initiative moves forward, describing it as a positive and practical step that would attract international attention.
UN Resident Coordinator a.i. Max Tunon underscored the strategic importance of measuring corruption and assessing the effectiveness of anti-corruption efforts for good governance, sustainable development and public trust in institutions.
He reaffirmed the UN system’s commitment to implementing the United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC) and relevant resolutions of the Conference of the States Parties, particularly those related to corruption measurement.
He also stressed the importance of strengthening evidence-based public policies through the adoption of the UNODC statistical framework to demonstrate the actual impact of anti-corruption efforts in Bangladesh.
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) Executive Director Iftekharuzzaman highlighted the need to strengthen institutional capacity to generate credible corruption-related data.
“The problem in Bangladesh is often not so much the generation of data, as the lack of interest and commitment to use the available data and knowledge that already exist on corruption,” he said.
He also called for exploring innovative approaches to measuring the comparative implications of the multi-trillion-dollar global money-laundering economy for source and host economies.
Dr Sofie Schuette, principal adviser at the U4 Anti-Corruption Resource Centre at the Chr Michelsen Institute, and Shah Mohammad Naheeaan, head of office at UNODC, also attended the high-level session.
Schuette stressed the importance of data in driving reforms, saying credible evidence could help Bangladesh translate anti-corruption commitments into meaningful change by guiding reforms, strengthening accountability and making progress measurable.
The workshop concluded on Tuesday with panel reflections from representatives of key oversight bodies and development partners on establishing sustainable accountability mechanisms.

item.title: Clashes erupt in Mirpur for third consecutive day
item.description:
Clashes between police and garment workers erupted in Mirpur for the third consecutive day on Tuesday, disrupting traffic and prompting the temporary closure of Mirpur-11 metro station.
The clashes began around 10:15am when police intervened to prevent workers from blocking the road in the Mirpur-11 area, eyewitnesses said.
Workers intermittently emerged from side streets and hurled bricks and stones at police, who responded by firing tear gas shells and sound grenades to disperse them. The confrontation triggered repeated chases and counter-chases, leaving the area tense and traffic at a standstill.
Earlier in the morning, garment workers had left their factories and gathered outside their workplaces, with groups assembling along nearby side streets.
Yusuf Ahmed, a local resident and eyewitness, told Bangla Tribune that male and female workers from several factories between Mirpur-10 and Mirpur-11 had gathered outside their workplaces.
“Looking at the situation, it seems they could take to the main road at any moment,” he said.
Police remained on high alert as the situation developed.
Hafizur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Mirpur police station, said the situation in Mirpur-10 was normal.
“We remain on high alert, and any attempt to cause disorder will be met with strict action,” he said.
Garment workers have been protesting for some time, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. The protests turned violent on Sunday, when workers set fire to a police vehicle and clashed with law enforcement personnel.
Workers attempted to take to the streets again on Monday but were prevented from doing so by police.
According to a police source, around six people were arrested on Monday in connection with the unrest. Eleven cases have been filed over the clashes of the past two days, with more than 10,000 people named as accused.

item.title: Workers block Dhaka-Tangail highway, set fire to roadside waste in Gazipur
item.description:
Garment workers blocked the Dhaka-Tangail highway in Gazipur’s Naojor area on Tuesday, setting fire to roadside waste and bringing traffic to a standstill.
The blockade began around 9:30am in front of Diganta Sweater factory.
Workers dragged accumulated rubbish and waste from the roadside onto the highway and set it on fire, disrupting traffic between Joydebpur Chourasta and Naojor intersection.
Protesters also obstructed all vehicles, including auto-rickshaws and motorcycles. Some were seen playing cricket on the highway.
Journalists at the scene faced resistance from protesters when they attempted to speak to the workers and collect information, photographs and video footage.
Earlier in the morning, Mohammad Amjad Hossain, superintendent of Gazipur Industrial Police, said a group of workers had attempted to block the Dhaka-Tangail highway in the Mouchak area of Kaliakair shortly before 8am.
Law enforcement personnel intervened and persuaded the workers to clear the road without confrontation, he said, adding that security forces remained on high alert at several points along the highway.

item.title: BGB deployment in Gazipur increased to 11 platoons, magistrates to 25
item.description:
The administration has strengthened security in Gazipur amid ongoing garment workers’ protests over wage increases and other demands, deploying an additional platoon of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel and increasing the number of executive magistrates.
The district now has 11 BGB platoons on duty, up from 10, while the number of executive magistrates has risen from 21 to 25.
Arif Hossain, assistant commissioner (media) at the Gazipur deputy commissioner’s office, confirmed the development on Tuesday morning.
He said BGB personnel were operating under the supervision of 25 executive magistrates, while other law enforcement agencies remained on high alert.
The additional deployment aims to prevent damage to public property and protect the lives and belongings of residents, he added.
Meanwhile, workers attempted to block the Dhaka-Tangail highway in Gazipur’s Mouchak area around 8:30am on Tuesday, but law enforcement personnel prevented them from occupying the road. Groups of workers were also seen heading to factories to join their shifts.
Mohammad Amjad Hossain, superintendent of Gazipur Industrial Police, said workers had attempted to block the highway shortly before 8am. Law enforcement personnel dispersed them, and traffic subsequently returned to normal.
For the past few days, garment workers in different parts of Gazipur have been staging protests over wage increases and other demands, blocking the Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways.
The unrest has involved incidents of arson, including fires at a police box, a police vehicle and a factory scrap warehouse. Clashes between workers and law enforcement personnel have also left people injured on both sides, while several individuals have been detained.
Several factories have suspended operations amid the protests.

item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called for ensuring that young people’s innovative ideas are not left unrealised because of a lack of funding.
“A single innovative idea from you could prove to be a game-changer for Bangladesh,” he said, adding that the government had allocated Tk500 crore annually for startups in the current budget.
He made the remarks while addressing the inauguration of a two-day Solar Expo as the chief guest on Tuesday morning at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Exhibition Centre in Agargaon, Dhaka.
The exhibition, themed “Utilize every inch of your rooftop and increase income through solar energy,” opened to visitors immediately after the inaugural ceremony. The prime minister also toured various stalls.
Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud presided over the event.
The prime minister said Bangladesh had previously become heavily dependent on imported energy, leaving the country vulnerable to disruptions in global supply chains caused by international conflicts.
To help stabilize the country's energy and power supply, the government had provided Tk43,000 crore in subsidies to the power sector in the 2025-26 fiscal year, he said.
He added that electricity demand remained at a similar level in the current fiscal year and that the government had increased its diesel reserves. Initiatives had also been taken to ensure adequate coal supplies for coal-fired power plants, while efforts to engage alternative suppliers were continuing.
The government had allocated Tk600 crore to procure fuel oil for electricity generation, he said.
Rather than spending time debating the failures or roles of previous governments in energy security and power generation, the government's priority was to meet future electricity demand and ensure an uninterrupted supply for households and businesses, he added.
He said the government was pursuing several initiatives simultaneously, including reviewing power-sector expenditure and contracts, intensifying domestic gas exploration, diversifying energy sources and rapidly expanding solar power generation.

item.title: Fresh clashes erupt as garment worker protests continue in Ashulia

Although police dispersed the protesters using tear gas and charges, workers later regrouped in nearby alleyways.
Sources said several factory authorities had been forced to suspend operations amid the unrest, but the exact number of affected factories was not immediately known.

item.title: E-immigration launched at Shahjalal airport arrival counters, easing passenger hassle
item.description:
An automated border control system, or e-gate, has been introduced at the arrival counters of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka, allowing e-passport holders to complete immigration in just 18 to 20 seconds and avoid long queues.
The introduction of e-gates at the arrivals section has eased passenger hassle and significantly reduced the time required for immigration, officials said.
Speaking to Dhaka Tribune on Monday afternoon, Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP) Director General Major General Md Alimul Amin said e-gates had been introduced at the airport’s arrival counters and passengers could now complete immigration within a very short time.
“We also want to introduce e-gate services at departures. We are working on it,” he said.
However, he said the departure service was not yet technically ready. Although passengers’ passports can be scanned at the departure e-gates, the system cannot currently complete the required stamping process, leaving the service suspended.
During a visit to the airport, a Dhaka Tribune correspondent found that passengers still have to collect their arrival stickers manually from a police booth after completing e-immigration.
Officials said the process would be simplified once the third terminal becomes operational, and passengers would no longer have to visit the police booth separately to collect their arrival stickers.
Airport immigration officials said Bangladesh faces several technical and operational challenges in fully digitising immigration services, including e-gates and e-visa verification.
These challenges include an insufficient number of e-gates and barcode and biometric reader devices, frequent server downtime and delays in IT systems.
There is also no real-time integration among the databases of the National Identity Card (NID) system, the Department of Immigration and Passports (DIP) and the Bureau of Manpower, Employment and Training (BMET).
As a result, even minor discrepancies in passengers’ names or dates of birth can prevent e-gates from automatically identifying them.
Technical problems with facial-recognition cameras and fingerprint-matching systems can also cause the gates to reject legitimate passengers. In addition, some immigration officials lack the technical expertise needed to operate digital systems and verify e-visas.
Major General Alimul Amin said several technical, institutional and practical challenges remain in converting departure immigration into a fully digital system.
“That is why the service is currently suspended. But we are working to simplify this service, as well as passport-related services, as soon as possible,” he said.
Passengers said the introduction of e-gates at arrivals had reduced both waiting time and hassle, allowing them to complete immigration automatically within 18 to 20 seconds.
Liton Kabir, who recently returned from Thailand, told Dhaka Tribune: “The e-passport was once a dream for the people of Bangladesh. The e-gate was introduced alongside it. Although the service was closed for various reasons, I feel relieved now that it has reopened. If it is introduced at departures soon, travelling will become even easier.”
Rajib Ahmed, who recently returned from Turkey, said the service had made the arrival process much easier.
“This was our first family tour. With an e-passport, you can clear immigration in about 18 seconds. It would have been great to have the facility at departures too, as it would save a lot of time. The government should pay attention to this,” he said.
An immigration official said passengers using e-gates at departures still have to return to the immigration desk for visa verification and other checks, meaning the process takes almost as long as before.
“This makes passengers angry. Data from the e-gates also often fails to reach the immigration software. That is why the departure e-gates have remained closed,” he said.
He added that while e-gates are currently closed for departing passengers at Shahjalal Airport, they are operational for arriving passengers.
Bangladesh introduced e-passports in February 2020, becoming the first country in South Asia to do so. E-gates were subsequently installed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport to facilitate faster and more efficient immigration processing.
However, technical problems and the continued need for manual visa verification and other checks created complications. As a result, passengers still had to visit immigration desks even after using the e-gates, prompting authorities to suspend their operation.
Several members of the Immigration Police's Special Branch, speaking on condition of anonymity, said around 40% of passengers using the airport each day hold e-passports.
They said the e-gates can automatically verify passport and passenger information but cannot independently verify visas.
The system also lacks provisions to automatically store information on passengers’ destinations or flights.
Consequently, visa verification continues to be conducted manually, even when passengers use the e-gates. This contributes to long queues at departure immigration, particularly when several flights arrive or depart around the same time.
Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport Executive Director Group Captain SM Ragib Samad told Dhaka Tribune that the e-gates can currently verify only passport information and cannot verify visas and other details.
“That is why the e-gates have been kept closed at departures. But we hope the service will start soon,” he said.
The government has taken an initiative to modernise Bangladesh's immigration system by integrating the existing Immigration Management System (IMS) with new technologies.
The Ministry of Home Affairs has formed a 10-member committee to review fee-setting, payment collection and settlement procedures under the system and develop an appropriate financial model.
The notice was issued on October 19 by the Departure-4 branch of the ministry's Security Services Division and published on October 25.
According to the notice, the government plans to integrate the Advance Passenger Information System (APIS), Passenger Name Record (PNR), e-Visa and Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) systems, as well as a sovereign data analytics platform, with the existing IMS.
The government is also considering appointing a third party to modernise the relevant infrastructure and implement the programme. As part of the initiative, the committee will review immigration facilitation charges, revenue collection and remittance procedures, and payment mechanisms. It will also prepare proposals on appropriate fees and a suitable financial model.
The committee is headed by the Joint Secretary of the Planning-1 wing of the Ministry of Home Affairs, while the Deputy Secretary of the Departure-4 branch will serve as its member-secretary.
Other members include the Joint Secretary of the Departure-1 wing of the Home Ministry and representatives from the Finance Division, National Board of Revenue (NBR), Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), Special Branch, Biman Bangladesh Airlines, Bangladesh Land Port Authority and the Department of Immigration and Passports.

item.title: LPG price hiked again, 12kg cylinder now Tk2,060
item.description:
The Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC) has raised liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices by Tk223 per 12kg cylinder, setting the new price at Tk2,060 amid an ongoing supply shortage.
The price was previously Tk1,837. The price of autogas has also increased from Tk84.62 to Tk91.95 per litre.
The revised prices will take effect at 8:00pm on Monday, BERC said.
Prices have been raised across all cylinder sizes, ranging from 5kg to 45kg.
BERC last raised the price of a 12kg LPG cylinder by Tk252 on October 4, from Tk1,585 to Tk1,837. The latest hike comes just a month later, amid ongoing supply shortages and complaints of higher market prices.
On October 29, BERC held a public hearing on LPG prices and proposed increases in storage, bottling and distribution charges. During the hearing, LPG operators, distributors and retailers placed separate proposals for raising their charges.
Operators proposed increasing bottling charges from Tk15–16 to Tk25–30 per kg. They also sought to raise distribution charges from Tk4.17 to Tk8.33 per kg and retail charges from Tk3.75 to Tk10 per kg.
Distributors proposed increasing their charge on each 12kg cylinder from Tk50 to Tk150, while retailers sought to raise theirs from Tk45 to Tk70.
After reviewing the proposals, BERC's technical evaluation committee recommended raising the price of a 12kg cylinder from Tk1,837 to Tk1,976, an increase of Tk139.
Following the hearing, the commission set November 2 as the deadline for submitting opinions on the proposals. It announced the revised prices on the final day for receiving feedback.

item.title: Garment worker protests disrupt operations at 264 factories in Savar, Ashulia
item.description:
At least 264 garment factories in Savar and Ashulia declared general holidays on Monday following clashes between workers and police over demands for a minimum wage increase and other labor-related issues.
Superintendent of Police of Industrial Police-1 Mominul Islam Bhuiyan confirmed the development on Monday afternoon.
For the 3rd consecutive day, garment workers in the industrial areas of Savar and Ashulia took to the streets demanding a Tk30,000 increase in the minimum wage, an end to blacklisting and a halt to worker layoffs.
In the morning, workers blocked the Nabinagar-Chandra Road in the Baroipara area, pressing for the wage increase and 3 other demands. Police later persuaded them to leave the road.
Meanwhile, workers at Newage Garments in the Nischintapur area entered the factory premises and staged a work stoppage. They later gathered in front of Ananta Garments on the Baipail-Abdullahpur Road.
Several factories, including Knit Asia, Al-Muslim, Trouser Line and Ananta Garments, declared general holidays on Monday, as they had on the previous day.
Later, when workers staged a sit-in on the road, police attempted to disperse them. At one point, workers threw bricks and stones at police, triggering clashes and chases between the two sides.
Police fired tear gas shells to disperse the protesters. During the unrest, agitated workers also set fire to a covered van in the Narsinghpur area, further escalating tensions in the industrial zone.
According to police, incidents of brick-throwing and subsequent clashes were reported in front of the factories of Picard Bangladesh Ltd, Artistic Design, Janoron Sweater Ltd, Ferrari Garments Ltd, Denitex Limited, Anlima Textile Limited, Al Islam Textile Limited and GQ Industries.
Police later attempted to bring the situation under control through discussions with workers. Two garment workers were detained during the incidents.
Mominul Islam Bhuiyan said the unrest in the Savar industrial area stemmed from workers' demands.
He said general holidays had been declared at 264 garment factories across the Savar-Ashulia industrial area due to the unrest. Additional police personnel were also deployed in the area to prevent further incidents.

item.title: 10,500 sued in four cases filed over Mirpur workers’ clashes, arson
item.description:
Four cases have been filed over two consecutive days of workers’ protests, clashes, arson and attacks on police in Mirpur, Dhaka.
The cases name about 10,500 unidentified people as accused. So far, 22 people have been arrested. The Detective Branch (DB) of police claims that 11 of them are activists of the Awami League, whose activities have been banned, Jubo League, and Chhatra League.
Law enforcement operations continue in connection with the violence surrounding the workers’ movement demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Officers-in-charge (OCs) of Mirpur Model and Pallabi police stations shared the information on Monday afternoon.
Md Hafizur Rahman, OC of Mirpur Model Police Station, said one case has been filed over vandalism of a traffic box and attacks on police in Mirpur. Three thousand unidentified people have been named as accused in the case. Six people have been arrested so far.
Meanwhile, Jalal Uddin, OC of Pallabi Police Station, said three cases have been filed at Pallabi over arson on a police vehicle, attacks on police, obstruction of government duties, and vandalism of a traffic box. Police are the complainants in these cases.
He said each case names between 2,000 and 2,500 unidentified people as accused. So far, 16 people have been arrested in the three cases.
The DB says local activists of the Awami League had planned to create violence in Mirpur by exploiting the workers’ movement for their just demands. A section of them had organised through online groups. They also had plans for large-scale sabotage under the cover of the movement.
Of those detained in Mirpur, 11 are activists of the Awami League, Jubo League and Chhatra League. They are not local garment workers. According to the DB’s claim, they came from various districts and gathered in Mirpur.
Meanwhile, at around 10:45am on Monday, workers tried to take to the road through an alley in the Senpara Parbata area of Mirpur-10. Police dispersed them and also fired several tear gas shells.
Later, workers also tried to take to the road at Proshika Intersection beside the Mirpur-2 Stadium. Police moved them away from there as well.
Eyewitnesses said workers were coming in scattered groups from the Rupnagar area, passing by the Mirpur-2 Stadium towards Proshika Intersection. When they tried to get onto the road, police obstructed them at around 11am. Tension arose between police and workers.
After two consecutive days of garment workers’ protests and clashes in Mirpur, police and other law enforcement personnel have been on alert since Monday morning. Police were seen stationed at the Mirpur-10 roundabout and surrounding areas from the morning. Riot-control vehicles, water cannons and other vehicles have been kept ready at the roundabout.
However, traffic on the roads at Mirpur-10 and surrounding areas is normal on Monday. No disruption was seen on the roads.
On Monday morning, after a meeting at the secretariat with representatives of owners on the recent situation in the garment industry, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, responding to journalists’ questions, said some industrialists and a few individuals operating under the banner of workers’ organisations are involved in creating unrest in the garment sector. Video footage, audio and other evidence of these individuals’ activities have been collected. Some people were brought under the law on Sunday as well.
He said strict action would be taken if anyone tried to worsen the law and order situation in the name of the workers’ movement.
On Sunday, garment factory workers blocked the road and demonstrated at the Mirpur-10 intersection in the capital, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Around 8am that day, workers from several garment factories took position on the road, disrupting traffic in the surrounding areas.
Clashes between workers and police began at around 11:15am. According to eyewitnesses, police used batons, water cannons, sound grenades and tear gas shells to disperse the workers. The workers then also hurled bricks and stones at police from various directions.
Chases and counter-chases between the two sides continued until 11:45am. At one point around midday, a police vehicle was set on fire beneath the Mirpur-11 metro station.
Because of the clashes, the Mirpur-10, Mirpur-11 and Pallabi metro stations were closed from 11:38am to 1:58pm.
The day before, on Saturday, garment workers had also blocked roads in Mirpur over the same demand. That day, from 10:30am to 1pm, traffic came to a standstill in Mirpur-10, 11 and 12 and surrounding areas.

item.title: Govt targets 3,000-4,000MW of solar power ahead of next summer
item.description:
The government aims to generate 3,000-4,000 megawatts of electricity from solar power ahead of next summer to help keep power shortages at a manageable level, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit said on Monday.
As part of the initiative, the government is promoting rooftop solar systems at public universities, considering them a relatively simple and effective way to expand renewable energy generation.
Speaking at a consultation meeting on installing solar power systems at 31 public universities, organized by the University Grants Commission (UGC) in Agargaon, Dhaka.
The state minister Amit said the government was working to prevent a repeat of the electricity-related hardship experienced by consumers during the current summer.
A solar power policy was formulated within two months to accelerate the expansion of solar energy, he said, adding that it could be revised based on feedback from relevant stakeholders.
The state minister emphasized that the initiative would not be imposed on universities. Decisions would instead be made based on each institution’s needs, capacity and practical circumstances, with support from the government and the UGC.
Amit said the expansion of rooftop solar power could help universities reduce carbon emissions and create opportunities to earn carbon credits.
The Power Division would support universities in obtaining carbon credits in recognition of their emissions reductions, he added.
One carbon credit generally represents the reduction or removal of one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent. Credits may be sold after completing the required verification and certification processes.
The state minister also announced that the Bangladesh Solar Expo would be held in Dhaka on November 3-4 to promote the use of solar energy.
A separate expert meeting involving university vice-chancellors is also planned to discuss solar installations at public universities. He urged all vice-chancellors to participate.
Presiding over the meeting, UGC Chairman Professor Dr Mamun Ahmed said the consultation was organized to address confusion surrounding rooftop solar installations and gather feedback from relevant stakeholders.
The commission has already conducted a survey and formed a team to assess the feasibility of installing solar systems at its own premises and at different public universities, he said.
The UGC would provide technical assistance to universities, but no decision would be imposed on them, he added.
Mamun stressed the importance of adopting the operating expenditure (OPEX) model, under which a service provider typically finances, installs and operates a solar power system while the institution pays under an agreed contractual arrangement.
A significant portion of universities’ operating budgets goes towards electricity and gas bills, he said, adding that wider use of solar power could substantially reduce these expenses.
Referring to an initiative at Jashore University of Science and Technology (JUST), the UGC chairman said a solar power system was being pursued through a tripartite agreement under the OPEX model.
Similar arrangements could be introduced at other universities, he added.
The UGC chairman urged universities to incorporate carbon credit opportunities into their solar power plans from the outset.
He said institutions should establish mechanisms to measure the amount of carbon emissions avoided through solar power generation, which would be essential to pursuing carbon credits.
The UGC would also provide vice-chancellors with necessary guidelines, draft agreements and relevant information on installing solar systems, Mamun said.
Universities could begin implementation within a month if they took the initiative immediately, he added.
At the meeting, Professor Dr M Shamsul Alam, dean of Daffodil International University, and Tahmilur Rahman, senior assistant secretary at the Power Division, presented separate papers on rooftop solar installations at university buildings and the expansion of solar power under the OPEX model.
Among those present were Power Division Secretary Mirana Mahrook, UGC member Professor Dr Masuma Habib, JUST Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Iarul Kabir, Bangladesh University Council president and BUET Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr SM Abdur Razzak, Rajshahi University Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Md Faridul Islam, Hajee Mohammad Danesh Science and Technology University Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr M Enamullah, and UGC Secretary Dr Md Fakhrul Islam.
Other UGC members, senior officials and vice-chancellors of the 31 public universities also attended the meeting.

item.title: Cabinet clears draft law to expedite solar power installations
item.description:
The Cabinet on Monday gave approval – both in principle and final – to the draft Special Solar Power Installation Act, 2026, aimed at expediting the expansion of solar power installations across the country.
The approval came at the cabinet meeting held at the Bangladesh Secretariat with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in the chair.
The draft law was placed to turn the Special Solar Power Ordinance, 2026, already promulgated, into an act.
“The draft law was placed before the cabinet meeting for the approval. The cabinet cleared it subject to vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division,” Cabinet Secretary Dr Nasimul Ghani said while briefing reporters after the meeting.
He said the Special Solar Power Ordinance, 2026, was promulgated under Article 93(1) of the Constitution to expedite the expansion of special solar power installation activities.
Explaining the rationale for the draft law, Nasimul Ghani said an ordinance promulgated under Article 93(1) of the Constitution must be placed before parliament at its first meeting following the promulgation, as stipulated in Article 93(2).
Following the cabinet's approval, the draft law will be placed before parliament as a bill.
Once passed by parliament and assented to by the president, it will turn into an act.
The Cabinet Secretary said the proposed law would undergo parliamentary debate, during which changes could be made if necessary.

item.title: Cabinet approves draft Public Procurement (2nd Amendment) Act, 2026
item.description:
The cabinet on Monday gave approval to the draft of the Public Procurement (Second Amendment) Act, 2026, aiming to ensure greater transparency, accountability, equal treatment and open competition in government procurement.
The approval – both in principle and final – came at the 26th cabinet meeting of the current government, chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Bangladesh Secretariat.
Cabinet Secretary Dr Nasimul Ghani briefed reporters after the meeting.
The Public Procurement Act, 2006, which serves as the principal legal framework for government procurement, has so far been amended six times.
The latest amendment was made through the Public Procurement (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, promulgated on September 21, 2026.
The ordinance was issued to introduce updated provisions aimed at protecting local industries and creating greater competition in procurement activities.
The proposed amendment includes special provisions for new, micro and small, women and disadvantaged bidders to ensure their participation in government procurement.
It also seeks to modernize the procedures under the open tendering method and expand the application of the limited tendering method to ensure a more equitable distribution of resources.
The draft law also aims to clarify provisions relating to professional misconduct and introduce alternative procurement arrangements to meet urgent state requirements.
The draft of the Public Procurement (Second Amendment) Act, 2026, was published on the websites of the Bangladesh Public Procurement Authority (BPPA) and the Implementation Monitoring and Evaluation Division (IMED) for public opinion.
An ordinance promulgated under Article 93(1) of the Constitution must be placed before Parliament at its first meeting following the promulgation, as stipulated in Article 93(2).
The cabinet gave final approval to the draft law, subject to vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division.

item.title: COP31: Bangladesh to highlight climate resilience, seek grants
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Monday said Bangladesh will urge developed countries to provide climate finance in the form of grants rather than loans and take responsibility for their contribution to global carbon emissions at the upcoming COP31, scheduled to be held in Antalya, Turkey, from November 9 to 20.
Talking to reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, she said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman would make a brief visit to attend the two-day high-level sessions of the conference.
COP is the annual UN Climate Summit, officially known as the Conference of the Parties.
The prime minister will participate in the World Leaders’ Summit, scheduled for November 11-12, a senior official told UNB.
“The prime minister's visit will be formally announced at a press conference, as we do ahead of every foreign visit. You will know the details then,” Shama said.
She said Bangladesh would highlight its achievements in climate resilience and its experience in addressing the impacts of climate change across South Asia and the wider Asian region.
At the same time, Bangladesh would highlight the support it needs to tackle future climate challenges, particularly the need to ensure that climate finance is provided as grants rather than loans, she said.
The state minister stressed the need for major carbon-emitting countries to take responsibility and ensure accountability during climate negotiations.
“Although Bangladesh's contribution to global carbon emissions is almost negligible, we are ultimately among those suffering the consequences,” she said.
Shama said the government would also showcase the initiatives taken by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman over the past six months to address climate change and improve the environment.
These include canal excavation, tree plantation drives, and greater emphasis on solar power and renewable energy, which directly contribute to tackling climate change, she said.
An inter-ministerial coordination meeting chaired by State Minister Shama was held last month to review Bangladesh's preparations for the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31).
The meeting reviewed various aspects of the preparations, including the Prime Minister's participation in the high-level segment of COP31.
Bangladesh's priorities and concerns at COP31 were discussed at the meeting, which also reviewed possible bilateral meetings and seminars to be held on the sidelines at Bangladesh's pavilions in the Blue and Green Zones, an official told UNB.
Asked about the latest developments regarding execution of two Bangladeshis in Saudi Arabia, Shama said the Bangladesh mission in the Kingdom has been maintaining regular communication with the relevant authorities.
“Communication with Saudi Arabia through our mission is continuing. We hope to receive some information from them soon. The process is underway. We hope to hear something from the Saudi government shortly,” she said.

item.title: Experts call for subsidies to promote organic fertilizers
item.description:
Experts and policymakers have called for government subsidies to promote the production and use of organic fertilizers, citing concerns over declining soil fertility, food nutrition and the sustainability of agriculture in Bangladesh.
Despite achieving self-sufficiency in food production, Bangladesh continues to face nutritional challenges, ranking 84th among 122 countries in the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2026. Meanwhile, prolonged dependence on chemical fertilizers has contributed to declining soil fertility, raising concerns about the long-term sustainability of agricultural production.
The call was made at a roundtable titled “Subsidizing and Promoting Organic Fertilizer for Healthy Soil, Crops and Environment” at the CIRDAP Auditorium in Dhaka on Monday.
ActionAid Bangladesh and the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute (BARI), in collaboration with 20 national and international development organizations and 5 universities, jointly organized the event.
Agricultural experts, government officials, development organizations, farmers and organic fertilizer entrepreneurs discussed barriers to production, registration, marketing and use, along with ways to facilitate access to government subsidies.
Speakers highlighted administrative complications in registering organic fertilizer products and gaps in quality assessment and monitoring mechanisms. While acknowledging that organic fertilizers may produce lower yields than chemical alternatives in some cases, they stressed their importance in maintaining soil health and improving crop quality.
They also called for balanced fertilizer use based on soil conditions and crop requirements.
Dr Md Abdus Salam, executive chairman of the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council (BARC), attended the first technical session as the chief guest. He discussed the existing registration process for entrepreneurs and invited recommendations to simplify it.
Mosammat Sabira Sultana, MP and member of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on the Ministry of Agriculture, attended the event as a special guest.
“Just as keeping a mother healthy help ensure the birth of a healthy child, maintaining soil health makes it possible to produce nutritious crops,” she said.
She stressed the importance of quality assurance, effective marketing and identifying genuine farmers under the Farmer Card initiative.
Sultana urged participants to prepare specific proposals and an action plan for the balanced use of organic and chemical fertilizers. She pledged to raise the recommendations with the parliamentary standing committee, parliament and the prime minister.
Anwar Faruque, director of Bangladesh Krishi Bank, attended the second technical session as the chief guest and proposed introducing a district-level registration system for organic fertilizer entrepreneurs.
“There is no alternative to natural methods if we are to make agriculture sustainable,” he said, emphasizing balanced fertilizer use and the need to provide farmers with accurate, science-based information.
Farah Kabir, country director of ActionAid Bangladesh, called for coordinated efforts to strengthen quality control, address marketing irregularities and reduce administrative barriers. She also expressed the organization's willingness to work with the government on necessary policy reforms.
The second session was chaired by Professor Dr Abdul Karim of the International University of Business, Agriculture and Technology (IUBAT).
Dr M Nazim Uddin of BARI and Professor Dr Md Mizanur Rahman of Gazipur Agricultural University presented research papers during the 2 sessions.
The discussions are expected to inform the development of a policy framework for subsidies, simpler registration procedures and stronger quality assurance mechanisms for organic fertilizers.

item.title: Crude bomb explodes beneath Agargaon metro station
item.description:
A crude bomb exploded beneath the Agargaon metro rail station in the capital on Monday night.
Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Monirul Islam told Dhaka Tribune that police rushed to the scene after receiving reports of the explosion shortly after 8:30pm.
“Upon reaching the spot, we found that miscreants had detonated a cocktail bomb and fled,” he said.
He added that police were examining CCTV footage from nearby areas to identify those responsible for the explosion.

item.title: Bangladesh, UK express satisfaction over bilateral ties as Kobir meets Miliband
item.description:
Acting Foreign Minister Humaiun Kobir met with UK Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs Ed Miliband on Monday on the sidelines of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in St John's, Antigua and Barbuda.
During the meeting, both ministers expressed satisfaction over the growing bilateral relations between Bangladesh and the UK, marked by robust exports of Bangladeshi goods to the UK market and British investment in Bangladesh.
They also discussed Bangladesh's agreement to purchase Airbus aircraft for its national flag carrier, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The two ministers agreed to extend reciprocal support in multilateral forums on various issues, including climate change, safe, orderly and regular migration, and humanitarian assistance.
The UK Foreign Secretary thanked Bangladesh for hosting around one million forcibly displaced Myanmar nationals (FDMNs) and assured continued British humanitarian support for the Rohingyas.
During the meeting, the Acting Foreign Minister also conveyed an invitation from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to his British counterpart to visit Bangladesh at a mutually convenient time.
