Democrats, Trump hold final rallies before midterm elections
item.description:
Democrats teed up final get-out-the-vote rallies Monday on the eve of midterm elections where they expect to win at least partial control of Congress and impose political constraints on President Donald Trump for the first time in two years.
Rallies -- including by star Democratic Senate candidates James Talarico in Texas and Adam Hamilton in Kansas -- were capping a campaign of breathtaking tension and bitterness.
For his closing argument, Trump chose a speech in Washington at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool -- a landmark that has become synonymous with the 80-year-old president’s obsessive, controversial drive to redevelop the US capital.
“We’re going to win,” he said on Sunday.
Polls, however, show that Democrats are near certain to take the majority from Republicans in the House of Representatives and have a real shot at winning the currently Republican Senate.
Even winning just the House would mean Democrats have voting power over the federal budget and would lead powerful committees able to investigate alleged corruption under Trump, the Epstein files and other explosive issues.
The loss of total Republican dominance would push Trump into unfamiliar and uncomfortable territory: a lame-duck period beset with high inflation at home, the sputtering war against Iran and hostile Democratic investigations into his activities in Washington.
But a decade into the Trump era, Democrats remain wary about predictions of victory.
“Nauseously optimistic,” Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock told CNN to describe the mood.
Democrats are facing late internal divisions, with left-wing candidates clashing at times with the party’s establishment.
In a startling display of infighting on Sunday, Democratic congresswoman Haley Stevens in Michigan endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers against left-wing progressive candidate Abdul El-Sayed in her state’s key Senate race.
Trump was quick to praise Stevens for her “bravery,” posting on his Truth Social platform that “Haley said what few people are willing to say.”
Stevens, who lost a bruising primary to El-Sayed in August despite being backed by the Democratic establishment, struggled to explain her decision in an interview with CNN.
“It’s just where I was at the end of the night and earlier this morning,” she said.
Trump’s Republicans have fought a political scorched-earth campaign, painting Democrats as communists and openly branding El-Sayed, who is Muslim, as a terrorist.
Addressing a crowd in Iowa on Sunday, Trump said Democrats are “extreme and dangerous radicals” who will “steal your wealth” and let in migrants to “ransack, rape and plunder.”
But polls show Americans heavily souring on Trump’s wrecking-ball act.
An NBC News poll released on Sunday showed 60 percent disapprove of his performance, particularly over high prices exacerbated by his now eight-month-long war against Iran.
While the House seems highly likely to turn Democratic, the battle for the Senate is up in the air.
Only a third of the Senate’s 100 seats are being contested in these midterms, and few of the races were seen as favorable to Democrats.
However, with surprisingly strong challenges in deeply Republican states, pollsters now say the odds of a Democratic flip are at minimum even.
The final New York Times/Siena poll released Sunday evening showed Democratic candidates leading in all seven seats viewed as most competitive, though five remained within the margin of error.
A Democratic Senate would be able to shut down Trump’s lifetime appointments to courts -- including the Supreme Court.
While Tuesday is election day, early voting has already seen a record 54 million people cast ballots around the country.
The midterms have seen about $11 billion spent on advertising, with large chunks coming from individual mega-donors.
Elon Musk, a close Trump ally who led the so-called DOGE effort in dismantling entire government departments, has given a staggering nearly half-billion dollars to help get Republicans elected.

item.title: Police detain several over unrest in Savar, Ashulia
item.description:
Police have detained several people from different areas of Savar and Ashulia over allegations of vandalism, attacks on garment factories and attempts to create unrest amid ongoing workers’ protests, Dhaka District Police Superintendent Shamima Pervin said on Monday.
However, she could not immediately confirm the number of people detained, saying arrests had been made separately by industrial police and police from Ashulia and Savar police stations.
Speaking to journalists in front of a factory in Jamgora on the Ashulia-Baipail road in the afternoon, Shamima said those accused of trying to vandalise vehicles, attack garment factories, injure workers and hurl brickbats had been detained.
She said police teams were still conducting operations and that the total number of arrests would be confirmed after information from different units was compiled in the evening.
Dhaka Range Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Md Mostafizur Rahman, who was also present during the visit, said the police would take strict legal action against those creating instability in the industrial belt and those backing them.
He said the government had formed a wage board for garment workers on Sunday and that it had already started its work to address wage-related concerns through the legal process.
“Those who are creating instability despite the formation of the wage board are not, in our view, part of the workers’ movement. They are people creating disorder in society, and strict legal action will be taken against them,” he said.
The DIG urged workers to return to their jobs without fear and called on factory owners to resume normal operations, assuring them that police would ensure security at factories.
He said police were collecting information about those allegedly instigating the unrest from behind the scenes, adding that no one would be allowed to act outside the law. Those involved in vandalism and arson at factories and other locations were being identified, and cases and arrests were underway, he added.
Addressing rumours that a worker had been killed by police gunfire, Mostafizur said no such incident had occurred and accused a group of spreading misinformation on social media to destabilise the country and mislead workers.
He urged journalists to report verified information, saying false claims could create confusion among workers and the public. He also warned that legal action would be taken against anyone spreading misleading information or inciting unrest, including labour leaders or others providing financial support.
The DIG said police had been monitoring several social media groups for the past four days, alleging that they were circulating provocative messages announcing demonstrations at specific locations for the following day.
He also expressed concern over the safety of students during the unrest, saying a student was injured by bricks thrown by protesters while trying to flee near a school at the Bangladesh Krira Shikkha Protishthan (BKSP) on Monday.
Mostafizur said a large number of police personnel had been deployed across the industrial belt, including uniformed and plainclothes officers, members of the Armed Police Battalion (APBn) and the RRF.
He said workers in some factories had initially entered their workplaces before gradually stopping work. After general leave was declared at the factories, they took to the streets to protest.

item.title: Home minister holds meeting with garment owners to resolve workers' unrest
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Monday held a meeting at the Secretariat with leaders of garment factory owners as part of the government's efforts to resolve the ongoing unrest in the readymade garment (RMG) sector and restore normalcy in industrial areas.
The meeting was convened following Sunday's violent demonstrations by garment workers in Dhaka, Gazipur, Savar, Ashulia and Tangail, where protesters demanded a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
The government has taken initiatives to address the situation through dialogue with industry stakeholders while maintaining law and order and ensuring the uninterrupted operation of the country's vital export-oriented garment sector.
During Sunday's demonstrations, several areas witnessed clashes between protesters and law enforcement personnel, road blockades and incidents of vandalism targeting factories and vehicles.
Meanwhile, police arrested 19 leaders and activists of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations, including the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League and Jubo League, in Dhaka on allegations of instigating the demonstrations.
The government has also formed a six-member minimum wage board to review the existing salary structure of garment workers, with representation from workers, employers, the government and an independent member.
At present, the minimum monthly wage for garment workers stands at Tk12,500. Workers are demanding Tk30,000, citing rising living costs, including house rent, food, transportation and healthcare expenses.
The government has called upon workers to return to their workplaces and pursue their demands through dialogue and peaceful negotiations, rather than resorting to violence, vandalism and road blockades.
The BGMEA has expressed concern that prolonged unrest could disrupt production, delay export shipments and affect Bangladesh's commitments to international buyers.

item.title: Police disperse garment workers after fresh clashes in Mirpur
item.description:
Clashes broke out between garment workers and police again in the capital’s Mirpur area on Monday morning, as police moved to disperse workers attempting to gather on the roads.
At around 9:15am, police chased away workers who had taken positions on the road. As of the latest reports, confrontations between the two sides were continuing.
Hafizur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Mirpur police station, confirmed the incident, saying: “The workers came to block the road, and we dispersed them.”
Earlier on Sunday, garment workers clashed with police during protests demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
On Monday morning, when workers attempted to gather again in the Mirpur-10 area, police intervened, triggering a series of chases and counter-chases. Workers threw bricks and stones at police, who responded by firing tear gas shells.
The workers were subsequently dispersed, but tension remained high across the area. Most shops remained closed, while police restricted people from gathering on the streets and questioned individuals they considered suspicious.

item.title: Garment workers block Dhaka-Tangail highway again, traffic halted
item.description:
Garment workers blocked the Dhaka-Tangail highway in Gazipur again on Monday, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000 and bringing traffic to a standstill.
The blockade began around 8:30am, when workers from several factories gathered on the highway in the Palli Bidyut area.
Mohammad Amjad Hossain, superintendent of Gazipur Industrial Police, said around 1,000 workers occupied the highway at the time, halting traffic in both directions.
He said Industrial Police and other law enforcement agencies were working to bring the situation under control and restore traffic movement.
On Sunday, workers staged protests in Konabari, Safipur, Palli Bidyut and surrounding industrial areas, demanding the same wage increase.
Workers and police clashed intermittently, escalating tensions at several locations. Protesters also set fire to a police box and vandalized several vehicles.
The unrest disrupted traffic on the Dhaka-Tangail highway for around six hours on Sunday.

item.title: 10 BGB platoons deployed in Gazipur, 21 magistrates assigned
item.description:
Ten platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have been deployed in Gazipur to maintain law and order amid ongoing garment workers’ protests demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. They are being assisted by 21 executive magistrates.
Arif Hossain, assistant commissioner of the Media and Research Cell at the Gazipur deputy commissioner’s office, confirmed the deployment in a message sent to the “Media Cell DC of Gazipur” group at 8:26am on Monday.
Sources at the deputy commissioner’s office and Industrial Police said Industrial Police, district police, BGB personnel and executive magistrates were working together to keep the situation under control.
Amjad Hossain, superintendent of Gazipur Industrial Police, said around 1,500 workers gathered in the Palli Bidyut area along the Dhaka-Tangail highway at around 8:30am on Monday, bringing traffic to a standstill.
BGB personnel, Industrial Police and other law enforcement agencies have been deployed in Chandra, Palli Bidyut, Safipur, Konabari and Mouchak to manage the situation and restore traffic movement, he added.
Garment workers in Gazipur have been protesting for the past two days, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Thousands of workers have occupied the highway at different points, halting traffic and causing severe inconvenience to long-distance bus passengers and other commuters.
The protests initially involved road blockades in Mouchak, Safipur and the Chandra-Palli Bidyut areas of Kaliakair, bringing traffic on the Dhaka-Tangail highway to a complete halt.
During the unrest, gates of several factories in the Palli Bidyut area of Kaliakair were vandalized. A police box was also vandalized in Mouchak, another was set on fire beneath the Konabari flyover, and a pickup van was torched in front of the Ansar Academy.
The unrest later spread to nearby industrial areas, including Ratanpur, Konabari and Kashimpur. Operations at around 30 factories in these areas were suspended amid the protests.

item.title: Clashes break out between garment workers, police in Ashulia
item.description:
Clashes broke out between garment workers and police in Ashulia, Savar, on Monday, prompting police to fire several rounds of tear gas shells to disperse the protesters.
No casualties were immediately reported. Following the clashes, workers and police remained in a standoff.
The incident occurred after 10am in the Narsinghapur and Nishchintapur areas along the Abdullahpur-Baipail road. Most factories along the road declared a general holiday amid the unrest.
According to witnesses, workers initially gathered in front of a factory owned by Ananta Group before moving to a Hamim Group factory, where they allegedly threw bricks.
Tensions escalated when the workers attempted to block the road to press home their demands, triggering a confrontation with law enforcement personnel and subsequent clashes.
Police fired several rounds of tear gas shells in an effort to disperse the workers and bring the situation under control.
Shoeb Ahmed, additional superintendent of police (operations and intelligence) at Industrial Police-1, said police were working to restore order.
A tense situation prevailed in the area at the time of filing this report, with additional police personnel deployed to maintain law and order.

item.title: Gold prices rise by Tk3,194 per bhori after two days
item.description:
The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus) has raised gold prices in the domestic market, just two days after announcing a reduction, citing an increase in the price of pure gold in the local market.
The new rates came into effect at 10am on Monday. Under the revised prices, 22-carat hallmarked gold costs Tk18,935 per gram, or Tk220,786 per bhori (11.664 grams), including VAT.
The decision was taken at a meeting of the Bajus Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring on Monday morning, chaired by its chairman, Dr Dewan Aminul Islam Shahin.
According to the new price list, 21-carat gold costs Tk18,085 per gram, or Tk210,871 per bhori. The price of 18-carat gold has been set at Tk15,535 per gram, or Tk181,128 per bhori.
Gold made using traditional methods now costs Tk12,690 per gram, or Tk147,932 per bhori.
On Saturday, Bajus reduced the price of 22-carat gold by Tk5,481 per bhori, bringing it to Tk217,592, including VAT. The revised rate also took effect at 10am that day.
With Monday’s increase, the price of 22-carat gold has risen by Tk3,194 per bhori from the previous rate.
Bajus has also announced new prices for silver ornaments. The price of 22-carat silver has been set at Tk300 per gram, including VAT. The rates for 21-carat and 18-carat silver are Tk290 and Tk250 per gram, respectively, while silver made using traditional methods costs Tk190 per gram.
Bajus said making charges would depend on the design and craftsmanship of the jewellery. As VAT is included in the fixed retail prices, it cannot be charged separately.
For exchanges of old gold jewellery, 12% of the value must be deducted, excluding making charges and the cost of stones. For the purchase of old jewellery, the deduction will be 18%. VAT cannot be deducted separately in either transaction.
The revised prices will remain in effect at jewellery shops across the country until further notice.

Petrobangla: Fire at Inani gas well may take 15 days to control
item.description:
It may take up to 15 days for the fire triggered by a gas blowout at a deep well in Chhota Inani of Cox's Bazar to subside, Petrobangla has said.
The fire broke out on October 27 when gas erupted from underground during drilling operations at a depth of around 1,000 feet near Chhota Inani Bridge in Jaliapalong Union of Ukhiya Upazila.
According to a Petrobangla press release issued on Sunday, two geologists from the Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company Limited (BAPEX) have been sent to monitor the situation. They are currently stationed in Cox's Bazar to oversee developments.
On the advice of experts, the gas is being allowed to escape freely to prevent the fire from spreading. The intensity of the blaze is expected to gradually decline over the next 15 days.
If the gas flow does not decrease within this period, the expert team will take alternative measures, including firefighting operations and steps to stop the flow, the release said.
As a precautionary measure, public access within a 100-metre radius of the well has been prohibited. Local authorities have also taken necessary steps to maintain law and order.
Petrobangla, BAPEX and the local administration are jointly monitoring the situation round the clock.
Meanwhile, geological and 2D seismic surveys are underway to assess the potential gas reserves in the surrounding area.
Petrobangla has urged people not to panic, remain cautious and cooperate with the authorities.

item.title: Filipino woman injured in Banani gas leak fire dies
item.description:
A 32-year-old Filipino woman who suffered severe burns in a fire caused by a gas leak in the capital’s Banani area has died while undergoing treatment.
Keistin Ver Bunag died at around 3:30am on Tuesday at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery.
She had suffered burns to 63% of her body, while her respiratory tract was also damaged by smoke or hot gases.
Dr Sultan Mahmud Shikdar, a resident surgeon (emergency) at the institute, said Keistin was admitted to its emergency department on October 28 after being referred from Continental Hospital.
According to preliminary information, she sustained the injuries at around 7am that day while attempting to light a gas stove.
Her condition remained critical following admission. Despite receiving treatment and close medical attention, she could not be saved, the doctor said.

item.title: Antonelli becomes youngest Formula One world champion
item.description:
Kimi Antonelli drove the perfect race to finish third in his Mercedes at the Mexico Grand Prix and seal his place in Formula One history as the youngest world champion.
Max Verstappen took the chequered flag but all eyes were on the young Italian who takes the crown at the age of 20 years and 68 days, more than three years younger than Sebastian Vettel in 2010.
He is the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.
"We did it. I wouldn't be here without Mercedes, without my family," said an emotional Antonelli who has won nine races so far this season.
"I am very grateful for this moment, it will be with me forever. I am speechless, just trying to process what happened.
"It's been an incredible season and to share this podium with Max and Lewis (Hamilton) is incredible. I am looking forward to some more battles in the future."
The race broke into two parts as it was suspended after 46 of the 71 laps following a crash involving Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas.
The Finn's suspension on the front left side had collapsed causing his wheel to buckle and making him a helpless passenger as his car flew backwards off the track and slammed into the barriers.
The 37-year-old Bottas was slow to emerge from his car but waved to the crowd as he walked away, with all the other cars returning to the pits to await a restart.
Antonelli, who needed just to finish in the top nine to seal the title, was running third in his Mercedes when the race was stopped behind Red Bull's Verstappen and the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc.
His nearest challenger teammate George Russell was out of the running after suffering a poor start dropping from second on the grid to fifth and struggling with his power.
Russell had to win to have any hope of prolonging the title race.
Lewis Hamilton, who started on pole and also needed to win to push Antonelli, was furious with his Ferrari teammate after an incident at the start that saw Leclerc leave the track and steal the lead. The Monegasque was handed a five-second penalty but he retained track superiority over Hamilton.
That changed on the restart when Hamilton powered past Antonelli and Leclerc and bumped wheels with Verstappen before settling into second.
There was a further yellow flag when the Racing Bull of Arvid Lindblad also crashed out 10 laps from the end after tangling with the McLaren of Oscar Piastri.
Antonelli sat tight in third as Hamilton continued to press Verstappen. It was entirely appropriate that the young Italian, in tears as he crossed the line, was led in by two of the all-time great drivers with 11 championships between them.

item.title: Mbappe strikes after China controversy as Real beat Santander
item.description:
Kylian Mbappe moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander on Sunday.
The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d'Or to Bayern Munich's Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.
Real Madrid's match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout.
Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande were also on target to keep third-place Madrid within three points of leaders Barcelona, who thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday.
Jose Mourinho's side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind city rivals Atletico Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0.
"In the first half we were very strong, we came out to play well," Mourinho told reporters.
"The team is growing, playing well, I think we should have scored even more goals with the chances we had."
Mbappe won a soft penalty as he went down under little pressure from Matteo Prati, smashing it home to put Madrid ahead at the Sardinero stadium in the 11th minute.
It was the 27-year-old's 12th league goal of the season, trailing only Barcelona's Raphinha with 15 in the scoring charts.
Madrid had control of the game and a fine pass from Arda Guler sent Bellingham through on goal for the second.
The England international knocked the ball past the goalkeeper and rolled home for his 50th goal since joining Madrid in 2023.
"Reaching 50 goals with Real Madrid is very special," Bellingham told Real Madrid TV.
"We played very well. It was very important to win after the victory at Camp Nou (against Barca last weekend), so we are very happy."
Guler spurned a good opportunity for the third after being set up by Mbappe, before Madrid's record signing Diomande lashed home from the edge of the box.
The hosts started the second half well, pushing Madrid back, much to the chagrin of Mourinho, who yelled at his players.
Madrid regained their control and racked up several more chances, with Mbappe hitting the post and Bellingham denied by Racing goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala.
Racing won a penalty after Madrid's Aurelien Tchouameni handled in the box, but the award was cancelled after a VAR review.
Bellingham had a second goal ruled out in stoppage time after he strayed offside before finding the net and Endrick bent an effort narrowly wide from distance.
Hosts Racing, 16th, back in La Liga for the first time in 14 seasons, fell to their first home defeat of the campaign.
Earlier Sevilla, sixth, suffered a 3-1 loss at Getafe, who moved into mid-table.
"(Madrid's penalty award) annoys me," Racing coach Jose Alberto told DAZN.
"Evidently we came across a great Madrid, who put us under a lot of pressure in the first half hour, and were much better than us, but what conditions everything was the first goal and the penalty."
Valencia, 19th, beat Elche 1-0 with a well-taken goal from Umar Sadiq to move to within a point of safety after a bad start to the season.
Elsewhere Athletic Bilbao, seventh, edged fifth-place Real Sociedad 2-1 in an entertaining Basque derby clash at San Mames stadium.
Inaki Williams lobbed Athletic ahead early on before Luka Sucic drilled home from the edge of the box to level.
Alex Berenguer controversially restored Athletic's advantage just before half-time from the penalty spot, after Jon Aramburu was adjudged to have fouled Nico Williams, although he appeared to win the ball.
"I think it's incredible that a penalty like that is given when I touched the ball, even Nico said it," complained Aramburu to DAZN.
Spanish World Cup-winning goalkeeper Unai Simon made several fine saves to ensure Los Leones claimed the three points.

Arsenal ride out Liverpool storm to top Premier League
item.description:
Arsenal moved to the top of the Premier League with their first win away to Liverpool in 14 years as Kai Havertz's early strike secured a 1-0 victory for the Gunners.
The defending champions were made to suffer after the German's 16th-minute opener but held out for what could be a telling win in their quest to retain the title.
Arsenal climbed three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the table.
But with City expected to be hit with a severe points penalty, unless they can overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules, Arsenal dealt a huge blow to their most likely rivals for the title.
"It's been such a long time without this feeling here, that we really needed it," said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta. "We are extremely proud of what the team, the players, everybody has done."
Liverpool produced arguably their best spell of Andoni Iraola's early months in charge with a blistering 30 minutes after conceding, but failed to take their chances as the Spaniard suffered just his second defeat in 14 games since arriving from Bournemouth.
Arteta was stinging in his criticism of the Arsenal side that crashed out to fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday in one of the biggest ever League Cup shocks.
The Arsenal boss got the response he desired in a strong start from the champions.
Havertz was one of the biggest culprits for wasting chances in midweek but made amends with a simple finish from Declan Rice's precise low cross.
The early goal lit the touchpaper for a pulsating first 45 minutes as Liverpool roared back.
Iraola and Arteta played together as boys for Basque side Antiguoko Kirol Elkartea.
Arteta's old friend gave his side one of the most uncomfortable afternoons they have experienced in recent seasons as Arsenal's rock-solid defence was left clinging on for half-time.
"I loved the reaction from my players after going 1-0 down," said Iraola. "I loved a lot of moments of the game.
"We have to keep going. It is very early in the season. Arsenal are in the best of the situations but it is just the start of November today."
All of Liverpool's three £100 million-plus ($134 million) forwards started together and there are signs the relationship between Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola is beginning to flourish.
Isak did Arsenal a favour by not going down as he was pulled back by Jurrien Timber when just failing to connect with a wicked delivery from Barcola.
"The Alex one is a clear penalty," added Iraola. "We can all see that he holds the shirt (but) because he doesn't go to the floor, you are not going to call the penalty? I don't understand it."
Wirtz curled a free-kick onto the bar from a narrow angle and Alexis Mac Allister should have buried a header into the goal rather than finding the stand behind David Raya's goal.
Half-time allowed Arsenal the chance to reset and take the wind out of Liverpool's sails as Iraola's men tired in the second period.
Alisson Becker produced a stunning save to turn behind Christos Tzolis's shot that was arrowing into the bottom corner to keep Liverpool in the game.
That intervention counted for little as Arsenal rode out the closing stages to register another clean sheet and an eighth win in nine league games.
Defeat leaves fifth-placed Liverpool nine points adrift of the leaders and already facing a mountain to climb to get back in the title race.

item.title: Bangladesh slip in WTC standings after defeat to West Indies
item.description:
An eight-wicket defeat to West Indies in the opening Test of the two-match series saw Bangladesh slip from fourth to fifth in the World Test Championship (WTC) standings.
Bangladesh started the match with an aim to make a giant leap toward the maiden final appearance in the WTC. But the outside chance of making it final received a massive setback after the defeat, which allowed India to move up to fourth.
Bangladesh's points percentage fell from 55.56 to 47.62 while India currently stands at 51.52 per cent.
The West Indies, meanwhile, improved their points percentage from 20.83 to 26.92 following their victory, although they remain eighth in the table.
They have narrowed the gap on seventh-placed Sri Lanka, who have a points percentage of 33.33.
Chasing a target of 170, the West Indies reached 172-2 in just 35.1 overs on Day 4, frequently interrupted by rain, lightening and bad light.
Brandon King led the run-chase with 81 not out while his fellow opener John Campbell made 49. Kevam Hodge was unbeaten on 31 with King when West Indies sealed the deal with incredible ease.
West Indies captain Roston Chase said the team was targeting an improvement in their position in the WTC standings, a goal achieved showing a superlative performance. "We came here with the aim of improving our rankings by winning two Tests. We want to finish the cycle at least at number six or five on the points table. To achieve that goal, we had to win both these matches," Chase said after the match.
Earlier, Bangladesh were bowled out for 272 in their first innings, with opener Shadman Islam scoring 105. West Indies left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican claimed five wickets.
In reply, the visitors were wrapped up for 245 in the first innings, with John Campbell and Tagenarine Chanderpaul making half-centuries. Justin Greaves scored 46, while Chase added 43. Nayeem Hasan was Bangladesh's leading bowler with 4-33.
A sensational batting collapse saw Bangladesh dismissed for 142 in the second innings, leaving West Indies a modest 170 for victory. Chase was the wrecker-in-chief with 5-33 while Warrican added 4-63 with his five-wicket haul in the first innings.
The West Indies completed the chase comfortably, securing a victory that boosted their WTC campaign and further reshaped the points standings.
Meanwhile, Australia slipped from first to third in the standings following a 176-run defeat to South Africa in Cape Town, while New Zealand climbed to the top of the table.
South Africa moved into second place after the victory, with their points percentage rising to 71.43 from 66.67. New Zealand now lead the standings with 72.22 per cent, while Australia's percentage dropped to 69.23.
Australia, chasing a target of 288 on the final day of the third Test, were bowled out for just 111 before the end of the second session, handing South Africa a comprehensive victory.

item.title: Amite replaces Mominul for final West Indies Test
item.description:
The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) has called up Amite Hasan to their 15-member squad for the second and final Test against the West Indies, replacing the injured Mominul Haque.
The BCB announced the squad in a press release on Saturday, confirming one change from the opening Test which Bangladesh lost by eight wickets after a sensational batting debacle at Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium.
Mominul sustained a head injury on the third day of the first Test while fielding at short leg. He was injured while attempting to take a catch in the 78th over of the West Indies' first innings, with Jaker Ali Anik subsequently coming in as his concussion substitute.
According to the BCB, players who suffer a concussion must remain out of action for at least seven days before returning to the field. As a result, Mominul will miss the second Test, paving the way for Amite's inclusion.
"The concussion rule that states that a player diagnosed with a concussion must observe a mandatory minimum of seven calendar days away from play before returning to the field," the BCB press release stated.
Meanwhile, Jaker Ali has retained his place in the 15-member squad after featuring as Mominul's concussion replacement in the first Test.
The second and final Test of the series is scheduled to begin on November 5 at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium.
Squad:
Najmul Hossain Shanto (Captain), Shadman Islam, Tanzid Hasan Tamim, Tawhid Hridoy, Litton Das, Jaker Ali Anik, Mehidy Hasan Miraz (Vice Captain), Nayeem Hasan, Hasan Mahmud, Taijul Islam, Shoriful Islam, Mushfiqur Rahim, Taskin Ahmed, Ebadot Hossain Chowdhury and Amite Hasan.

item.title: PM sits with ministers over garment sector unrest
item.description:
In the wake of the unrest in the country's garment sector, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has sat in a meeting to address the crisis.
The meeting started at 6pm at the Bangladesh Secretariat with the participation of several ministers and others concerned.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury, State Minister for LGRD and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, PM’s adviser and also PMO Spokesperson Mahdi Amin and Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal chief coordinator and transport leader Shamsur Rahman Shimul Biswas attended the meeting.
Garment workers staged demonstrations and blocked roads in Dhaka and Gazipur on Sunday, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000, disrupting traffic and triggering clashes with police and vandalism.
At least 20 people, including four to five police personnel, were injured in sporadic clashes between police and workers in the capital's Mirpur area as workers took to the streets to press for their demand.

item.title: Precise PetLab marks first anniversary, launches mobile app
item.description:
Precise PetLab Diagnostics & Hospital Ltd., a specialized veterinary hospital in Gulshan, Dhaka, is celebrated its first anniversary Sunday with an event at its premises, where it is also launched a mobile app.
The app will make it easier for pet owners to access the hospital’s services and their pet’s medical records.
The program began with a welcome and introduction of guests, followed by a presentation on the hospital’s facilities and innovations, a guided facility visit, and a feedback session in which guests are invited to share their views and suggestions.
Precise PetLab opened to the public on 25 August 2025 with a clear purpose: to give pet owners timely and accurate diagnosis, dependable emergency support, and treatment guided by established medical standards.
Veterinary healthcare in Bangladesh is still not fully equipped to meet these needs, so the hospital has focused on standardized emergency protocols, advanced diagnostics, and practice aligned with international guidelines.
The anniversary was an occasion to recognize the team behind this progress, introduce the hospital’s facilities to guests, and gather feedback to guide its next phase of growth.
Through the app, owners will be able to book appointments from home, reach the hospital quickly in an emergency, and view their pet’s medical records on their phone.
This will make care easier to access and more continuous from one visit to the next.
For the hospital, it will be a direct way to follow up on patients and hear from clients.
Sadia Zareen Shampa, managing director of Precise PetLab, said: “Through the implementation of our organization’s programs and initiatives, we are committed to ensuring the welfare, health, and protection of all animals across the country, whether stray, domestic, or wild.”
Precise PetLab is Bangladesh’s first 24/7 emergency veterinary hospital with a dedicated emergency unit.
It has remained open for 504 consecutive days up to 30 October, without closing even for a moment.
It is also the only veterinary hospital in the country with a dedicated emergency unit, advanced ICU, automatic ventilation and critical care.
With 15,000 square feet of space and 30 doctors, it is the largest veterinary hospital in Bangladesh.
In its first year, the hospital has served more than 4,000 appointments, attended to 1,364 emergency clients, and performed over 800 surgeries, earning the trust of pet lovers across Dhaka.
As it enters its second year, Precise PetLab remains committed to strengthening its clinical capabilities, developing its people, and raising the standard of pet healthcare in Bangladesh.

item.title: President calls for skills-based training, support for young entrepreneurs
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Sunday called for expanding skills-based training, providing financial support to small entrepreneurs and creating employment opportunities for young people to harness the country's demographic dividend.
He made the call while speaking as the chief guest at the inaugural ceremony of National Youth Day 2026 at Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Dhaka.
The President said youth are the country's most valuable human resource and the key driving force behind national development. "Bangladesh cannot move forward through political change alone," he said.
He said the country must make the best use of its large young population to strengthen its capacity and prepare for graduation from the least developed country (LDC) category, stressing the need to make young people employment-oriented and equip them with productive skills so they can contribute to the national economy.
Referring to the achievements of young entrepreneurs, including women entrepreneurs, he said many are successfully expanding their businesses and exporting products despite having limited capital. The President said the government should provide aspiring entrepreneurs with proper training and minimum financial assistance to help them become self-reliant.
He also called for expanding the programs of Department of Youth Development across the country, particularly its training and loan facilities, so that more young people can benefit.
Mirza Fakhrul emphasised the need to shift towards a need-based education system, saying greater importance should be given to vocational and technical education to meet domestic and international labour market demands.
Bangladesh can earn significantly more foreign currency if it sends skilled workers abroad, he said, adding that technical training institutions should be expanded. Highlighting the potential of biogas, the President said the technology can help rural families, particularly those involved in livestock farming, produce energy from animal waste and reduce pressure on the country's energy supply.
He also expressed concern over the growing drug addiction among young people, calling for effective measures to address the problem.
Unemployment and frustration, Mirza Fakhrul said, are among the factors contributing to drug addiction, making it necessary to create employment opportunities and raise awareness.
He urged young people to stand against violence against women, dowry and all forms of discrimination, calling for community-based organisations and movements to resist such social problems.
The President also stressed ensuring equal opportunities for young women in education, employment, entrepreneurship and leadership.
Referring to the country's political transition, he said the opportunities created through the establishment of a democratic system should be utilised for national development.
The President urged the youth never to give up and remain committed to building a self-reliant, skilled, technology-oriented and humane Bangladesh. "Never give up. We will continue our struggle and move forward," he said.

item.title: 6,000-tonne fertilizer warehouse opened in Dhaka
item.description:
Agriculture, Fisheries and Livestock Minister Mohammad Amin Ur Rashid on Sunday inaugurated a newly built 6,000-tonne fertilizer warehouse at the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) campus in Gabtoli, Dhaka.
The prefabricated steel warehouse was constructed under a BADC project to expand fertilizer storage capacity, said a press release.
BADC Chairman Md Azizul Islam presided over the inauguration ceremony, attended by Agriculture Secretary Md Selim Khan, ministry officials, BADC representatives, and fertilizer dealers.
Speaking at the event, the agriculture minister said BADC plays a vital role in ensuring farmers receive fertilizer and other agricultural inputs at fair prices and on time.
Stressing that storing fertilizer was not enough, he said ensuring its timely delivery to farmers must be the priority. Delays in supplying essential agricultural inputs could disrupt crop production, he added.
He directed officials to strengthen the entire supply chain, from storage and transportation to distribution, and ensure regular monitoring of fertilizer stocks. He also called for digitalization of inventory management and distribution systems.
The agriculture minister said more warehouses would be built in different parts of the country, including the northern region, in line with the prime minister's directives to increase storage capacity.
He further stressed the need for advance planning based on farmers' actual demand and warned against creating artificial shortages of agricultural inputs.
Saying agricultural development was key to national progress, he noted that the government was prioritizing farmers through timely fertilizer supplies, canal re-excavation, and tree-planting initiatives.
He urged BADC officials and employees to work with sincerity and accountability to ensure farmers receive fertilizer, seeds, and other essential inputs on time.

item.title: Sajek blockade partially lifted, counter-blockade disrupts traffic
item.description:
An indefinite blockade on the Khagrachhari-Sajek road in Rangamati was partially relaxed yesterday by two UPDF-backed organisations, while another group enforced a counter-blockade, disrupting traffic movement.
On the 11th day of the blockade, light vehicles were seen operating between Baghaihat Bazar and the Sajek tourist spot, allowing residents to buy essential commodities.
However, no vehicles were seen travelling to Sajek from Dighinala and Baghaichhari in Khagrachhari.
The Sajek Gono Odhikar Rakkha Committee and Sajek Karbari Association, backed by the United People's Democratic Front (UPDF), have enforced the blockade since October 22.
Citing humanitarian considerations, the two organizations announced a temporary relaxation of the blockade from morning until evening on Sunday.
However, the Parbatya Chittagong Rakkha Committee rejected the announcement and called a counter-blockade on the road.
Meanwhile, transport owners and workers announced a temporary suspension of vehicle operations.
Protesters blocked vehicles heading towards Sajek from Khagrachhari, Baghaichhari and Langadu from Sunday morning. They obstructed several points along the road by placing tree trunks and burning tyres, causing further suffering for commuters.
The two organizations had called the blockade demanding the removal of members of the Parbatya Chattagram Jana Samhati Samiti (PCJSS) from the area.
They announced that the blockade would resume on Monday after the temporary relaxation ends on Sunday.

item.title: Ex-ambassador’s wife murdered, son sent to jail
item.description:
The son of a former Bangladesh ambassador to the Philippines has been sent to jail in a murder case filed over the death of his mother, Afia Akter, while their house help, Nargis Begum, has given a statement before a Dhaka court as a witness.
The accused, Tahsin Tarik Arnab, and Nargis were produced before the court on Sunday by the investigation officer, Dhanmondi Model police station Sub-Inspector Mohammad Touhidur Rahman.
The investigation officer filed an application seeking to keep Arnab in jail custody and another seeking to record Nargis’s confessional statement as a witness.
Following the applications, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid ordered that Arnab be sent to jail. Another Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahbub Alam, recorded Nargis’s statement, said Sub-Inspector Sharifuzzaman of the prosecution department.
While at the court, Arnab told journalists that he was a Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) student at United International University (UIU).
He said he found his mother lying in the dining room in a bloodied condition early in the morning.
“There is a mosque downstairs in our building. I called the imam. I called 999, but they did not respond,” he said.
Arnab said he later spotted a police patrol vehicle while on his way to Dhanmondi Ibn Sina Diagnostic Centre and informed its personnel about the incident. The police then accompanied him to the house.
Claiming that he was ill, Arnab said his mother was a heart patient and also had diabetes.
Afia Akter, wife of the late Abul Kashem, a former Bangladesh ambassador to the Philippines, was found murdered at a flat on Road 9/A in Dhanmondi.
Her daughter, physician Nahrin Nashid Swarna, filed a murder case accusing her younger brother, Arnab.
In the case statement, Swarna alleged that Arnab was not involved in any work or occupation and frequently asked their mother for money. Whenever she refused, he would quarrel with her and threaten to kill her.
According to the case statement, at around 6:30am on Saturday, the house manager, Mahbub, called Swarna and informed her that he had learned from the building's security guard about a disturbance at their house.
Swarna immediately called the house help, Nargis. Nargis told her that Arnab had stabbed Afia Akter in the throat with a knife and left her lying in the dining room.
Swarna then asked Mahbub to take her mother to the hospital immediately. Afia Akter was taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where the on-duty doctor declared her dead.
Later, after speaking with Nargis, Swarna learned that her mother had dinner at around 9:30pm on Friday before going to sleep in her bedroom. Arnab was in his own bedroom at the time.
According to the case statement, Nargis heard Afia Akter scream at around 5:30am and went to the dining room. She saw Arnab standing with a knife in his hand, while Afia Akter was lying in a bloodied condition.
When Nargis tried to approach Afia Akter, Arnab threatened to kill her while showing her the knife. He then forced Nargis out of the house and locked the door.
After confirming his mother's death, Arnab left the house.
Police said Arnab was arrested from the Dhanmondi area after the case was filed.

Tahsif's female friend placed on 4-day remand in murder case
item.description:
A Dhaka court has placed a female friend of former Air Force official Tahsif Souri on a four-day police remand in a murder case filed over his death.
Inspector Md Firoz Uddin, the investigation officer of the case filed with Uttara East Police Station, sought a seven-day remand to question her.
Following the hearing, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ripon Hossain granted a four-day remand.
In the remand petition, the investigation officer said she was suspected of being involved in the incident.
State prosecutor Shamsuddoha Sumon argued in favour of the remand, saying investigators needed to cross-check her statements against information provided by another accused, Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip, who is already on remand.
He sought the maximum remand period in the interest of a proper investigation.
Defence lawyer Imam Hossain Javed opposed the remand and sought bail, arguing that she had no involvement in the killing.
He said Dip was the main accused named in the case and that Tahsif Souri’s female friend had been arrested solely on the basis of CCTV footage. According to the lawyer, Souri had dropped her off at her home in his car around midnight that night, after which they had no further contact.
He added that the two had gone to a restaurant for a meal because of their relationship, and that she knew nothing beyond that.
Tahsif's female friend was arrested from the Kafrul area around 2am on Sunday.
Earlier, on Saturday, another accused in the case, Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip, described as a younger friend of Souri, was placed on a four-day remand for questioning.
Souri’s father, KM Enayetul Karim, filed the murder case with Uttarkhan Police Station on Friday night after his son’s body was recovered.
Souri, who came into the spotlight as the person who recorded the video of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina leaving the country, was found floating in the Turag River near Rajabari Ghat on Wednesday afternoon. Naval police recovered his body.
He had left his home on his motorcycle on Tuesday evening after Dip called him downstairs.
Dip told reporters on Thursday that he had parted ways with Souri in the Uttara House Building area after they had dinner together at a restaurant.
That night, the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) took Dip into custody for questioning from his home on Babar Road in Mohammadpur.
Based on information provided by Dip, investigators recovered Souri’s motorcycle on Friday morning.
Dip also admitted to going with Souri to the area, which is known as a drug hotspot, late that night. PBI officials later took him to the area on Friday as part of the investigation.

item.title: Pakistani High Commissioner meets Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad
item.description:
Pakistani High Commissioner to Bangladesh Imran Haider paid a courtesy call on Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad at the latter’s office in the city on Sunday.
During the meeting at the National Parliament, the speaker thanked the government of Pakistan for supporting Barrister Jahrat Adib Chowdhury, chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Bangladesh Parliament, as a member of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) Executive Committee at the 153rd IPU Assembly held in Tanzania.
Both sides emphasized the importance of forming the parliamentary friendship group between Bangladesh and Pakistan and exchanging visits by parliamentary delegations.
They also exchanged views on providing training to officials and employees of the Bangladesh Parliament Secretariat at Pakistan's legislature, Majlis-e-Shoora.
The speaker invited the Pakistani high commissioner to observe the upcoming session of the Bangladesh Parliament, which will begin on November 09.
Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad, Bir Bikram, will visit Pakistan on November 23 at the invitation of the Speaker of Pakistan Parliament, according to a press release.
Representatives of the Pakistan High Commission, the Secretary of the Bangladesh Parliament Secretariat and other senior officials concerned were present at the meeting.

item.title: Garment workers block Dhaka-Tangail highway, set police box on fire
item.description:
Garment workers blocked the Dhaka-Tangail highway in Gazipur on Sunday, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000, bringing traffic to a standstill. Five platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) were deployed to help control the situation.
A police box in Konabari was also set on fire during the unrest.
Workers began gathering on the highway shortly after 8am and blocked the road by 9:30am, disrupting traffic along the busy route.
Chanting slogans demanding higher wages, workers occupied several points along the highway, including Safipur Bazar, Chandra Polli Bidyut, Mouchak and Telichala in Kaliakair upazila.
Hundreds of workers, some carrying sticks, took positions at different points, halting traffic and causing significant hardship for passengers.
Workers from several factories, including Karani Knit Composite and Knit Asia in the Ratanpur area of Kaliakair, joined the protest instead of continuing their work.
They had initially entered their factories in the morning to mark their attendance before leaving the premises to join the demonstration near Safipur Bazar.
Several nearby factories suspended operations amid the unrest.
Iftekhar Hossain, officer-in-charge of Konabari police station under Gazipur Metropolitan Police, said protesters had set fire to a police box located in the middle of the Dhaka-Tangail highway in the Konabari area.
Shahidul Islam, officer-in-charge of Kaliakair police station, confirmed that traffic remained suspended as workers continued occupying the highway and demonstrating since Sunday morning.

item.title: Tahsif’s death: Police claim preliminary evidence against Dip
item.description:
Police have reportedly found preliminary evidence linking Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip to the death of his friend, former Bangladesh Air Force officer KM Tahsif Souri, who is suspected to have been murdered.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Hasib Ullah Pias on Saturday placed Dip on a four-day remand in a case filed over Tahsif’s death, said Additional Public Prosecutor Muhammad Shamsud Doha Sumon.
Police had sought seven days of remand, citing preliminary findings in their petition.
“We have found preliminary evidence of Dip’s involvement in Tahsif Souri’s death. We will question him in greater detail during remand. We cannot disclose anything further at this stage in the interest of the investigation,” Abdullah Al Mamun, superintendent of police (Dhaka region) of the River Police, told The Daily Star.
A police official involved in the investigation, speaking on condition of anonymity, said CCTV footage collected from different locations showed Dip accompanying Tahsif between 6:30pm and 1:30am.
Investigators also found that Dip had accompanied Tahsif to the Mazar Basti area in Tongi but returned alone, the official said.
“This has raised questions among the investigators,” the official added, saying information obtained during preliminary questioning also pointed to Dip’s involvement.
The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) picked up Dip from his residence on Babar Road in Mohammadpur late Thursday night. He was later shown arrested in the case filed by Tahsif’s father, KM Enayetul Karim, against unidentified persons with Uttarkhan police late Friday night.
Although registered as a murder case, the father’s written complaint did not directly accuse anyone of murder. Instead, he asked the authorities to establish the actual cause of his son’s death and take necessary action.
Tahsif, 28, left his Uttara residence on Tuesday evening and went missing. His body was recovered from the Turag river near Rajabari Ghat in Tongi the following afternoon.

item.title: Anti-state conspiracy: Major (retd) Khandaker Hafiz arrested
item.description:
The Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has arrested Major (retd) Khandaker Abdul Hafiz in a case filed over alleged anti-state conspiracy, violent incitement, illegal funding, and social media propaganda.
A DB team picked him up from the capital’s Banani area late Thursday night, said DMP Additional Commissioner (DB) Md Shafiqul Islam.
He said Hafiz was arrested in connection with the case in which two other former Army officers have already been arrested.
Shafiqul alleged that Hafiz, Lt Col (retd) Debashish Kumar Barua and Lieutenant (retd) Kazi Gulshan Ara were involved in anti-state activities.
Debashish and Gulshan Ara are currently in jail in connection with the case filed with Pallabi Police Station under several sections of the Anti-Terrorism Act and the Cyber Security Ordinance.
Earlier, DB arrested the two retired Army officers from Dhaka on the night of October 11.
It earlier claimed that it had information about their alleged links to activities of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, as part of an alleged conspiracy to create instability in the country.
The DB also said the two officers were arrested based on specific information about their alleged involvement in anti-state propaganda on social media and attempts to undermine public security through cybercrimes.

HC grants bail to ex-lawmaker Akhtaruzzaman in airport case
item.description:
The High Court on Sunday granted bail to former lawmaker Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman in a case filed over allegedly obstructing government work and misbehaving with officials at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
A High Court bench led by Justice KM Zahid Sarwar passed the order after hearing his bail petition.
Senior lawyer Mohammad Shishir Manir appeared for Akhtaruzzaman, who was expelled from BNP several times and joined Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami in December 2025, during the hearing.
Earlier, on October 26, the Dhaka Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge Court-5 rejected his bail petition.
The Detective Branch (DB) of police arrested Akhtaruzzaman from his residence in the Dhaka Cantonment area on October 2. The following day, a court placed him on a one-day remand for interrogation.
After the remand, he was produced before a court on October 4, which rejected his bail petition and sent him to jail.
The case was filed over an incident at the airport on October 1, when passengers arriving from Madinah on a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight faced a shortage of luggage trolleys and delays in collecting their baggage.
According to the case statement, Akhtaruzzaman allegedly verbally abused and threatened Airport Executive Director Group Captain SM Ragib Samad and assaulted security supervisor Warrant Officer Mohammad Kamal Uddin.
He was also accused of throwing bottles of Zamzam water from passengers' trolleys and behaving aggressively towards a Biman representative.

item.title: Metro rail skips three stations amid garment workers’ protests
item.description:
Metro rail services in Dhaka are operating without stopping at three stations following a request from police amid clashes between garment workers and law enforcement.
Since Sunday afternoon, trains have been bypassing Pallabi, Mirpur-11 and Mirpur-10 stations, Md Nazrul Islam, director (operations and maintenance) of Dhaka Mass Transit Company Ltd (DMTCL), confirmed to Bangla Tribune.
He said train services at the three stations had been suspended following a clash between garment workers and police around noon.
Meanwhile, a police vehicle was reportedly set on fire in the Mirpur-11 area. Hamidur Rahman, a duty officer at the Fire Service, said two firefighting units had been sent to the scene.
Police also fired tear gas shells to disperse workers in the Mirpur-10 area.
Earlier, hundreds of workers from different garment factories took to the streets around 9am, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. The protest brought traffic in Mirpur to a standstill.
Workers and police clashed in a series of confrontations, including chases and counter-chases.
Around 11am, police charged batons and fired tear gas shells to disperse protesters in the Mirpur-10 area. Some workers were also seen throwing bricks and stones during the clashes.

item.title: Govt forms six-member wage board for garment workers amid protests
item.description:
The government has formed a six-member wage board to review the minimum wage structure for garment workers amid protests across industrial areas, including Dhaka and Gazipur, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury announced the formation of the board at a press briefing at his ministry on Sunday and urged the protesting workers to return to work instead of taking to the streets.
The ministry also issued separate gazette notifications on the formation of the minimum wage board for garment workers on Sunday.
The board has been constituted under Section 138 of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 (amended in 2026), with the mandate to determine the minimum wage for workers in the garment industry under Section 139 of the law.
Senior District and Sessions Judge Sheikh Ashfakur Rahman has been appointed chairman of the board.
Prof Dr Mosleh Uddin Ahmed of the Department of Public Administration at Dhaka University has been appointed as its neutral member.
As general representatives, Asif Ayub, joint secretary general of the Bangladesh Employers Federation, has been appointed as the employers' representative, while Anwar Hossain, president of the Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal, will represent workers.
The board will also have two representatives from the garment industry: ABM Shamsuddin, a director of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), will represent employers, while Babul Akhtar, general secretary of the Bangladesh Garments and Industrial Workers Federation (BGIWF), will represent workers.
The formation of the wage board comes as garment workers have been staging demonstrations and blocking roads in different industrial areas, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000.
On Sunday, workers blocked the Mirpur-10 intersection in Dhaka and several points of the Dhaka-Tangail Highway in Gazipur, disrupting traffic.
Clashes between workers and police in Gazipur also prompted authorities to close most factories in the affected areas.

item.title: Shanto rues batting collapse, fielding lapses in Test defeat
item.description:
Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto admitted that his side failed to deliver in all three departments, particularly with the bat but insisted that the play came into the game with right intent.
The hosts suffered batting collapse in both innings - in the first innings, they lost the last seven wickets for 59 runs after being nicely placed with 213-3. In the second innings, they were reduced to 35-5 before being all out for just 142.
The batting debacle meant they could set only a 170-run target, which the visitng West Indies side overhauled with remarkable ease to seal an eight-wicket victory.
"I think the intention in the dressing room and during preparation was good. The players really wanted to do well for the team, but it was just a bad day. As I said, we didn't do well in all three departments, specially in the field. These things can happen sometimes, but I believe our intention and preparation were quite good," Shanto said.
He praised Shadman Islam for his batting after he scored a century in the first innings but regretted the middle order's inability to build substantial partnerships, particularly when the wicket offered favourable batting conditions in the first innings.
"The way Shadman batted was really good to see, especially with him getting back into form. But the middle order, in particular, couldn't build a big partnership. The wicket was pretty good in the first innings, and we should have added a few more runs to the total," he added. Shanto also lauded Nayeem Hasan for his impressive bowling after returning to the side following a lengthy absence, while praising the contributions of Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Shoriful Islam, Hasan Mahmud and Taijul Islam.
"Nayeem did a great job, especially coming back after a long time and bowling like that. It was really impressive. Mehidy, Shoriful, Hasan and Taijul also bowled really well," he remarked.
The Bangladesh captain acknowledged that poor batting, particularly soft dismissals and a lack of runs, had put the team under pressure.
"We didn't bat well. We started really poorly and gave away too many soft dismissals. Going forward, we need to look at those areas and work out how we can do better in these conditions," he said.
Bangladesh had been poor in slip cordon, missing several chances and also dropped some crucial catches at various point of the game.
Shanto stressed the importance of taking difficult catches and making extra efforts in the field when the team fails to post a competitive total.
"When you're not putting enough runs on the board, you need to take your chances. In the field, too, you need to make that extra effort and take some unbelievable catches. Those are the things you need, but unfortunately, we didn't get those opportunities today. These things can happen in cricket," he concluded.

item.title: Chase hails spinners after West Indies crush Bangladesh in first Test
item.description:
West Indies captain Roston Chase heaped praise on his team's disciplined bowling attack, particularly the spinners, after they secured an eight-wicket victory over Bangladesh in the opening Test at Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium today.
West Indies spinners claimed 16 wickets in the match, twice as many as Bangladesh's spinners, playing a decisive role in the visitors' victory and giving them a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.
Chase singled out left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican for his outstanding contribution, saying the experienced bowler had been leading the spin attack with consistency and confidence.
"We have a quality spin attack, especially led by Jomel Warrican. He's a guy that I've known for many, many years. He went to school with me and he's a good craftsman," Chase said at the post-match press conference.
"He's been improving and anytime he gets a chance, he always delivers. He's been leading us as a spin bowling unit and giving us confidence to do well."
The West Indies skipper, however, was equally pleased with the contribution of the fast bowlers, who kept Bangladesh's scoring rate under control through disciplined lines and lengths.
He identified restricting Bangladesh's first innings lead and taking four quick wickets in the second innings as the two crucial factors behind their victory.
"Not letting them lead us by too many runs was a key, because you don't want to be getting too many runs in Bangladesh, especially in the last innings," he said. "I thought we put them under pressure and got four quick wickets early in that second innings. I thought that really broke the back of the Bangladeshi batting."
Bangladesh, who were bowled out for 272 in their first innings, managed only 142 in the second innings, setting West Indies a target of 170.
Chase said he considered the target manageable, as the pitch remained good for batting despite being a fourth-innings chase in Mirpur.
He also praised openers John Campbell and Brandon King for providing the solid start that allowed West Indies to complete the chase comfortably.
"I just wanted the guys to give us a good start because sometimes when you're chasing a total and you lose too many wickets early, it can set a bit of panic into the dressing room," he said.
West Indies eventually reached the target with eight wickets in hand, with King producing an impressive unbeaten innings against the Bangladesh spinners.
Chase was particularly pleased with King's approach, saying the right-hander showed remarkable control against spin despite being more accustomed to facing fast bowling.
"Brandon played well. He never really looked like the spinners were on top of him. He looked like he was in control, even using his feet and coming down the wicket," he said.
"He's more a guy that likes to play fast bowling. So, to see him dominate the spin like that was very pleasing for me."
The West Indies captain also admitted that repeated interruptions due to bad light and adverse weather were frustrating, as they disrupted the momentum of the game.
